title: 63-357 Inspection of Case Records
content: 63-357 Inspection of Case Records Table o f Contents Section Family Re source Center (FRC) Proced ures 357.1 Privil eged Commun ication/ Information whi ch Cannot be Rele ased to the Clien t 357.2 x 63-35 7.1 Family Resource Center (FRC) Procedures Authorize d pe rsons req uesting review, as w ell as those authori zed to actuall y complete the inspection will b e subject to the Family Reso urce Center (F R C) review procedure s listed bel ow. This incl udes those person s r equesting revi ew in prep aration for a State Hea ring. If a mo re extensive review is re quested, the app licant/recipi ent should be referred to the Appe als section to schedul e an appoi ntment. FRC review p rocedures are a s fol lows: Review Procedure Requirement 1. The comp lete case reco rd, except for privileged communications as noted i n 63-3 57.2 belo w and information no t p r o vided solely b y or authorized by the client or h is/her autho r i zed representative , will be ma de avail able for inspe ct i on. The privi leged commu nication an d information no t pro vided solel y by or authorized by the ap plicant/recipi ent or hi s/ h er authori zed represe ntative, wi ll be remove d fr o m th e case record before any rev i e w by the appli c ant/ r ecipi e n t or his/h e r autho r i zed repre sentative. Note: T he case n a rratives must be p r o vided fo r review; however, privil e g e d comm u nication/in form atio n must first be removed from the c ase re cord prior to the inspection . (See 6 3-357.2 below fo r a su m mary of privileged c o m mun ica ti on/information .) 2. Case i nspection is permi t ted on ly during no rmal work hours. 3. FRCs will make a private roo m availa ble for case record review w here review ers may discuss the case conten t s. No case wi ll be ma d e ava i lable unl e ss the worker or a suitable su bstitute is present in the room during the entire period o f exa min a ti on. 4. The reviewe rs will not be pe rmitt e d to remove, alter, photoco py or p hotograph an yt h ing in the case record. The review ers are permitted to make notes. On request, e ligibi lity staff may ph otocopy specific items in the ca se record for the re viewer. Photocopies in resp onse to gene ral requ ests (the wh ole case file, al l SAR 7s etc.) shoul d not be provide d. Program Guides or othe r regu lations may be made availa ble, on request, d uring t h e case review . Entire chapters are not to be cop ied but ph otocopies of ap plicabl e regula t i ons may be made . 5. The worke r will reco rd in the case comments all requests for inspe ct i on of case records. Note: Requ ests to re view a close d case in Record Library should be directed to the Pub lic Assistance Information (PAI) Unit. 63-35 7.2 Privileged Communicati on/ Information which ca n not be Release d to th e C l ient There are communication s/ i nformation contained in case re cords which a re not su bject t o revi ew by the applica nt/ re cipient or his/her represe ntative. Ad ditional ly, there are commun ications that are not subje ct to revi ew by the applican t /reci pients authorized represe ntative withou t specific consent of the appli cant/recipient as refere nced in Sections 63 -353 and 63-3 54. Some of the privil eged commun ications are brie f l y summarized bel ow: PHYSICIAN  MEDICA L PERSONNEL/PATIENT Confid ential information from a physi cian canno t be disclose d to t h e authori zed rep resentative without spe cific written consent of the clien t /pa t i ent. Some ph ysicians may request a report not b e re leased to the patient. In such cases, the ph ysicians consent to rel ease the report must be obtai ned. PAFD REPORTS All repo rt s, summarie s a nd other confidentia l communication s an d informatio n o btained by PAFD in the process of investiga t i ng an alle ged fraud w ill be re moved from the case record prio r t o its inspe ct i on by an appl icant/recipien t or an authorized rep resentative. IDENTITY O F INFORMER Staff may not di sclose t he ide ntity of an informe r to the appl icant/recipie nt o r h is/her authorize d representative. CHILD ABU S E H O TLINE REPORTS All reports and othe r confid ential communicatio ns/information obtained as a resul t o f a C hild Abuse Hotline comp laint will be removed from the case record prior to i t s inspectio n by an appli cant/recipient or an authori zed represen t a t i ve. LAWYER/APPLICANT/RECIPIENT Matters of confide ntial commun ication betwe en a law yer and cli ent canno t be di sclosed to an au t h orized re presentative without spe cific written conse nt o f the ap plicant/recipi ent. SPOUSES Confid ential communicatio n betwe en spo uses du ring t he ir mari t a l relatio nship ca nnot be disclosed unless b oth agree t o its disclo sure, even after the marria ge has terminated .

title: 63-358 Court Appearances and Subpoenas
content: 63-35 8 Court Appearances a n d Subpo e n as 63-35 8.1 General A subpoena is a court o rder to co mpel a person t o appea r at a depo sition or court procee ding to testify as a witness. A sub poena duces tecum is a court order normall y use d to compel a person to pro duce all docu ments or records named i n t he subpoena . The t e st i mony of Heal t h and Huma n Servi ces Age ncy (HH SA) emplo yees i nvolving case records for matters not directly related t o the admin istration of public social service pro grams is an in appropri ate use of case record s and a viol a ti on of con fidentiality. To avo id viol ating con f i dentiali t y and/or cou rt orders t he proced ures in 63-35 7.2 and .3 below w ill apply. These proce dures apply on ly to subpo enas invol ving HHSA records an d applica nts/ re cipients. 63-35 8.2 District Attorney/ County Counsel Subpo e n a Staff is r outinely served w ith subp oenas issued by the District Attorneys (DA) office. It is HH SA p olicy to fully coope rate with the DA in the investiga t i on or p rosecution of all matters directly related to t h e admin istration of publi c so cial services. Procedu res f o r staff served wi t h a su bpoena i ssued by the DA are outlin ed below : A deman d f o r w itness fees and milea ge should not be made. The employe e wi ll n otify his/he r supe rvisor o r the approp riate Family Resou rce C enter (F R C) ma nager immedia t e ly when served w ith a subpoena . The emp loyee na med on the sub poena i s expected to app ear as directed . o When the employe e i s no lo nger assigned to HHSA, the supervi sor or FRC ma nager will immediatel y contact t h e Depu t y DA ide ntified on the sub poena t o provide the iden t i t y o f the employee who wil l respond a s a substitute. o If t h ere has bee n a change i n t h e worker assig ned to the case, the Dep uty DA must be informed so tha t he / sh e may make the d ecision on who will be require d t o appe ar. The employee must contact the Deputy D A to discu ss the case an d restrictions to avail ability for court (pla nned vacatio n or medica l leave). If unsure whe t h er t he subpoena re lates to a matt e r d irectly conne ct e d to HHSA pro grams, the employe es sup ervisor or FRC Manag ement must con t a ct the Subp oena Liai son who is the Publi c Assi st a nce Information (PAI) Supervisor. If the s u bpoena relates t o a matter not directly related t o the admin istration of pub lic so cial service programs, t h e emp loyee wil l f ol low the proced ures outline d in 63-356.4 be low. 63-35 8.3 Private Attorney Subpo e n a/ Subpo e n as Duces Tecum General Staff is occasion ally served with subpo enas or subp oenas du ces tecum that are initia t e d by: Private attorneys; Lega l Aid Society; or The Publi c D efender. These subpoe nas no rmally request the presen ce of st aff and/or ca se records and may dea l with civil or criminal matt e rs not directly rel ated to the official admi nistration of publ ic social service p rograms, such as: Divorce ; Chil d support; Chil d custody; or Property settlemen t matters. By St a t e Law (W & I Code 1085 0), the testimony of staff and/or use of case record s for matters not rela t e d t o the a dministration of pub lic social service progra ms is considere d ina ppropria t e use of pub lic social service records and i s a v i olation o f confidentiali ty . Subpo e n a A d dres sed to the Custodian o f Re cord Frequen t l y these subpoe nas w ill be for the case re cord, rathe r than a specific pe rson and wil l be addressed to the Cu st o dian of Record. HHSA staff must not ac cept ser vice of sub poenas addressed to the Custodian of Record. The serve r of the sub poena duces tecum must be informe d that the Custodi an of Re cord f o r HH SA is the Eligi bility Operations Chie f and that service of the subpo ena may b e arrange d by the serve r by contacting the PAI Supe rvisor. 63-35 8.4 Private Attorney Subpo e n a Procedures All HH SA st aff served with a subpoe na or subpo ena duces tecum from a private attorney that is addressed to th e sta ff per son (not the Custodi an of Re cord) must accept the sub poena and adh ere to the follow ing proced ures: Procedures 1 The employee must demand witness f e es and milea ge at the time the subpoe na is served . HHSA empl oyees must also dema nd t h at HH SA rece ive t h e fee s an d mi leage prior to the court appeara nce. Witness fees and mil eage reimbu rsement amounts are establ ished by State Law. The pe rson del ivering t he subpoe na may w rite a che ck and presen t it a t the t i me the subpo ena is served (paye e on the check shou ld be the Heal t h a nd Human Service s A g ency). The empl oyee must send the che ck with the subpoe na to the Subpoen a Li aison Eligibi lity Opera t i ons, Mai l Stop W414. For su bpoena duces tecum, send to the PAI Supervi sor at Ma il Stop W409. 2 Immediatel y followi ng the se rving of the subpoe na, the emplo yees immedi ate supervisor wi ll call the Subp oena Liai son, who wil l determine i f the pe nding l egal proce edings are related to the admi nistration of a publi c socia l servi ce progra m. 3 Upon notification, the Subp oena Lia ison wil l request that the subpo ena and check for witness fees, i f appl icable, be deli vered to him/her as soon as ad ministratively po ssible. 4 Upon recei pt of the subpo ena, the Subpo ena L iaison will contact the se rving attorney and expla in the le gal provi sions of confid entiality (W& I C ode 10 850) and request the subpo ena be withd rawn. 63-35 8.5 Attorney Agrees / Refuses to Withd r aw Subpo e n a Attorney Agree s to Withdraw Su bpoena The Subpoena Lia ison w ill notify the employee s supe rvisor tha t the emplo yee is excused from compli ance with the subp oena. Attorney Refuse s to Withdraw Su bpoena The Subpoen a Li aison will return the sub poena to the empl oyee and provid e him/her w ith a copy of t h e Points an d Authorities i n Oppositio n to Sub poena Duce s Tecum. The Points and Authoritie s is a statement prep ared by the Cou nty Counsel s O ffice, and se rves as a formal req uest t o t h e court to excuse the witne ss and/or records on the grounds that the record s are confide ntial. The employee must appe ar in court at t h e designa t ed t i me. The em p loyee must n ot testify or allo w anyon e to se e the record until the Poi nts of Autho rities has been pre sented to the judge an d the judge has made a determin ation. The Poi nts and Authoritie s shoul d be give n to the judg e at the time the empl oyee is cal led to the stand to testify. If the judg e rules a g a i nst t he Points of Autho rities, the emplo yee must: Compl y w ith t h e decision ; Submit the case reco rd; and Give testimony. If p arts of the case record are i ntroduced as evide nce, t he e mployee wil l se ek c o urt a pproval, on the record, of substitution of photocop ies so that the case record and its documents can remain intact w hen the emplo yee is excused.

sections.text: 63-35 8 Court Appearances a n d Subpo e n as 63-35 8.1 General A subpoena is a court o rder to co mpel a person t o appea r at a depo sition or court procee ding to testify as a witness. A sub poena duces tecum is a court order normall y use d to compel a person to pro duce all docu ments or records named i n t he subpoena . The t e st i mony of Heal t h and Huma n Servi ces Age ncy (HH SA) emplo yees i nvolving case records for matters not directly related t o the admin istration of public social service pro grams is an in appropri ate use of case record s and a viol a ti on of con fidentiality. To avo id viol ating con f i dentiali t y and/or cou rt orders t he proced ures in 63-35 7.2 and .3 below w ill apply. These proce dures apply on ly to subpo enas invol ving HHSA records an d applica nts/ re cipients. 63-35 8.2 District Attorney/ County Counsel Subpo e n a Staff is r outinely served w ith subp oenas issued by the District Attorneys (DA) office. It is HH SA p olicy to fully coope rate with the DA in the investiga t i on or p rosecution of all matters directly related to t h e admin istration of publi c so cial services. Procedu res f o r staff served wi t h a su bpoena i ssued by the DA are outlin ed below : A deman d f o r w itness fees and milea ge should not be made. The employe e wi ll n otify his/he r supe rvisor o r the approp riate Family Resou rce C enter (F R C) ma nager immedia t e ly when served w ith a subpoena . The emp loyee na med on the sub poena i s expected to app ear as directed . o When the employe e i s no lo nger assigned to HHSA, the supervi sor or FRC ma nager will immediatel y contact t h e Depu t y DA ide ntified on the sub poena t o provide the iden t i t y o f the employee who wil l respond a s a substitute. o If t h ere has bee n a change i n t h e worker assig ned to the case, the Dep uty DA must be informed so tha t he / sh e may make the d ecision on who will be require d t o appe ar. The employee must contact the Deputy D A to discu ss the case an d restrictions to avail ability for court (pla nned vacatio n or medica l leave). If unsure whe t h er t he subpoena re lates to a matt e r d irectly conne ct e d to HHSA pro grams, the employe es sup ervisor or FRC Manag ement must con t a ct the Subp oena Liai son who is the Publi c Assi st a nce Information (PAI) Supervisor. If the s u bpoena relates t o a matter not directly related t o the admin istration of pub lic so cial service programs, t h e emp loyee wil l f ol low the proced ures outline d in 63-356.4 be low. 63-35 8.3 Private Attorney Subpo e n a/ Subpo e n as Duces Tecum General Staff is occasion ally served with subpo enas or subp oenas du ces tecum that are initia t e d by: Private attorneys; Lega l Aid Society; or The Publi c D efender. These subpoe nas no rmally request the presen ce of st aff and/or ca se records and may dea l with civil or criminal matt e rs not directly rel ated to the official admi nistration of publ ic social service p rograms, such as: Divorce ; Chil d support; Chil d custody; or Property settlemen t matters. By St a t e Law (W & I Code 1085 0), the testimony of staff and/or use of case record s for matters not rela t e d t o the a dministration of pub lic social service progra ms is considere d ina ppropria t e use of pub lic social service records and i s a v i olation o f confidentiali ty . Subpo e n a A d dres sed to the Custodian o f Re cord Frequen t l y these subpoe nas w ill be for the case re cord, rathe r than a specific pe rson and wil l be addressed to the Cu st o dian of Record. title: 63-359 Inter-County Transfer
content: County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guid e Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-35 9 1 of 3 Revision Date: 11/01/20 23 Back g r o und: The Inter-Co unty Transfer (ICT) is designe d to help customers rece ive uni nterrupted b enefits when they move wi t hi n t h e st a t e of C alifornia. Purpose: This section ha s b een revised du e t o su nset review. There are no cha nges in leg islation. Poli c y: The ICT transfers the responsib ility of the case manage ment of self-sufficiency services to a d iff e rent county. Staff must initia t e an ICT whe n a hou sehold (H H) reports a move from one county to anothe r, this includ es HH s expe riencing home lessness. A HH may volun t a rily re port thei r move to either the receivi ng (county to wh ich the HH h as moved to) or se nding (cou nty from which the HH has moved from) cou nty. The co unty the cust o mer notifie s of thei r move will initiate t h e ICT wi t h in seve n busin ess days. Cou nties must communicate w ith each other throug hout the ICT process to ensure t ha t the HH s b enefits are not interru pted. An ICT w ill not requ ire the HH to compl ete a new app lication, recertificatio n, sub mit veri f i cations previousl y pro vided, or complete an interview . The transfer period of benefits must be compl eted within 30 da ys af ter a cou nty i s n otified of a HHs move. Note: When the 3 0 th day lan ds on a wee kend or holi day, the next busine ss day is conside red the last day of the 30 th da y transfer pe riod. A transfer of respon sibility may occur at an ea rlier d ate if there is mutual a greement betwe en the counties i nvolved. The examp le below shows when a t ra nsfer may occur at an earl ier date. Example: ICT i s initia t e d Apri l 20 th , the receivi ng co unty wou ld be re quired to assu me resp onsibil ity May 21 st . Howe ver, the recei ving cou nty notifies the sending county of pro posed be nefit appro val on May 18th. T h e se nding county will di scontinue bene f i t s in a timely manne r an d re ceiving county wil l approve ben efits e f fective Jun e 1 st . 1. Sendi ng County Respo nsibili t i es The follow ing are the send ing countys respo nsibili t i es: Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh Informing Notice of Se nding Inter-County Transfer (NA 1268 ). Provide the receivi ng county, the followi ng items: Copi es of a ll verification s tha t we re in the HHs file. Any informatio n which migh t affect elig ibility. CalFresh Notificatio n of Intercoun t y Transfer (CF 21 5). Publi c Assistance CalFresh (PAC F ) cases must inclu de CalWORKs Notificatio n of Intercou nty Tran sf e r (C W 2 15). Note: The name and ph one number of the ICT sp ecialist must be includ ed in the comment section. Appli cation for Cash Aid , CalFresh and/or Med ical Assi st a nce (SAWS 2 Plus), Appli cation for CalFresh Benefits (C F 285), an d Initial Applicatio n for Ca lFresh, and/or Medi-Cal / H ealthcare Programs (SAWS 1). County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guid e Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-35 9 2 of 3 Eligi bility Status Report (SAR 7). CalFresh Househol d Change R eport (CF 377.5) if applica ble. Any outstand ing over-i ssuance (OI) repaymen t re cords (with sup porting docu mentation such as OI Notice of Act i on [NOAs], bu dgets, etc. ) that wil l not be repaid be f o re t h e end of the transfer perio d. Once al l docume nts have been sen t and n otification i s obtaine d that the receiving county is respo nsible, the send ing county wi ll no long er be respon sible for the coll ection of the claim an d wil l re move t h e claim from t h eir case record. Refer to CalFresh ICT Receivin g and Sending Coun t y Job Aid an d Cal F r esh ICT P r ocessing Guide 359-01 for add itional information and proced ures. Transferring the benefit responsi bility t o the receiving coun t y no later t ha n the first da y of t h e ne xt avail able ben efit mon t h . 2. Recei ving Coun t y Resp onsibil ities The follow ing are the recei ving countys respo nsibili t i es: Process the SAR 7 or recertification when the cu st o mer moves durin g the last two mon t h s of the Semi-Ann ual Reporting (SAR) period . The SAR cycle an d recertificatio n t ha t wer e assigne d i n the sendi ng county must continu e in the receivin g co unty. The customer may be sent the NOA of the appro val of b enefits in the recei ving cou nty along with the Notice of t he Expiration of Certifica t i on perio d or separate notice s ma y be sen t . The table b elow illustrates whe n a customers case will be picked up by the receivi ng county when their recertification is due in S e ptember. If the then the rece i v i ng county ICT i s initiated in the month of August, comple t e s t h e rece rt i f i cation in Se ptember with an ICT pick- up date of October 1st. recertificatio n is comp leted by the sendi ng county prior to initia t i ng the ICT in Septembe r, picks up the ICT on Novemb er 1st. ICT i s initiated in the month of Septembe r, comple t e s t h e rece rt i f i cation in Se ptember with an ICT pick- up date of October 1st, rather than Nove mber 1st due to the recertificatio n endin g September in the sending county. Note: The se nding coun t y may process the SAR 7 or rece rt i f i cation if t h e sen ding and receivin g countie s agree that it is in the customers best interest for them to do so. Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh I n f o rming Notice o f R eceiving Inter-Co unty Transfer (NA 1267 ). Process e ligibl e Transition al Ca lFresh (TCF) cases. T h e recei ving county wil l b e respon sible for processi ng the recertificatio n an d determini ng eli gibili t y f or regul ar C alFresh. The custome r will continu e to receive T C F b enefits from the orig inal county until recertification i s comp leted in the receivi ng county. When the HH con sists of a n Abl e-Bodied Adu lts Withou t D ependen t s (ABAWD) i ndividua l, the county of reside nce i s respon sible to check i f the pa rt i cipant is mee t i ng the ABAWD work rule (Refer to 63-90 4). County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guid e Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-35 9 3 of 3 3. HHs Exclud ed from t h e I C T Proce ss Do not initia t e an I C T when only some members of the HH move to another county. Those i ndividu als wil l be added or remo ved from t h e curren t HH a ccording t o existing SAR rules. Indivi duals leaving the current H H must be removed from the case and may apply i n their new county of residen ce or be adde d t o a n existing Cal F re sh HH. 4. Restoration o f Aid HH s may be el igible for restora t i on i f the H H app lies i n a new county i n the month fol lowing their discon t i nuance. The d iscontinua nce can be f or any reason o t h er than failure to complete a recertificatio n or disq ualificatio n from receivin g be nefits. Staff sh all communicate with the previous county t o determi ne wh ich i s more beneficia l to t h e HH , having the benefits restore d or completin g a new appli cation (in the eve nt the HH is eli gible for exped ited service s). The send ing cou nty is respon sible for restoring t h e case and the receivin g county mu st provide any in f o rmation ne eded to comple t e the restoration. If it i s determined that the H H is better served by comp leting a new appl ication, the receivi ng county will no t i f y the HH a nd assist in the completio n of the a pplicatio n. 5. Domestic Abuse Strict con f i dentiali t y must b e mai ntained for do mestic ab use vi ct i ms duri ng ICT process. A l l communi cation of d omestic abu se issues, i ncluding documen t a t i on must be kept confide ntial so t h at the cu st o mers informa t i on is not avail able t o any staff wh o wil l not be directly involved in the case. The u se of fax f or domestic abuse case s is di scouraged . The send ing cou nty is strongl y encou raged to provide the cu st o mer with references to local domestic abuse servi ces t h at a re in the receivin g county. Dome st i c abuse ICT cases must be assigned t o st a f f wh o have recei ved the requ ired domestic abuse training to add ress the customers sp ecific ne ed to ensure a smooth case transfer. Victims of domestic abuse and their familie s can use the Safe at Home service for confidentia l ma il services. Program Impacts : Refer to the CalWORKs ICT process f o r Publ ic Assistance CalFresh cases when at l east one member of t he Cal F r esh H H recei ves C alWORKs (Cal WO R Ks Program Guide 40-10 0). The HH will be discon t i nued from the prio r coun t y at t h e same time the transfer of the CalWORKs case is comple t e d. Refer to the Medi -Cal I C T process for C alFresh cases w hen at lea st one member of the CalFresh H H receives Medi -Cal (Medi-C al Program Guide Articl e 3, Se ct i on 2 Int e r-County Transfer). Refer ences: All Cou nty L ett e r (AC L): 1 1-22, 11-70, 13-78 , and 1 7-58. All Cou nty Informa t i on Notice (ACIN) I-60-09. sections.text: County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guid e Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-35 9 1 of 3 Revision Date: 11/01/20 23 Back g r o und: The Inter-Co unty Transfer (ICT) is designe d to help customers rece ive uni nterrupted b enefits when they move wi t hi n t h e st a t e of C alifornia. Purpose: This section ha s b een revised du e t o su nset review. There are no cha nges in leg islation. Poli c y: The ICT transfers the responsib ility of the case manage ment of self-sufficiency services to a d iff e rent county. Staff must initia t e an ICT whe n a hou sehold (H H) reports a move from one county to anothe r, this includ es HH s expe riencing home lessness. A HH may volun t a rily re port thei r move to either the receivi ng (county to wh ich the HH h as moved to) or se nding (cou nty from which the HH has moved from) cou nty. The co unty the cust o mer notifie s of thei r move will initiate t h e ICT wi t h in seve n busin ess days. Cou nties must communicate w ith each other throug hout the ICT process to ensure t ha t the HH s b enefits are not interru pted. An ICT w ill not requ ire the HH to compl ete a new app lication, recertificatio n, sub mit veri f i cations previousl y pro vided, or complete an interview . The transfer period of benefits must be compl eted within 30 da ys af ter a cou nty i s n otified of a HHs move. Note: When the 3 0 th day lan ds on a wee kend or holi day, the next busine ss day is conside red the last day of the 30 th da y transfer pe riod. A transfer of respon sibility may occur at an ea rlier d ate if there is mutual a greement betwe en the counties i nvolved. The examp le below shows when a t ra nsfer may occur at an earl ier date. Example: ICT i s initia t e d Apri l 20 th , the receivi ng co unty wou ld be re quired to assu me resp onsibil ity May 21 st . Howe ver, the recei ving cou nty notifies the sending county of pro posed be nefit appro val on May 18th. T h e se nding county will di scontinue bene f i t s in a timely manne r an d re ceiving county wil l approve ben efits e f fective Jun e 1 st . 1. Sendi ng County Respo nsibili t i es The follow ing are the send ing countys respo nsibili t i es: Notify the customer of the transfer using the CalFresh Informing Notice of Se nding Inter-County Transfer (NA 1268 ). Provide the receivi ng county, the followi ng items: Copi es of a ll verification s tha t we re in the HHs file. Any informatio n which migh t affect elig ibility. CalFresh Notificatio n of Intercoun t y Transfer (CF 21 5). Publi c Assistance CalFresh (PAC F ) cases must inclu de CalWORKs Notificatio n of Intercou nty Tran sf e r (C W 2 15). Note: The name and ph one number of the ICT sp ecialist must be includ ed in the comment section. Appli cation for Cash Aid , CalFresh and/or Med ical Assi st a nce (SAWS 2 Plus), Appli cation for CalFresh Benefits (C F 285), an d Initial Applicatio n for Ca lFresh, and/or Medi-Cal / H ealthcare Programs (SAWS 1). County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guid e Number Page CalFresh Inter-County Transfers 63-35 9 2 of 3 Eligi bility Status Report (SAR 7). CalFresh Househol d Change R eport (CF 377.5) if applica ble. Any outstand ing over-i ssuance (OI) repaymen t re cords (with sup porting docu mentation such as OI Notice of Act i on [NOAs], bu dgets, etc. ) that wil l not be repaid be f o re t h e end of the transfer perio d. Once al l docume nts have been sen t and n otification i s obtaine d that the receiving county is respo nsible, the send ing county wi ll no long er be respon sible for the coll ection of the claim an d wil l re move t h e claim from t h eir case record. Refer to CalFresh ICT Receivin g and Sending Coun t y Job Aid an d Cal F r esh ICT P r ocessing Guide 359-01 for add itional information and proced ures. title: 63-360 Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 1 of 3 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: ESAP is a set of waivers that simplify the CalFresh application and recertification process for Non- Assistance CalFresh (NACF) households in which all members are age 60 or older or disabled. The goal is to increase CalFresh participation among eligible households by simplifying the application and recertification process. Purpose: This section details eligibility criteria and interview requirements for ESAP households. This section is being updated due to sunset review and to include the CalFresh Elderly Simplified Application (CF 485). Policy: A CalFresh household is considered ESAP when all members are aged or disabled (including ineligible or excluded household members) and have no earned income. Upon approval of CalFresh, ESAP households are assigned a 36-month certification period and are not required to complete the Eligibility Status Report (SAR 7). The following waivers apply only to ESAP households:  Recertification interview waiver.  Data matching waiver to reduce customer provided verifications.  Certification extension waiver.  SAR 7 waiver. 1. Application The CF 485 is a single signature CalFresh application designed specifically for use by ESAP households and is available in the Eligibility Forms Library. The CF 485 includes only required questions that are relevant to ESAP households. Note: An ESAP eligible household may apply for CalFresh using any of the acceptable applications, refer to CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-103. 2. Interview Requirements An interview is required at initial application. If the household is determined to meet ESAP criteria, document in the case record, and inform the household that a recertification interview is not required. Recertification interviews are waived for ESAP households, unless one of the following applies:  ESAP household requests an interview.  Information provided on the application for recertification will result in a denial.  Information supplied by the household is questionable, incomplete, or contradictory. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 2 of 3 Note: A copy of the Statement of Facts containing all information used to determine eligibility along with the Statement of Facts Notification (09-105 HHSA) form must be sent to the household when processing an ESAP recertification, even if an interview was not required. 3. Verifications Electronic resources, such as Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS), Payment Verification System (PVS), and Medi-Cal Eligibility Data System (MEDS) must be used to the greatest extent possible, refer to CFPG 63-117. 4. Reporting Requirements For ESAP households, a Changes for Cash Aid and CalFresh (SAR 2) form will be sent to the household in the 12 th and 24 th months of their 36-month certification period. These households are not required to submit a SAR 7. If an ESAP household submits a SAR 7, it will be treated as a voluntary mid-period report. 5. Losing ESAP Eligibility Households that are no longer eligible for ESAP will remain in their current 36-month certification period until it ends. At recertification, an interview will be required. If the household is still eligible for CalFresh, they will be placed in a 12-month or 24-month certification period, depending on their circumstances. Note: When the household loses ESAP eligibility, Semi-Annual Reporting requirements will resume, refer to CFPG 63-272. 6. ESAP Notices Each household will be mailed a Notice of Expiration of Certification (NEC) in the month prior to the last month of the certification period. The following notices will be sent based on the ESAP case circumstances: Notice Description CF 377.2B – CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. ESAP households that are not required to complete a recertification interview. CF 377.2C – CalFresh Notice of Expiration of Certification for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. Former ESAP households that are required to complete an interview. CF 377.2D – CalFresh Notice of Status Change for Households with Only Elderly and/or Disabled Members. The customer reports a change that would result in the household no longer meeting ESAP eligibility. Other Program Impacts: No impacts. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Number Page 63-360 3 of 3 References: All County Letter (ACL) 13-58, 17-34, 17-53, 20-126, 20-145, 22-15, 23-85. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 273.2(e)-(f), 273.10(f)(1)-(f)(4), 273.14(b)(3). Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) 2008 Sections 3(f), 11(e)(3), 17(b). Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-300.4, 63-300.5, 63-404.6, 63-504.14.142. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance by 09/30/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-380 Prepared Meal Programs
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Prepared Meal Programs Number Page 63-380 1 of 2 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: CalFresh households (HHs) that meet specific eligibility criteria may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase prepared meals from providers approved by Food and Nutrition Services (FNS). Purpose: The section has been updated due to sunset review. This section has been renamed to incorporate CalFresh benefit usage at communal dining facilities and authorized homeless meal providers for eligible CalFresh HHs. There are no changes to the policy. Policy: Eligible HHs may use their CalFresh benefits for home-delivered meals, at communal dining facilities, or with other authorized homeless meal providers. Home-Delivered Meals To qualify for home-delivered meals, the CalFresh recipient must not reside in a boarding house or institution and meet the following:  Be 60 years or older; and unable to leave their home due to a disability, medical condition, or have limited mobility that prevents them preparing their own meals.  Be the spouse living with an individual who meets one of the above criteria. Home-delivered meals must be provided through non-profit meal delivery service programs that are approved by FNS to accept CalFresh benefits. Communal Dining Facilities CalFresh recipients who are 60 or older, or who receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and their spouses, may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase meals from approved communal dining facilities. Authorized Homeless Meal Providers CalFresh recipients who are experiencing homelessness may use their CalFresh benefits to purchase prepared meals from FNS authorized homeless meal providers. For a list of approved home-delivered meal providers, communal dining meal facilities, or homeless meal providers, HHs may contact:  Aging & Independence Services (AIS) Call Center: (800) 339-4661.  2-1-1 San Diego. References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 63-604.2. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 274.7(g)(1). All County Letter (ACL) 19-51. title: 63-420 Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS)
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63 - 420 1 of 4 Revision Date: 10/01/2025 Background: WINS is a state funded food benefit for CalFresh households (HH) that meet Work Participation Rate (WPR) requirements. WINS supports working families and helps improve the state’s WPR. Purpose: This section details WINS eligibility requirements for the WINS program. This section is being updated due to sunset review and includes clarification regarding the CalFresh Notice of Approval/Denial/Termination Work Incentive Nutritional Supplement (WINS) Benefit (WINS 1239) notice requirements. There are no changes to policy. Policy: WINS is a $10 monthly food benefit added to the Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) account for qualifying CalFresh HHs. WINS is evaluated at:  Initial application.  Semi-Annual Report (SAR 7).  Recertification.  When the HH reports a change. When determined eligible, the WINS benefit is issued prospectively between the 20 th and 24 th of the month until a change is reported that results in WINS ineligibility. WINS is issued at the case level, and not per individual. If two or more families are aided under one CalFresh case and are eligible for WINS, only one $10 WINS benefit is issued for the case. 1. WINS Terminology Refer to the table below for WINS-related terminology: Term Definition Parent A n atural, adoptive, or stepparent acting on behalf of a child . Caretaker Relative A relative (up to the fifth degree of kinship) acting on the behalf of the parent of a child . Work-Eligible Individual (WEI) An adult (or minor child head-of-HH) living with a child unless the parent is:  A minor parent and not the head-of-HH.  Ineligible due to immigration status.  Caring for a disabled family member living in the home.  Receiving Social Security Administration (SSA) Disability benefits.  In a HH receiving Tribal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families ( TANF ). Non-Two-Parent/Caretaker Relative A single parent with a child age 6 or older or a two- parent/caretaker relative HH with one WEI. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63 - 420 2 of 4 Unsubsidized Employment A job where the employer does not receive public funds to help pay wages. Subsidized Employment A job where the employer does get public funds, such as TANF, to help pay wages. Core Work Activities Any combination of cumulative hours from the following:  Subsidized employment.  Unsubsidized employment.  Work experience (WEX).  Job search and readiness.  Community service programs.  Mental health/substance abuse domestic violence services.  Vocational education training.  Job skills training (directly related to employment).  Education (directly related to employment).  Satisfactory school attendance.  Work activities other than those specified. 2. WINS Eligibility Requirements To qualify for WINS, a CalFresh HH must not have gross income that exceeds 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) and meet the following criteria:  Not receiving CalWORKs or Tribal TANF.  Have a child in the home who is: o Under the age of 18; or o Under the age of 19 if the child is still in high school and will graduate before their 19 th birthday.  Have at least one parent/caretaker relative who: o Is receiving CalFresh. o Meets the WEI definition. o Meets the required number of hours of core work activity hours.  Provide verification of hours work in subsidized or unsubsidized employment. 3. WINS Work Hour Requirements To be eligible to WINS, the WEI(s) must meet the following in subsidized or unsubsidized employment based on their HH type: Hours Required Per Week WEI HH Type 20 hours per week Single custodial parent/caretaker relative with a child under the age of 6 (one WEI) . 30 hours per week Non-two parent/caretaker relative or single custodial parent/caretaker relative with all children aged 6-18 (one WEI). 35 hours per week combined, with at least 30 core work activity hours completed by one parent (one WEI) Two-parent/caretaker relative (both working) with all children under the age of 18 (two WEIs). County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63 - 420 3 of 4 If the verification provided does not include the hours worked, estimated work hours may be calculated as follows:  Divide gross wages by the state minimum wage plus $0.50.  For self-employed individuals, divide net income (gross minus 40% or actual expenses) by the federal minimum wage. 4. WINS Aid Codes and HH Scenarios For information on WINS aid codes and WINS HH scenarios, refer to the WINS Desk Aid. 5. Mid-Period Changes and WINS Discontinuance If the HH reports a change mid-period report, determine if the reported change meets mandatory mid- period reporting requirements and take action accordingly. If the WEI’s hours fall below the required threshold, discontinue WINS benefits and issue adequate notice. For additional information regarding mandatory mid-period reporting, refer to CalFresh Program Guide (CFPG) 63-283. 6. Notice Requirements The WINS 1239 notice may be required depending on the WINS benefit status and specific case circumstances. The WINS 1239 approval and discontinuance notice will auto-generate in the automated system. WINS Status Notice Requirement Approved Issue the WINS 1239 approval notice. Discontinued Issue the WINS 1239 discontinuance notice in the month the ineligibility occurs (10-day timely notice is not required). Denied The WINS 1239 denial notice should never be issued when a HH fails to qualify for WINS during an initial evaluation. If a HH specifically requests to be evaluated for WINS (such as during a voluntary or mid-period report) but does not qualify for it, verbal notification is acceptable and must be documented in the case record. If contact is unsuccessful, issue the WINS 1239 denial notice. 7. Cases Approved for Transitional CalFresh (TCF) HHs discontinued from CalWORKs are screened for WINS eligibility at the start of the TCF period. To be eligible for WINS during the TCF period, the HH’s income must not exceed 200% of the FPL and must meet all other WINS eligibility criteria. If eligible, WINS benefits are issued for the entire TCF certification period. During the TCF period, HHs are not required to report any changes, and no action should be taken if a voluntary change is reported. If a TCF HH reports a change or requests to be evaluated for WINS before the end of the TCF period, the HH should be informed of the option to wait until the TCF period ends and then recertify for CalFresh; or recertify CalFresh at the time of the request. For additional information on TCF, refer to CFPG 63-320. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) CalFresh Program Guide Work Incentive Nutrition Supplement (WINS) Program Number Page 63 - 420 4 of 4 8. Benefit Use WINS can only be used to purchase food and cannot be applied toward repayment of CalFresh overissuance or CalWORKs overpayment claims. WINS benefits will be expunged if there is no activity (purchases or withdrawals) on the EBT account for 274 days. Once expunged, WINS benefits cannot be restored, even if the HH remains eligible for CalFresh. References: All County Information Notice (ACIN) I-14-14, I-14-14E, I-27-15. All County Letter (ACL) 13-71, 13-71E, 14-83, 22-62. All County Welfare Directors Letter (ACWDL) December 5, 2014, February 2, 2015. Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 16-120, 42-716. Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by 09/30/2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: 63-451 Establishment of CalFresh Claim
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Establishment of Non -Fra u d CalFresh Claims 63-45 1 1 of 3 Revision Date: 09/01/20 22 Back g r o und: A clai m is an amount ow ed beca use of ben efits that were overissued to the hou sehold (HH) or bene f i t s that were trafficked. Claims are categori zed as Inad vertent H ousehol d Error (IHE), Admini st ra t i ve Err or (AE), or Intentional Pro gram Violation (IPV) claims. IHEs and AEs are conside red non-frau d and IPVs are considere d f ra ud related clai ms. Purpose: This section details the type s of overissuan ce (OI ) cl aims and pro vides guid ance on h ow to establi sh and calcul ate them. Effective July 1 st , 20 22, there is a 2 4-month t i mef r ame to establish and calcul ate a non-frau d claim. This change w ill be appl ied prospe ct i vely. T h is sect i on is being re vised to incorp orate this change . Poli c y: To comp lete the collectio n process, claims must be est a blished when an O I is calcu lated. A claim shall not be establishe d in the followi ng circumstances: The customer did not sign the appli cation form. The HH resid es in another cou nty an d t h e case was certified in Sa n Diego Co unty by mistake. The 24-mon t h time frame to act on a no n-fraud OI ha s passed. The customer rep orted a manda t o ry chang e timely, and t he correct benefits could not be issued due to the 10-d ay notice require ment. When the OI is based on exce ss p roperty for a Categorical ly Eligibl e (CE) HH. The table be low describ es t he t ype s of cl aims: Claim Desc rip tion IHE Establish ed when an OI results from a misunde rst a nding or unintend ed error ca used by the customer. AE Establish ed when an OI results from an action or failure t o act by t h e agency. Note: IHEs could potentially resu lt i n an IPV, refer to section 63 -453 for further guida nce. Effective July 1, 202 2, a non-fraud clai m must only be establish ed when it occu rs wi t h in 24-months from the date of d iscovery. Any O I that occurred outsid e of the 24-mo nth period wil l n ot be a ct e d o n. The date of discove ry i s the d ate t he O I is calcul ated, and the claim is establ ished whe n a demand letter, budg et a nd repaymen t ag reement are issue d to the HH. This informatio n must be entered in the case record . Bel ow is an exampl e of the 2 4-month claim establ ishment time frame: Example Scenari o On July 1, 2022, a potential IHE OI is ide ntified from January 1, 2019, thro ugh March 31, 2021 . Outcome Staff may on ly ca lculate an OI and establ ish a cl aim for t h e period of July 202 0 through March 2021. A n OI cal culation and clai m establi shment must not be comple t e d for the mo nths of January 2019 through June 202 0 be cause the y are County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Establishment of Non -Fra u d CalFresh Claims 63-45 1 2 of 3 outside the 24-mon t h timeframe. Note: For a non-fraud clai m that was alre ady establishe d, bu t is later de t e rmined to be fraudule nt, the timeframe may incl ude OI mo nths beyond the 24-mo nth t i meframe. 1. Threshold Amo unts f or Establ ishing Cl aims: The table be low illu st ra t e s the thre shold amoun t for whe n a claim must be establi shed: Status of case and claim type Threshold amount Action Active AE $35 or less Do not establi sh a claim Close d AE $400 or less Do not establi sh a claim Active IHE $1 or more Establish a claim Close d IHE $400 or less Do not establi sh a claim The threshold amou nt wil l be ap plied based on the case stat u s. Staff must reassess the claim if the status of t he ca se has changed sin ce t he d ate o f disco very. The foll owing table w ill assist in making this determin ation: If the case status is then the case is considered closed on the date of disco very, an d is later rescind ed with no break in aid, active, apply t he thresh old limi t s specified above . closed on the date of di scovery an d the HH submits a n ew app lication (with a bre ak of aid) at a later date, closed , app ly the t h reshold limits specifie d above . 2. Claim R esponsibi lity: When establi shing a claim, a respo nsible indi vidual must be assigned for t h e col lection to b egin. Respo nsible in dividua ls include: All adu lt me mbers of t h e HH when the OI occurred. This inclu des exclude d HH members. A person con nected to the HH such as an Authori zed Represe ntative (AR). Sponso r o f a n oncitizen an d sponsored noncitizen w ill both be l iable, if the clai m is a result from incorre ct i nf o rmation provid ed by the sponsor. A sponsor wi ll not be held at fault for an AE clai m. 3. Lomeli v . Saen z C ourt Sett l ement: The Lomeli v. Sae nz cou rt settlement establishe d that all AE OI a re to be recouped at a rate of five percen t (5%) or $10 w hichever is greater. The allotmen t reduction will be set u p for a period of 36- month conse cutive calend ar months start i ng with the month the actual co llection beg ins. Af ter the 36 - month period, the collection will be suspen ded, and the remain ing ba lance w ill be compromised (Compr omised means that the clai m is reduced or forgive n). C laims can still be col lected after the case is di scontinued ; the mo nths would co ntinue to count toward s t h e 36-month li mit. When t h e 36- month perio d of recoupme nt expi res, the system will automatical ly com promise the claim, re ducing the remain ing bala nce to zero ($0.00). title: 63-452 Non-Fraud Claim Determination
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Clai m Determination 63-45 2 1 of 3 Revision Date: 04/01/20 19 Back g r o und: Inadverten t Househo ld Errors (IHE) and Admin istrative Error (AE) claims are considere d non-frau d OI claims. This section is being reformatted and revise d t o reflect the change in reg ulation as a result of the settlement of the lawsu it Brown an d Espi nosa -T a pia v. Lig htbourne. This regulation chan ges t he look back pe riod for collection of Inadverten t Househo ld Error (I H E) and A d ministrative Error (AE) overissu ances from 6 years t o 3 yea rs. Effective immedi ately, all newly establ ished IHE and AE claims must compl y with t h e new 3 year loo k back timeframe. OI clai ms establi shed p rior to t h is revisio n will not be affected. Purpose: This section de t a ils the establish ment and determina t i on of non-fraud Cal F re sh claims. Poli c y: 63-45 2.1 Establi s h m ent of IHE Claims: Initi al IHE Overissuance Month For Inadve rt e nt Househ old Error (I H E) claims, the initial month of overi ssuance w ill be the first month that the custome r received more bene f i t s t ha n it was en t i t l ed to, unle ss the overissu ance was caused by fail ure to rep ort a requ ired cha nge. In cases involvin g failure to report a require d change , t h e first month aff e ct e d by the customers f ai lure to report wi ll be the first mon t h in w hich the change would have be en eff e ct i ve had it been repo rt e d t i mely. Deter min a ti on of I H E Clai m s When d etermining the amou nt of benefits the househ old shou ld have received, d o not ap ply the twenty (20) percen t earn ed income ded uction to t he p ortion of earned income the custome r fai led to report. Calcu late the amount of the IHE claim. Off se t t h e amount of the claim ag ainst any un derissuan ce that was cal culated for the same month of the new cl aim. Adjust the claim balance to ze ro if the u nderissua nce i s more than t h e amo unt of the cl aim. Issue t he bala nce of t h e und erissuace to the cust o mer as a restoratio n of l ost bene f i t s. Refer to 63-456 . Establish a n I H E cl aim for househol ds when the customer: Failed t o report required information a ccurately an d/or timel y Failed to report a change on the S AR 7 for t h e D at a Mon t h and the SAR Payment period was inco rrectly computed base d on this failure Submits t h e SAR 7 late and benefits ca nnot be decreased due t o ten-day n otice requi rements If a C alFresh custome r has a n existing overissu ance that is bein g recoup ed by benefit redu ct i on and a recoupmen t for a nother t ype of overissuan ce ne eds to be calculated , base the amount o f the second overi ssuance recoupmen t on the i nitial CalFresh bene f i t , not on the adjusted ben efit after t h e OI h as been ded ucted. Refer to Definition an d E xa mples 63-11 03 for an example . County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Clai m Determination 63-45 2 2 of 3 63-45 2.2 Establi s h m ent of AE Claims: Initi al AE Overiss u a n c e Mo nth For Admi nistrative Erro r (AE) cla ims, the i nitial month of overissuan ce wil l be the first mo nt h the house hold recei ves more benefits than it was entitle d t o du e t o a n error caused by the coun t y. When t h e AE overissuance invol ves failu re to a ct timely o n a reported change, the initia l month of overissu ance wil l be the first month of the SAR paymen t pe riod for which a change sho uld have be en made, subj ect to timel y n otice. Deter min a ti on of AE Claims Determin e the claim amount by compu t i ng the difference betwee n the allotment the custome r receive d and the allotmen t the custome r sh ould have rece ived for each month of the overissu ance. If a C alFresh custome r has a n existing overissu ance that is bein g recoup ed by benefit redu ct i on and a recoupmen t for a nother t ype of overissuan ce ne eds to be calculated , base the amount o f the second overi ssuance recoupmen t on the i nitial CalFresh bene f i t , not on the adjusted ben efit after t h e OI h as been ded ucted. Refer to Definition an d E xa mples 63-11 03 for an example . Refer to 63-45 1.5 for t h e t h ree-year time frame requi rement to establish an AE clai m. Do not offset the amou nt of an AE claim again st any amoun t of underi ssuances, which have not yet been re st o red t o t he househol d. Re f e r to 63 -454.7. 63-45 2.3 Determining N o n-Fraud Claim Month s : Calcu late the amoun t of the non-fraud overissu ance tha t occurred durin g the 3 yea rs before the d ate the overissuan ce was discovere d as long as the overissu ance was estab lished timely (within t h e 3- year time frame). If the ove rissuance is no t estab lished timel y, the overi ssuance cann ot be recouped. Refer to 63-45 4 for recoupmen t regu lations and pro cedures. Date of Discover y The date that the budg et i s comp uted showin g t ha t the ove rissuance actua lly occurred. Date C l aim Esta b lished The da t e the clai m is establ ished i s the date a dequate notice (dema nd letter, bud get and repayment agree ment) is issued to the house hold. A claim is establ ished whe n t h e f o llowin g happens: The amoun t an d reason for the overissua nce is entered in case co mments, a nd A demand (o verissuance ) l et ter i s i ssued to the customer The date the overi ssuance letter is maile d to t he cust o mer is the date the claim is consi dered to be establi shed for tracking purp oses. 63-45 2.4 L ome l i v. Saenz Court Settlement: The Lome li v. Saenz court settlement establ ished that all new AE overissua nces establish ed on March 1, 200 0 and ongo ing are to be re couped at a rate of five pe rcent (5%) or $10 w hichever is greater. The al lotment redu ct i on wil l be set up for a period o f 36 conse cutive calen dar months st a rt i ng with t h e month the act u al co llection begin s. After the 3 6-month period, t h e col lection will be suspende d an d the remain ing bala nce will be forgi ven (compromise d). County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Non-Fraud Clai m Determination 63-45 2 3 of 3 Lomel i v. Sae nz clai ms can st i ll be colle ct e d after the case is discon t i nued; the months would continu e to cou nt towa rds t he 3 6-month limit. Whe n t he 3 6-month limit expires, the claim wi ll be compromi sed. When the 36 -month pe riod of recoup ment (coll ection) expires, the system w ill automatically compromi se t h e claim, reducin g t h e remainin g balance to zero ($0 . 0 0). 63-45 2.5 Determination o f an Overiss u a n c e i n CalWIN: Refer to Processin g G u ide 450-01 63-45 2.6 Non -Sy stem Deter min e d Claims (N SDC): Refer to How To # 536 H ow To Enter a Non-System Determin ed Claim. content: C o u n t y o f S an D i eg o , H eal t h an d H u m an S er vi c es A g en cy ( H H S A ) C al F r esh P ro g ra m G ui de I nt e nt i ona l P r ogr a m V i ol a t i on N um be r P a ge 63 - 4 53 1 o f 2 R evi si o n D at e : 07/ 0 1/ 2 024 B a c k gr ound : A f r au dul e nt ov er i s s ua nc e ( O I ) i s a c l ai m det er m i ne d t o h av e be en c aus e d by an I n t en t i on al P r ogr a m V i ol at i on ( I P V ) . title: 63-455 Management of Claims
content: County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Management of Claims 63-45 5 1 of 3 Revision Date 06/01/20 20 Back g r o und: CalFresh claims are estab lished by el igibil ity st a f f and referred to fiscal to process the collection. Revisi ons have b een made t o ref l ect the change of policy that in creases the clai ms establishme nt threshol d f o r cl osed CalFresh ca ses. Purpose: This section in cludes poli cies for managin g CalFresh clai ms. Poli c y: 63-45 5.1 I nter -State/ I nter -Cou nty Claims : Inter-State Claims In cases where a househol d moves from out of state, the coun t y can i nitiate or continue co llection for any overi ssuance (OI) t h at o ccurred whil e t h e case was unde r the othe r st ate's ju risdiction. The state has the optio n t o co ntinue OI collection pro cedures or transfer the OI claim to the stat e in which the customer is now residing. Prior to initiating actio n to colle ct clai ms ag ainst househo lds which have moved into the state, the county wil l co ntact the state that overissued be nefits t o de t e rmine that t he state doe s n ot in t e nd t o pursue collection . Once t he county accepts respo nsibili t y, cla im collectio n will be retained b y t h e county that is colle ct i ng t h e OI . Inter-County Claims When a hou sehold move s to an other county and continu es t o re ceive CalFresh : The sendi ng county will sen d all OI i nformation to the receivin g county The sen ding co unty will no lon ger be responsib le for coll ection of the OI and wi ll remove the claim from the record The receivi ng county will be responsibl e f o r co llection of the OI When a hou sehold move s to an other county and is not receivi ng CalFresh, the last coun t y respon sible for the initia t i on and colle ct i on of t he O I wil l continue to colle ct . 63-45 5.2 Criteria for Establishment o f Claims for Closed Cas es: Effective June 1, 2019 , the Cal F r esh claims establi shment threshold w ill be $400 . 0 0 f o r cl osed cases with an O I cause d by an Admini st ra t i ve Error (AE) or Inadvertent House hold Error (IHE). Previou sly the claims estab lishment thresho ld on closed case s was $125.00 or le ss for an AE an d $35.00 or less for a n IHE. The ne w thresh old does not app ly to OIs arisi ng from Intentional Progra m Viol ation (I PV) or Quality Con t ro l (QC) reviews. There is no cha nge to the method of collectio n f o r cl osed cases. Any claim estab lished before Ju ne 1, 2019 on a closed ca se with an OI caused by an AE or I H E will not be a f fected b y t hi s policy chan ge. The coun t y wi ll not refer colle ct i on of AE and IHE claims from no nparticipa t i ng househ olds (house holds not curren t l y re ceiving Cal F r esh benefits) when the county h as do cumentation that t h e liab le indivi dual cann ot be located. The county wil l not refer collection s of all I PV clai ms when: The house hold has al ready repaid the OI, or The county has do cumentation show ing the house hold (and i t s spon sor) cannot be loca t e d, or County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Management of Claims 63-45 5 2 of 3 The county determi nes t h at collection actio n will preju dice the case aga inst a househol d member referre d f o r legal prose cution 63-45 5.3 Su s p e n ding Col lec ti on of Claims: Suspendi ng Collection of AE and I H E cl a i m s If colle ct i on actio n has been initiated and a t least o ne dema nd le t ter has b een sen t , the coun t y may suspen d f u rt h er collection actio n of a n AE o r IHE cla im against a nonp articipating h ousehol d when: The house hold cann ot be located or The cost of f u rt h er collection a ct i on is likely to exceed the a mount that can be recovered Suspendi ng Collection of IPV Claims If collection actio n has been ini t i ated, and demand l et ters ha ve been sent, the county may suspen d further colle ct i on action on any IPV claim ag ainst a nonpa rt i cipating hou sehold or its spon sor when: The ho usehold o r i t s spo nsor cannot be loca t e d or The cost of f u rt h er collection a ct i on is likely to exceed the a mount that can be recovered Deman d letters will be sen t as foll ows: At least one deman d lett e r f or cl aims of less than $100 At least t w o demand le t ters for clai ms b etween $100 a nd $400 At least three deman d letters f o r cl aims of more than $400 63-45 5.4 Action Against Indi v i duals Failin g to Respond to Collection Lette rs: For n onparticip ating househol ds, the county will pursue other collection action s, as appropria t e , to obtain the amo unt o wed on a claim for any house hold or sponsor who fai ls t o resp ond to written deman d letters for repayment of any AE, IHE or IPV clai m, unless the coun t y can determi ne that su ch actions are g enerall y no t cost effective. Other collectio n act i ons may includ e, bu t ar e not limited to: Referral s t o col lection and / o r si milar private and p ublic sector age ncies State tax refund intercep t Lottery offsets Wage garn ishments Property li ens Small cl aims court Unemp loyment Compe nsation Benefits interce pt arr angements may be mad e t o i ntercept the liab le indivi duals un employment compe nsation ben efits to coll ect any claim. This collection may be incl uded as part of a repayme nt ag reement Publi c Se rvice  if authorized b y a co urt, the val ue of a claim may be pai d by t h e househo ld performin g public servi ce Tax Intercept Program Unde r t he T ax Intercep t Prog ram, a ny individ ual who has an outst a nding Ca lFresh OI may ha ve his/her State and / o r Fed eral tax return "intercep t e d" by t he California D epartment of Social Service s (CDSS) throug h t h e St a t e Fran chise Tax Board (FTB) and/or the Internal Reven ue Service (IRS). The indi vidual's tax refund di verted to t he county will be ap plied as payme nt a gainst the claim. The county wil l n ot intercept taxes simultane ously while an OI is bei ng recoupe d either by allotmen t red uction or regul ar payments. Customers contactin g st aff with que st i ons regardi ng the Int e rcept Program are to be referred t o the App eals depa rt me nt for an Admi nistrative Revie w. If the indi vidual has re quested a County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalFresh Program Guide Number Page Management of Claims 63-45 5 3 of 3 State hearin g or is awaiting a de cision from a State hearin g, the cou nty sh all notify CDSS to remove the indi vidual from the tax intercep t prog ram (MPP 20-403.24). 63-45 5.5 Delin quent Claims: A CalFresh OI claim is consi dered del inquent if: The claim ha s not been paid b y the d ue date, and a satisfactory payment arran gement has not been ma de. T h e date of delinqu ency for t h e claim is the due date on the i nitial written notificatio n/demand letter. The claim wi ll remain del inquen t un t i l payment is received i n f u ll, a satisfactory paymen t ag reement is negotia t e d, o r a llotment reduction b egun. A payme nt arrange ment has be en establ ished, and a sched uled p ayment has n ot been made by the due date. The date o f delin quency f or the cl aim is the due date of the mi ssed in st al lment paymen t . The claim wi ll remain deli nquent until pa yment i s rece ived in full, allotmen t redu ct i on begu n, o r the co unty determines to either resu me or renegotia t e the re payment schedul e. A claim wi ll not be conside red delin quent if: Another claim for t h e same househo ld is currently be ing pa id ei t h er through an i nstallment agree ment or allotmen t red uction, and the coun t y exp ects t o b egin coll ection on the cla im once the prior cl aim(s) is sett l ed. The county is una ble to determine de linque ncy st atus be cause colle ct i on is coordina t e d through the co urt system. Once a CalFresh claim has been d elinqu ent f or three consecutive years, the onl y a llowab le collection method is throu gh t h e Treasury Off set Progra m (T OP). The county must stop all other col lection methods an d a ll demand / re payment notices bei ng sent. Program Impact/s: None Refer ences: ACL 20-2 4; AC L 16-108; ACL 19-5 0; AC L 18-99; ACL 15-95 ; ACL 1 3-79, ACL 13-79E ACIN 1-33-1 4; MPP 63 -801; MPP 20-400.1 Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be revie wed for continua nce by 05/31/2023 Approval for Release: RICK WANNE, Director Eligi bility Operation s

title: 63-456 Restoration of Benefits
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide N u m b er Page Restora ti on of Benefits 63-45 6 1 of 4 Revision Date 03/02/20 20 Back g r o und: CalFresh b enefits will be re st o red when the loss i s du e t o the sp ecific reasons detai led in 63-4 56.1. This revisio n updates the section to the new f orm at . There ar e no changes du e t o state leg islation. Purpose: This section de scribes the regula t i ons regardi ng the restoration of CalFresh b enefits. Poli c y: 63-45 6.1 En titleme n t to Restora ti on of L ost Be n e fi ts : CalFresh b enefits will be g iven back to a customer whe n: The loss of bene f i t s wa s d ue to an administrative e rror or An admin istrative disqua lification for an Intention al Program Viol ation (IPV) is reversed by a judg e or court action or Regu lations state that the customer is entitled to a restoratio n of l ost b enefits Lost bene f i t s can b e restored for up to 12 months prior to the date the custome r re quests the restoration o r 1 2 months prior to the date the county disco vers or is notified that a loss of benefits occurred . Cu st o mers do not need to be curren t l y eligibl e t o C alFresh to receive a restora t i on of lost bene f i t s. Take the follow ing action whe n it is discovered that the customer may be e ntitled to receive a restoration o f lo st be nefits: o Revie w t h e case o Compu t e the C alFresh bene f i t s for the months in qu estion o Issue lost bene f i t s (reg ardless of customers curren t el igibil ity st atus) o I ssu e lost benefits (in add ition to the customers regul ar allotment amou nt) 63-45 6.2 Restoration o f Be n e fi ts D u e to Judicial Review: Restore l ost be nefits when instructed by an y judicial act i on. Benefits that are being restore d due to a state hearin g will be restore d f or 12 months prior to the date the state hearin g was initiated. If t h e judi cial action is the first action the customer ha s t ake n t o g et l ost b enefits restored, then benefits wil l be restored for 12 mo nths prior to the date the judici al action was in itiated. 63-45 6.3 Restoration o f Be n e fi ts due to Rever sal o f an IPV Disqual ification: If an I PV di squalifica t i on is reversed by a ju dicial actio n, the ho usehold w ill be entitle d t o an y benefits lost durin g t h e months that t h at cu st o mer was disqua lified. Benefits wil l be restored12 mon t h s prior to the date the county is notified of the reversa l. Howe ver, if the custome r was disqual ified in an ad ministrative disqu alification h earing that occurred before the ju dicial reve rsal, benefits will be rest o red from t h e eff e ct i ve date of the n otice of act i on informin g t h e househo ld of t h e administrative di squalifica t i on. For each month the custome r w as disqual ified, calculate the al lotment the customer should h ave receive d with the disqua lified indi vidual in the h ousehol d and compare that to the allo t me nt the house hold recei ved. I f the customer recei ved a smaller al lotment than it should have re ceived, issue the difference . County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalFresh Program Guide N u m b er Page Restora ti on of Benefits 63-45 6 2 of 4 63-45 6.4 L ost Be n e fi ts D u e to County Error: If a l oss of benefits occurs and the customer i s en t i t l ed to restoration of those bene f i t s, take immedi ate action to restore those bene f i t s. No actio n by t he cust o mer is required . A formal appl ication for restoration of lost ben efits i s n ot re quired. Docume nt a ny verbal restoratio n requests in case commen t s an d image any wri t ten re quests. Do not restore be nefits t h at w ere lost more than 12 months pri or to t he month the loss was discove red or reported to the county. Notify the customer of the follow ing: The amoun t of lost ben efits be ing restored Any offsetting that was done The right to appe al if t h e customer disagre es with the lost benefits process 63-45 6.5 Calculatio n of Lo s t Months for Erroneous Delays, Denials or Terminatio n: Lost benefits w ill b e restore d whe n app lications are delayed , denie d or terminated due t o county error. If the customer was eli gible, but received the wrong al lotment amount, t he l oss of bene f i t s wil l b e calcul ated for t h e months the househ old participa t e d in CalFresh. If a customer did no t have an opportun ity to participa t e because of an i ncorrect dela y, denial or terminatio n of b enefits, t he loss of benefits will be ca lculated as follo ws: Erroneous Delay If an el igible custome rs a pplicatio n w as de layed (beyon d the 30-d ay time li mit), determi ne t he months the loss of ben efits o ccurred based on regulation s i n T i me Limits and Dela ys 63-109. Erroneous Denial When a customer s appl ication has be en den ied i n error, t h e month the lo ss initia lly occu rred wi ll be the month of appl ication. If t h e customer filed a time ly recertification, the mon t h t he loss initial ly occurred w ill be the mon t h follow ing the expira t i on of t he cert i f i cation perio d. Erroneous Termination If the customer's benefits were terminated in error, the month the loss ini t i ally occurred will be the first month ben efits w ere not received du e t o the i ncorrect termination . 63-45 6.6 O ffs ettin g Lost Benefits: When a budg et re- computation results in lost ben efits an d the re is a lso an uncoll ected I H E o r IPV overissu ance (O I), t h e lo st bene f i t s must be used to off se t the O I. Do n ot offset Ad ministrative Error (AE) claims aga inst lost benefits. Note: Lopez v. Glickman prohib its offsetting o f Administrative Error (AE) claim s agai nst any amount of lost benefits whi ch have not yet been restored to the hou sehold. When a house hold is certified and rece ives an initial a llotment, t h is initial all otment i s no t con sidered lost bene f i t s an d will not be redu ced to off se t cla ims, e ven if t he allotment is paid re t ro actively. 63-45 6.7 Dispu te d Be n e fi ts : Customers t h at disagree with the de t e rmination of lost benefits ma y request a state h earing. State heari ngs must be requested within 90 days of the date the househ old is notified of the entitlemen t or non-e ntitlement of lost benefits. I f a state hearing is requ ested before or during the time lost bene f i t s are bei ng restored, issue the lost benefits pendi ng the results of the state hea ring. content: 63-601 Application (Q&A) Table o f Contents Subject Question/A nswer Appli cation Processin g Requ esting Verificatio n W i t h in the 30 Day Timeframe Expedi t e d Services Postpone d and Unavai lable Veri f i cat i on Requesting Verification Withi n the 30 Day Timeframe An ap plicant ap plies for C alFresh on June 4th an d is schedu led for the first intervi ew on June 8 th . At t h e time of appli cation, the applican t is given a ge neric l ist of verificatio ns to pro vide wi t h the ap plication . The appl icant misses the interview an d the cou nty sen ds t he N otice of Missed Intervie w (NOMI). On June 14 th the househ old resched ules the appoin t me nt for June 30 th . The interview is held, b ut inco me verificatio n is mi ssing. The worker gives the client 10 days to provid e the missing ve rification. The appli cant does not provide the mi ssing verificatio n by the 30 th day follo wing the ap plication . The veri f i cation is receive d in the second 30-d ay period on Jul y 8 th . QUESTIO N Can the appli cation be denied on the 30 th day af ter the appli cation, if the verificatio n was not received w ithout a 10-day waitin g period? ANSWER No. T he ap plication can not be de nied withou t waitin g an additiona l 1 0 days for veri f i cation. Since the worker correctly a llowed 10 days for the missing ve rification, the worker, in esse nce, pended the ap plication beyon d the 3 0-day ap plication processin g time frame. Refer to Section 63-10 9.5(b) . Steffens v. McMah on provi des that the CalFresh appli cation must be processe d withi n the establishe d time f ram e as provided in Section 63- 109.1 , which is 30 days from the receip t of the i nitial appli cation. The appl ication is conside red processed if on t h e 3 0 th day the worker deni es or se nds a notice expl aining what the househ old mu st provide to complete the ap plication w ithin those extende d 30 days. ACIN I-16-05 Postponed and Unavailable Verification A family appl ied, and was app roved, for CalFresh expe dited services in Jan uary, with postpone d verification (i ncome). The family had appl ied a f ter the 15 th of t h e month and was certifie d for Ja nuary an d February. The famil y reported at the en d of Jan uary that the person whose inco me veri f i cation was p ending (postpon ed) l eft the home at the end of Janu ary and postponed verification is not avai lable. QUESTIO N Shoul d t h e worker disreg ard the postponed ve rification since the owne r of that inco me left t he home? ANSWER A co llateral contact sh ould be mad e to the in dividua l who left, if contact i nf o rmation w as provid ed by t he house hold. T he worker will otherwi se assist the househ old in ob t a ining the ne cessary verification as docume ntation for benefits paid in January. Section 63-117 4 states t h at a worker must continu e to assist recip ients in obtai ning requ ired verification w hen necessa ry. Althoug h docu mentary evi dence is the primary source for all verificatio n, colla t e ral contacts continue to be an acce ptable means o f verifying some househol d circumstance s when the wo rker or the house hold cann ot ob t a in documen t a ry evi dence. If it is not po ssible to o btain verification through a collatera l con t a ct or by assisting the househol d, the ve rification wil l not be required . ACIN I-58-06
