title: E. Initial Engagement Activities
content: County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Initi al Engagement Activities 10-00 5.E 1 of 2 Revision Date: 09/1/201 8 Back g r o und: Effective 1/1/2014, Assembly Bill (AB) 74 mod ified t h e WTW se quence to allow indi viduals who are iden t i f i ed during Appra isal as being in ne ed of Me ntal Health/Substan ce A b use and/or Family Stabili zation Services to be en gaged in WTW through these barri er removal activitie s. Purpose : The pu rpose of this re vision i s t o include AB 74 chan ges and st rea mline p olicies and proced ures related to in itial enga gement activities. Poli c y: Newl y referred W TW partici pants, whose CalWORKs ha s been approved f o r the first time o r after a break i n a id longe r tha n 30 days, are require d t o p articipate in Initial Job Search (JS) after Appraisal , unle ss t h ey meet specific exclu sion criteria o r are identifie d as being be t ter se rved by other ini t i al enga gement activitie s such as Family Stab ilization (CPG 10-007.A), Mental H ealth/Substance Abuse Services (MHS/SAS) and / o r Domestic Violen ce Services (CPG 40-1 00.O). Initial engage ment activities may be assigned in se quence or concu rrently prior to the signi ng of t he f i rst WTW plan. Initial Job Se arch Initial JS activitie s i nclude lo oking for suitable j ob openi ngs through ind ependen t an d/or supervised Job Search , contactin g p otential emplo yers, com pleting appl ications, submitting resum es, intervie wing for jo bs and netwo rking. Job Cl ubs may be u sed to develo p job see king strategies a nd inform partici pants of employer s e xpectations and emp loyees respo nsibili t i es. Initial JS i s a core activity that cannot excee d f e deral limi t s (up t o a t o t a l of 6 weeks or up to a total of 12 weeks in a 12-month period whe n the State of C alifornia is conside red a Ne edy State). Initial JS is assigned for up to 4 consecutive weeks. Extensi on(s) be yond the initial 4 weeks may only be appro ved, on e wee k a time, i f neede d to complete schedul ed j ob i nterviews and/or accept emplo yment offer(s) resulting f rom participation in the previ ous weeks. If after the 4 conse cutive weeks there are no pending interview s or j ob offers req uiring a follo w-up, JS exten sion w ill no t be granted a nd an Assessment will b e completed to assign appropria t e a ct i vities in a WTW pl an. The leng t h o f Initia l Job Search may be shorten ed when: Identified b arrier(s) are precl uding partici pation and satisfactory pro gress in assign ed activity The particip ant would be nefit f rom ed ucation or traini ng in place of Initial Job Search activities Initial Job Se arch Exclusion s The follow ing are all owable excl usions from Initial Job Se arch: Participa nt h as barriers that must be addre ssed with different initia l engage ment act i vities Participa nt i s me eting participa t i on require ments with employmen t or sel f -e mployment JS activity con f l icts wi t h empl oyment or pa rt i cipation in SIP or other appro ved educa t i onal/traini ng activity County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Initi al Engagement Activities 10-00 5.E 2 of 2 Participa nt is a 19-yea r old pare nting teen wi t h no high school di ploma or eq uivalen t ce rt i f i cate, who i s i neligib le to participate in C al-Learn Participa nt is a noncitizen victim of human traf ficki ng, d omestic violence or other serious crimes who is not yet au t h orized to work in the Un ited States (CPG 1 0-200.A) Mental H ealth and Substan ce A b use Assessment A particip ant may be referred to MHS an d/or SAS as an initia l engage ment core activities for up t o 4 weeks if there is a con cern that a men t a l hea lth and / o r substance abuse probl em exi st s that wi ll impai r his/he r abi lity to obtain/retai n emp loyment, or particip ate in other WTW activities. An assessmen t a nd devel opment of a W TW pla n are req uired to exten d these activitie s beyond t h e four- week pe riod. WTW Pla n and Treatment Services WTW Pla ns will be de veloped b ased on the results of the mental he alth and/or substance a buse assessmen t , and w ill i nclude appropri ate accommod ations o r restrictions, supportive services, an d treatment requi rements to meet t he participants ne eds. S u bstance Abuse Service s may include: Assessment/Evalu ation Case man agement Treatment and/or Co unselin g Monitori ng of att e ndance and sa t i sf a ct o ry p rogress Referral t o or pro vision of other app ropriate services 10-00 5.E. 5 Su bstance Abuse Treatment and C oncurrent Activities Concu rrent partici pation in a nother WTW activi t y is required if the participa nt is in a substance abuse treatment prog ram for long er than six mo nths. WT W pa rt i cipation re quiremen t s a re conside red to be met and concu rrent act i vities are not requi red if t h e participan t is eithe r: In a state-lice nsed residentia l facili t y or a cer t i f i ed no nresiden t i al su bstance abuse program that req uires hi m/ h er to stay at the pro gram site f o r at lea st three ho urs a d ay, three d ays per week, or Unab le to participate in othe r W TW activities as determi ned by the treatment provide r Procedure: Processin g G u ide 10-005 . E.1 Refer ences: All C ounty Letter (ACL) 15-09, Elig ibility Assistan ce Standards (EA S) 42.711.53, Ca lWO R Ks Program Guide (CPG) 10-0 05.H. Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be revie wed for continua nce by 09/30/2021 .

title: F. Assessment or Reassessment
content: County of Sa n Diego, Health and Human S e rvices Agency (HH SA) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Asse ssment and Reasse ssment 10-00 5.F 1 of 3 Revision Date : May 1, 2021 Back g r o und : The primary focu s of E m ployment S e rvices (ES) is to help particip ants set and ach ieve career g oals and bui ld skills necessary to obtain and retain empl oyment. ES partici pants must be assig ned to activities lea ding to self-sufficiency through empl oyment, ed ucation or training . Employme nt Ca se Manag ers (EC Ms) util ize t h e Asse ssment (ASMT) as the primary t o ol f o r de velopin g the first ES p lan to assign the most app ropriate activitie s a nd supportive servi ces. Purpose : The purp ose of this revisi on is to provi de information per Senate Bi ll (SB) 1232 o n new reg ulations regard ing particip ants who are enrol led in publ icly fund ed postseconda ry e ducation. Poli c y : ASMT is the evaluatio n of vario us factors rela t e d to a pa rt i cipants e mployabi lity, such as personal and family needs, wo rk and education history, caree r goals, areas of st ren gth, skills, a nd nee ds for suppo rt i ve services to remove barri ers t o e mployment and pa rt i cipation. The ECM i s r equired to co mplete an ASMT whe n the particip ant is ready to si gn the first ES plan aft e r: Successfull y co mpleting Initial Job Search Being e xcluded from Initial Job S e arch or other Initial Eng agement activities for a vali d reason Being assig ned t o Men t a l H ealth/Substance Abuse/Famil y Viol ence Services in excess of four consecu t i ve weeks, which req uires the devel opment of a plan Note: An ASMT is no t required to a ssign activitie s and suppo rt i ve services spe cified in a F a mily Reun ification Plan (C PG 40 . 1 83.D). ES Participan t s Enro lled in Publicl y F un ded Postsecond ary E d ucation ES particip ants enroll ed in publi c l y f un ded postseco ndary educa t i on will complete an A SMT or Reasse ssment (ASMT2) only f or t h e purpose of assigni ng appro priate activitie s to address i dentified barrie rs. If ASMT /ASMT2 is comple t e d, the ou t co me ca nnot be used to limit or restrict a pa rt i cipants choice i n education al or training go als. ES pa rt i cipants ca nnot be prevented from attend ing scho ol du e to a barrie r or p laced in Non complian ce for refusa l to complete ASMT/ASMT2. The ECM wi ll do cument the reason f o r refusal to compl ete ASMT/ASMT 2 in case comments. Note : Stud ents not enrolle d in pub licly funded postseconda ry educa t i on ar e still require d to complete an ASMT/ASMT 2 , as appl icable, to develop a plan to assign ap propriate activitie s an d n ecessary suppo rt i ve services. title: G. Employment Services Plan
content: County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 1 of 3 Revision Date: October 01, 2025 Background: Employment Services (ES) participants must be assigned to activities leading to self-sufficiency through employment, education and/or training. These activities are assigned through an ES plan using the Welfare-To-Work Plan Activity Assignment (WTW 2) form after the participant’s initial engagement. Per state regulations, an ES plan must include activities and services designed to remove barriers to participation and employment leading to self-sufficiency. Purpose: The purpose of this revision is to provide guidance on ES plan requirements for Student Training and Education Program (STEP) participants attending publicly funded or nonprofit postsecondary educational institutions per Senate Bill (SB) 768. Policy: Assessment ES participants will be assessed for the following items when developing an ES plan:  Work history and job readiness  Education level and vocational interest and goals  Learning Disabilities (LD)  Mental Health, Substance Use Disorder, Domestic Violence  Basic reading/math competencies  English language skills  Local labor market conditions  Other needs, such as Family Stabilization and Housing Procedure: Timeframe All non-exempt customers are required to sign an ES plan within 90 calendar days of whichever occurs first: the completion of initial Job Search or other initial engagement activities, the date the customer’s eligibility for cash aid is determined, or the date the customer is required to participate in ES. The 90-day period to develop an ES plan does not include the time that a participant spends in good cause determination, compliance or sanction curing processes, or time between the date an LD evaluation appointment is scheduled and the date the final report is received (up to a maximum of 90 days). The 90-day period will resume after the final report from the LD evaluator is received, or on the 91st day if the final report has not been received. All participants are required to sign an ES plan except participants who are assigned to initial engagement activities as referenced in Processing Guide 10-005.E1. Elements of the ES Plan All ES plans will include the following:  Participation status County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 2 of 3  Total hourly requirements  Activities, location, schedule and hours  Date when participation verification is due  Standards for maintaining satisfactory progress  ES supportive services, including accommodations  Participant's certification, including rights and responsibilities  Date to change terms of the ES Plan  Participant and Employment Case Manager (ECM) signature/date Change to an ES Plan Any time there is a change in a participant's current activity, a new ES plan is required. Participants have:  30 days from the beginning of their initial ES activity to request a change or reassignment to another activity Note: This is only available once in a lifetime to each participant  3 business days after signing an ES plan to evaluate and request changes to the terms of the plan If the participant and the ECM are unable to reach an agreement on the ES plan, the matter must be referred to a Third-Party Assessor for a review of the participant's assessment and ES plan. Prior to making the third-party referral, the ECM must contact their assigned Self-Sufficiency Services (SSS) Program Specialist to review the request and the ES plan to ensure the plan is suitable for the participant's self-sufficiency goals. The ECM is required to contact the participant and schedule an appointment to complete a reassessment prior to the expiration of the current ES plan. The ECM will document all efforts to contact the participant and attempt to conduct the reassessment to avoid gaps in services. Backdating of an ES Plan Backdating of an ES activity start date on the WTW 2 is only allowed when a participant contacts the ECM timely to report new employment or a new educational activity and:  The participant is unable to attend an appointment to complete a WTW 2 due to work or school schedule conflicts  The ECM does not follow-up with the participant timely and the WTW 2 is not signed within the appropriate time frames due to ECM error Limited and Non-English-Speaking Participants The ES plan must be provided in a language that is understood by the participant. When the ES plan is not available in the participant's preferred language, bilingual staff or interpreter services must be provided. Use of bilingual staff or interpreter services during the development of the ES plan must be clearly documented in a journal entry. County of San Diego, Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) Program Guide Employment Services Plan Number Page 10-005.G 3 of 3 Enrollment in Publicly Funded or Nonprofit Postsecondary Education ES participants enrolled in publicly funded or nonprofit postsecondary educational institutions are required to sign a WTW 2 plan each semester/quarter to receive supportive services. If enrollment verification is obtained, the ECM will develop/sign the WTW 2 plan with the participant and issue an Advance Standard Payment (ASP) at least 10 calendar days prior to the beginning of the academic period. If enrollment verification is not obtained at least 10 calendar days prior to the beginning of the academic period, the ECM will develop/sign the WTW 2 plan with the participant and issue an ASP no later than 10 calendar days from the date of receipt of all required items. If the participant provided school enrollment verification and the WTW 2 plan is not developed/signed timely with the participant for the next academic period, an ASP will be issued to the participant. The ECM will follow-up with the participant regarding the development and signing of any ES plans as required. See Processing Guide 10-011.A2 Ancillary Supportive Services for information regarding ASP and reimbursements. Important: The ECM will discuss the importance of reporting school enrollment as soon as possible with the participant to ensure timely issuance of an ASP and successful participation. Procedure: Processing Guide 10-005.G1 References: Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) 42-711.4-.8, 42-714.2, 42.750.2-.4 All County Information Notices (ACIN) 1-03-19 All County Letter (ACL) 15-80, 20-120, 21-04, 21-75E, 22-80, 24-32 Sunset Date: This policy will be reviewed for continuance on or by October 31, 2028. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficiency Services

title: I. Case Transfers and Returns Between Regions
content: Page 1 of 2 I. Case Transfers a n d Returns Betwee n Re g ions Case Tra n s fer Overview When a Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participa nt move s f rom on e county region to anothe r, the curre nt Employme nt Case Manager must transfer t h e case to the new regio n where the partici pant now reside s f or con t i nued service s. Status Codes for Transfer Case s Cases in active status can be transferred. C ases with sanctioned and no n-complia nt indi viduals in non-active statuses can be transferred when mutual agreemen t is reache d between the send ing and recei ving regio ns. Transfer of Companion Case s Compa nion cases (spouse, child, teen of the particip ant) mu st be transferred together. Transfer Procedures for WTW Case s Refer t o CalWORKs Processing Guide 10-260.A.1 WTW Do cument Cap t u re Activities Transferr i ng Sanctioned and/or Compliance Plan Cases Cases may not be transferred when there is a pend ing sanction or pendi ng comple t i on of a complia nce plan, excep t on a case-by-case ba sis when mu t ua l agree ment is re ached b etween the sendin g and receiving region . Regi ons shou ld assign t h e authority to accept cases i n non-active status to a speci f i c st a f f leve l or person . When a WT W san ct i oned in dividua l moves and it is in the ir best intere st t o have his or her W TW case transferre d to the new re gion of resi dence to facili t a t e a concil iation or sa nction cure, the sen ding reg ion shoul d follow the procedure belo w: Step Action 1 Contact the new re gion and req uest acceptance of sanction case t ran sf e r. If the reg ion agree s to accep t the case , then con t i nue to Step 2. 2 Compl ete t h e WT W Case T ra nsfer/Closing C hecklist (27-31 3) ensuring all appro priate areas are ch ecked. Write in Comments section tha t the pa rt i cipant is in sanction ed or non- compli ance status. Note the name of the perso n in the receivin g region who a greed to accept the case. 3 Ensure t h at case is sent to receiving region within 24 ho urs of the time the mutual ag reement was reach ed for t ran sf e r. Timing of Transfer of Cases may not be transferred after the 20 th of t he month u nless su pportive se rvice paymen t s for t h e next month have been approved and issue d. This is to en sure that Page 2 of 2 Case all ne cessary supportive pa yments are issued timel y. Transfers to Incorrect Regions Cases transferre d t o a n inappro priate region w ill be returne d t o the sen ding regi on. Former Refugee Case s Unle ss a Federal Off i ce of Refugee Rese t tle ment (ORR) waiver is in ef fect, refugee cases, for people who ha ve be en in t h e U nited States for five or more years, are t o be tran sf e rred from the Re f u gee WTW Employment Servi ces provid er region s to the mainstrea m W TW Regio ns. Case R eturn Regi ons must ke ep the number o f returned cases to the lowest level p ossible t o avoid un necessary disrup t i on of service s, inco nvenien ce a nd confusion to particip ants. A case sha ll only be return ed if at l east one of t h e f o llowin g occurs: 1. One of the followi ng require d f orm s i s mi ssing, as appropri ate: Signed WTW 1 Completed a ssessment with case comments Current and ap propriate WTW P l an Activi t i es open in Ca lWI N mu st match assi gned activities on t he W TW Plan Note: I n a si t ua t i on whe re the applican t has no t reached the stage f o r obtain ing a p articular form, the case canno t b e returned f or missing such a form. 2. There are no appropria t e C alWIN participatio n entries for the last month. 3. A require d service is not provid ed. Example: The case record indicates t he participa nt requested a ncillary paymen t s for tools to attend an ap proved vocatio nal training a nd there is no record of issuance of such paymen t , nor is there explana t i on f o r no n-issuance . Since supportive servi ces were no t a pproved, it is po ssible that the p articipant may not be abl e t o participate in req uired activities. 4. A require d referral is not made. Example: The Simple Scre ening Instrument for Substance Abu se indicates a high degree of abu se but a referral wa s not made to the Coun t y Al cohol and Drug Servi ces.

title: B. Child Care Eligibility
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Child C are Eli gibili t y 10.010 . B 1 of 8 Revision Date: Oct o ber 1, 2025 Back g r o und: The Ca lWO R Ks St a ge One Ch ild Care (Stage One C hild Ca re) program is for current an d former CalWORKs cu st o mers. The pro gram assists in payin g for chil d care se rvices to a provider of the customers ch oice. CalWORKs customers w ill be au t h orized for 24 mon t h s of ch ild care up on CalWORKs ap proval or a nytime thereafter whe n a CalWORKs custome r indicates a need for chil d care. Purpose: The purpose of thi s section is to expl ain t h e criteri a for Stage O ne Chi ld Care eligibi lity. The ma t er ial revisio ns are to i ncorporate p olicies t o extend 12-mo nth eligi bility to 24 months and t o clarify pol icies for aband onment of care, discontin uing child care, and verification of a chil ds exception al needs. Poli c y: CalWORKs customers, who meet child care eligib ility criteria, will have access to 24 months of Stage One Chil d Care once they are d etermined eli gible for Cal W ORKs, and they: Are reque st i ng child care se rvices. Have secu red a child care p rovider. Are expected to be re f e rred to Employment Services (ES). Eligi ble Adult CalWORKs customers w ho are eligi ble to receive Stage One C hild Care i nclude: Manda t o ry ES pa rt i cipants. Cal-L earn (CL) partici pants. ES exempt volun t e ers. ES sanctio ned particip ants who express an i nt e nt to cure the sa nction. San ct i oned or p enalize d partici pants w ho a re wo rking or pa rt i cipating in county-appro ved a ct i vities. CalWORKs famili es with no aide d adults are not elig ible for Stage One Chil d Care, for example: Adults recei ving Suppl emental Security Income (SSI) bene f i t s. Inelig ible non citizen adults. Non-n eedy caretaker rela t i ves. Timed-ou t ad ults eligib le to S tag e T w o Child Ca re. Timed-ou t an d F o rmer CalWORKs Customers Timed-ou t adults and f o rmer CalWORKs custome rs who rece ived aid within the past 24 mo nt h s may receive P o st Aid child care service s t hro ugh Stage One unde r the fol lowing ci rcumstances: The CalWORKs cust o mer can not rece ive ch ild care se rvices i n Stage Two because of p rogram barrie rs o r ot h er administrative i ssues. The child ca re services are not avai lable in Stag e T w o or S tag e T h ree due to funding . The custome r will benefit from re maining with Stage O n e Chil d Care services; for exa mple, when a customer has a req uest f o r re t ro active child care that isn t al lowed in Stag e T w o. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Child C are Eli gibili t y 10.010 . B 2 of 8 Timed-ou t adults and f o rmer CalWORKs custome rs who rece ived aid within the past 24 mo nt h s, and ES pa rt i cipants w ho are in a lon g-term sanctio n, will be ref e rred to St a ge Two Child Care, unless t h ey meet one of the circumstan ces listed above . Eligi ble Chil dren Chil dren up to and through age 12 are eligibl e to receive child care services. Child ren w ho ar e und er court sup ervision ma y receive se rvices up to age 18. Ch ildren w ith exception al need s and/or who are severel y d isabled ma y co ntinue to receive chi ld care services up t o ag e 21. Children m ay receive Sta g e One Child C are when a l l the follo wing ap ply: And at l e ast one o f the follo wing ap plies: The paren t ha s a n eed for child care services. The family is recei ving CalWORKs, or receive d CalWORKs within the la st 24 months and ch ild care isn t ava ilable i n Stage Two or Stage Three C hild Care. There is no pa rent or legal gu ardian or member of the Assistance U nit (AU) living in the home who is able an d availab le to provid e child care. Lack of child care would resu lt in the customer not bei ng able to partici pate in ES or CL activities, empl oyment, or any other coun t y ap proved activity. The child i s a m ember of t h e AU, includin g the child o f a C L participant. The child i s n ot a member of t h e AU becau se t h e child is recei ving SSI/ State Suppl ementary Payment (SSP) benefits or is in a Foster Care pro gram. The child i s a m ember of a f a mily with a former CalWORKs pare nt (w ho received aid w ithin the past 24 months) who has a verified c hild care nee d. The chi ld is a non-AU mem ber, but a CalWORKs pare nt i s re sponsibl e f or the care and co ntrol of t h at ch ild (for example exempt stepsib ling or hal f -si bling). The preferred p lacement for 11 and 12 -year-old chil dren is in a before or after schoo l program. Subsid ized ch ild ca re shou ld onl y be utilized for the portion of care needed that is not avai lable in a before or after schoo l program. Howe ver, to en sure child care ne eds are met: Chil dren may con t i nue to receive child care subsidize d services wh en a before or aft e r school progra m is not availabl e. Famili es may combine care provid ed i n a before or a f ter school prog ram wi t h subsi dized child care for those hours wh en the before or after school pro gram does not ope rate. Note: Child ren w ho are 1 2 yea rs ol d w hen certified must be certified for no less than 12 mo nths o f child care. If a child turns 13 years old during the first 1 2 months of the eligib ility pe riod, their certification of child care services should clearl y indi cate that t h ey are only eligi ble f or 12 months, in cluding time af ter they turn 13 years. Their el igibil ity does not extend to 24 months. When chi ld care i s b eing de t e rmined for a chi ld 13 throu gh 21 yea rs of age becau se the child is physica lly or mentall y incapab le of caring for self, verifica t i on must be provid ed that the child re quires child ca re or supervisio n. The pa rent must pro vide: Form 24-707 D ocumentation of a Chi lds Exception al Needs, and A written statement from a physicia n or licensed or certifie d psycholog ist, or County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Child C are Eli gibili t y 10.010 . B 3 of 8 Verificatio n of SSI/SSP bene f i t , or Individ ualized Ed ucation Program (IEP) and Form 24-7 93 St a t e ment of Exce ptional Nee ds. Note: I f a provider requests an adjusted reimburse ment rate to co ver extra costs for caring for a chi ld with excep t i onal nee ds, the pro vider must submit verificatio n of the a ccommodation an d extra costs need ed to meet the child s exceptiona l needs. For more informa t i on about excep t i onal nee ds rate adju st me nts se e CPG 1 0-010.E Child Care Payments and 10-0 10.E1 Payment Procedure s. Two-Paren t Famil ies Stage One Chil d Care will not be gran t e d f or two-p arent househo lds in which one pa rent i s ab le and avail able to pro vide care for the children. A pa rent is conside red avail able to provi de care un less they are worki ng (or sleepi ng after working a ni ght shift ), goi ng to school, participa t i ng in an app roved ES activity o r has a conditio n that pre vents them from caring f or the chil dren. When both pa rents are particip ating in ES, working, or are otherwi se u navaila ble to care f o r thei r ch ildren, Stage One Chil d Care w ill be made ava ilable to them. title: C. Child Care Provider Requirements
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-010: CHILD CARE
TITLE: C. STAGE ONE CHILD CARE PROVIDER REQUIREMENTS

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
This section specifies regulatory qualifications, background clearance standards, and health and safety requirements for child care providers receiving CalWORKs Stage One Child Care reimbursements under CDSS MPP EAS 47-240 and California Education Code Section 8200.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & PROVIDER CATEGORIES
• Licensed Child Care Providers: Licensed child care centers and licensed family child care homes operating with an active license issued by the CDSS Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD). Verification consists of active license confirmation.
• License-Exempt Child Care Providers: Care provided by relatives (grandparents, aunts, uncles, adult siblings) or non-relative friends in the child's home or provider's home.
• TrustLine Background Clearance: Non-relative license-exempt providers must be registered and fingerprinted through the TrustLine registry before payments can be authorized. Payments cannot be issued to non-relatives who fail TrustLine clearance.
• Health & Safety Self-Certification: License-exempt providers must complete the Health and Safety Self-Certification form certifying basic fire, safety, and health standards in the care facility.
• Ineligible Providers: Parents, legal guardians, members of the assistance unit, and individuals convicted of violent crimes or child abuse are strictly prohibited from serving as paid child care providers.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Provider Form Issuance: Issue the Child Care Provider Request and TrustLine forms to the customer.
• TrustLine Tracking: Verify TrustLine clearance status via the electronic state registry before releasing child care payment checks.
• Rate Verification: Confirm the provider's requested rate does not exceed the statutory Regional Market Rate (RMR) ceiling.

title: D. Child Care Approval or Denial
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-010: CHILD CARE
TITLE: D. APPROVAL OR DENIAL OF STAGE ONE CHILD CARE

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Under CDSS MPP EAS 47-300, County HHSA must promptly determine eligibility and authorize Stage One Child Care assistance for CalWORKs participants who need child care to participate in approved Welfare-to-Work (WTW) activities, education, or unsubsidized employment.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & DECISION TIMEFRAMES
• Timeliness of Approval: The caseworker must approve or deny child care requests within 10 calendar days of receiving completed application forms and provider information.
• 12-Month Continuous Authorization: Once approved, Stage One Child Care must be authorized for a minimum of 12 continuous months without requiring re-verification of income, work hours, or participation, regardless of temporary changes in hours.
• Grounds for Approval: Child care is approved when:
  (1) The participant is engaging in an approved WTW activity, job search, education, or employment;
  (2) The child is a member of the AU or child-only unit under 13 years of age (or up to 18 if disabled); and
  (3) The chosen provider meets all licensing or TrustLine requirements.
• Grounds for Denial: Requests are denied only when the provider fails background clearance, child age exceeds statutory limits, or the parent refuses to participate in an approved activity.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Written Notice Requirement: Issue an approval or denial Notice of Action (NOA) to both the participant and the child care provider within the 10-day timeframe.
• Payment Certificate: Issue the Child Care Payment Certificate outlining approved hours, monthly authorized reimbursement amounts, and billing submission instructions.
• Transition to Stage Two: Coordinate transfer to the local Alternative Payment Program (APP) for Stage Two Child Care as the participant approaches 24 months of aid.

The RMR is a resul t of a survey comp leted by child ca re providers. The RMRs are use d by t h e Californi a Department of Social Servi ces and t h e Dep artment of Educa t i on to d etermine the maximum payment H U Top U rates. RMRs are determined by the type of provi der, age grou ps of the child ren, how a provid er charge s (hourly, w eekly or monthly), full-time or part-time rates, and categ ories of care. The RMR represen t s the maximum that each child care prog ram can pay for child care . If a provider charg es l ess t ha n t he R MR ceiling rate, paymen t is for the rate that i s be ing charged . How ever, should the actual cost of chil d care exceed t he RMR ceilin g rates, the parent is respon sible for p aying the diff e rence in t h e cost (referred to as co - paymen t ). See Specia l Notice 15-09 for San Diego County RMR ceili ngs, effective 10/1/2015 . 3B Maximum Payme n t Ra te The maximum pa yment rate f o r child care is set b y the State at the rate where 85% of providers charge less, an d 15% charge more for the same type of care for the same age ch ild in a give n regio n. Reimb ursement ceiling s for t yp es of care are fou nd on the H U Depa rt me nt of Education w ebsite. U 4B Rate Categories H U Top U The foll owing payment gui deline s will be used when determining the provid er reimburseme nt: Rate Type Desc rip tion Hourl y Hourl y rates shall be used when h ours of care are less than 30 h ours p er we ek an d less than six h ours on any da y; or An unsched uled but documented need of less than six ho urs per occurrence, such as the p arents nee d to wo rk overtime, tha t exceeds t he certified need f or child ca re; or The portion of the certified need for child care exceed s 52.5 hours pe r week and t h e hou rs are not durin g t h e provider s n ormal opera t i ng hours. Dail y Dail y ra t e s sha ll be used when h ours of ca re are six hour or mor e per day; or An unschedul ed bu t documen t e d need of six or more hours per occurre nce, su ch a s the pare nts ne ed t o work overtime, that e xceeds t h e certifie d n eed f o r child ca re. Part- Time Weekly Part-time we ekly rates sha ll be u sed when hours of car e are less than 3 0 hours per wee k. When establi shing a rate category for a child, sel ect the appro priate rate category based on the need for child care, how the p rovider label s their rates, an d wh ether the provid er can docu ment wh at a private-pa y family pays for the same servi ces. The C ounty is no t bound by the RMR ceiling when there are no more than two child care provi ders of the t yp e need ed by the client i n the county. 8B Payme n t Requirements Chil d Care Payments are: Made by the contractor d irectly to t h e chil d care provide r on behalf of the client on a monthly basi s a f ter the chil d care service has been re ndered. Not made by the con t ra ct o r d irectly to t h e client. Not made in ad vance b y the contractor, for services n ot yet provid ed. Made according to the pro viders a ct u al charge s as requ ested on the Att e ndance Shee t submitted and as indi cated on t h e Parent/Provid er Fee Agreemen t , up to the maxi mum pa yment allo wable by the State, for full-time or part-time rates. No co-pa yments will be req uired or enforced b y the co ntractor. 10B Family Fees 11BH U Top U Some f a milies are req uired t o pay a portio n of thei r child care costs. This portio n is called the f ami ly fee. Family fees, if any, are base d on the fee s c hedule establi shed by the State and shall be paid by the paren t di rectly t o the ch ild care provi der. Chil dren at Risk: The Fami ly Fee ma y also be wai ved for child ren at risk of abuse, neg lect, o r exploitation , as d etermined by a legally qua lified profession al from a legal , medica l, or social se rvice agency, or emerg ency shelter, for a period of up to three months. Cumul ative Exemptio n Period: The cumulative time perio d for the t w o fee exemptio ns li st e d ab ove for families shall not exceed 1 2 months. 13B Registration Fee 14BH U Top U The Cou nty w ill pay reg istration fees charge d by license d child care provid ers, as lon g as these fees are the same as those charged private-p ay familie s. title: F. Child Care Notices of Action
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-010: CHILD CARE
TITLE: F. NOTICES OF ACTION FOR STAGE ONE CHILD CARE

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
In accordance with CDSS MPP EAS 47-400 and state due process mandates, County HHSA must provide formal written Notices of Action (NOAs) to both the client and the child care provider whenever child care benefits are approved, denied, changed, or terminated.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & NOTICE PERIODS
• Timely Notice Standards: Any action that reduces child care hours, lowers reimbursement rates, or terminates child care requires a minimum 10-day advance notice before the effective date of the action.
• Adequate Notice for Approvals: Approvals and rate increases require adequate notice delivered to the client and provider on or before the effective date.
• Concurrent Provider Notice: The child care provider must receive a concurrent copy of any notice affecting payment authorization, hours of care, or termination of provider reimbursement.
• Required Notice Elements: Every notice must state:
  (1) The specific regulatory action being taken;
  (2) The legal citations under CDSS MPP EAS Chapter 47;
  (3) The exact dollar amount or hours affected;
  (4) The client's right to request a formal State Fair Hearing and continue receiving child care benefits pending the hearing outcome (Aid Paid Pending).

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• System Automation: Generate the appropriate CalSAWS NOA template (approval, modification, or termination).
• Dual Mailing: Verify that notices are generated and dispatched simultaneously to the participant's mailing address and the child care provider's facility address.
• Hearing Request Processing: If the client appeals within the 10-day notice window, immediately maintain child care authorizations and notify the child care payment contractor.

title: B. Behavioral Health Services
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-011: SUPPORTIVE SERVICES
TITLE: B. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
The County of San Diego Health and Human Services Agency (HHSA) provides behavioral health services to Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participants to identify, address, and remove mental health and substance abuse barriers that impede self-sufficiency and sustained employment. This section outlines caseworker screening, referral protocols, clinical assessment sequencing, and participation credit rules under California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP) EAS 42-711.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & CLINICAL REFERRALS
• Screening & Identification: Caseworkers must screen WTW participants for behavioral health concerns during orientation, appraisal, and at any subsequent WTW interaction or reassessment. Screening tools evaluate emotional, psychological, or substance-related barriers.
• Voluntary Treatment & Confidentiality: Behavioral health services are strictly voluntary and confidential. Participation in clinical counseling or substance treatment cannot be mandated as a condition of cash aid eligibility.
• Core Hours & Concurrent Activities: Clinical assessment, psychotherapy, psychiatric treatment, and residential or outpatient substance abuse rehabilitation count toward mandatory WTW hourly participation requirements (20, 30, or 35 hours per week) as approved activities.
• Dedicated Service Providers: Services are coordinated directly with County Behavioral Health Services (BHS), contracted clinical clinics, and licensed community mental health centers.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Referral Generation: When a customer expresses interest or displays need, generate an immediate referral via the automated system and issue the Behavioral Health Information Notice.
• Transportation & Child Care: Authorize immediate supportive services, including public transit passes or mileage reimbursement and Stage One Child Care payments, to ensure the participant can attend clinical appointments without hardship.
• Case Narrative & Medical Safeguards: Document the referral in the case narrative without disclosing confidential medical diagnoses or psychotropic medication details. Comply with strict HIPAA and state confidentiality protections.

title: A. Employment Services Exemptions
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-020: WTW EXEMPTIONS
TITLE: A. EMPLOYMENT SERVICES (WTW) EXEMPTIONS

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Under CDSS MPP EAS 42-712, every CalWORKs adult recipient is required to participate in Welfare-to-Work (WTW) employment services unless they qualify for a statutory exemption. This section outlines all statutory exemption categories that excuse an individual from mandatory participation and pause the CalWORKs 60-month time-on-aid clock.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & EXEMPTION CATEGORIES
• Disability / Medical Incapacity: An individual with a documented physical or mental impairment that prevents participation in work or training activities for at least 30 calendar days is exempt upon submission of a physician's certification (CW 61).
• Advanced Age: Individuals who are 60 years of age or older are automatically exempt from WTW participation requirements.
• Care of an Incapacitated Household Member: A caretaker is exempt when substantial, continuous care is required for an ill or incapacitated household member, and no other care provider is available.
• Care of an Infant: A parent or caretaker relative is entitled to an exemption to care for one infant child up to 24 months of age, or an exemption for caring for a child under six months of age.
• Domestic Abuse Waiver: Victims of domestic violence are entitled to a domestic abuse waiver excusing them from WTW participation and stopping the 60-month time limit clock.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Identification & Screening: Screen every client for potential exemptions during intake, annual renewal, and WTW appraisal.
• Time-Limit Stopping: Ensure the exemption code is entered in CalSAWS to pause the state 60-month time-on-aid clock.
• Voluntary Participation: Inform exempt individuals that they have the legal right to volunteer for WTW education and supportive services without losing their exempt status.

title: B. Employment Services Good Cause
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-020: WTW GOOD CAUSE
TITLE: B. EMPLOYMENT SERVICES GOOD CAUSE DETERMINATION

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Good Cause excuses a non-exempt Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participant from participation in assigned work, education, or training activities for a temporary period due to circumstances beyond their control under CDSS MPP EAS 42-713. Establishing good cause protects the participant from financial noncompliance sanctions.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & QUALIFYING REASONS
• Lack of Supportive Services: Good cause is mandatory when the County fails to provide necessary child care, transportation assistance, or required work-related ancillary payments. A participant cannot be penalized for non-participation if child care or transit was unavailable.
• Temporary Illness or Injury: Acute illness of the participant or a dependent child, verified by medical statement or reasonable customer declaration.
• Family Emergency & Crisis: Sudden death of a family member, severe domestic crisis, eviction, or homelessness.
• Breakdown of Transportation: Unexpected breakdown of primary transportation or temporary disruption of public transit services.
• Court Appearances & Legal Mandates: Required attendance at court hearings, custody proceedings, or probation appointments.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Good Cause Interview: When a participant misses scheduled WTW hours, the caseworker must contact them by telephone or written notice to explore good cause before initiating noncompliance.
• Verification Standards: Accept reasonable customer explanations; third-party documentation should only be demanded when the stated reason is questionable.
• Barrier Removal: Immediately resolve the underlying barrier (e.g., re-authorize bus passes or arrange child care) to facilitate re-engagement.

title: A. Employment Services Noncompliance and Sanctions
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-025: COMPLIANCE PROCESS
TITLE: A. WTW NONCOMPLIANCE, CAUSE DETERMINATION, AND SANCTIONS

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
This section establishes County HHSA procedures for addressing failure to participate in mandatory Welfare-to-Work (WTW) activities under CDSS MPP EAS 42-721. The compliance process ensures full due process, requiring the County to explore good cause and offer conciliation before imposing financial sanctions.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & SANCTION PROCESS
• Noncompliance Notice (NA 840): When an individual fails or refuses to participate without pre-established good cause, issue the Cause Determination Notice (NA 840) allowing 20 calendar days to establish good cause or request a conciliation appointment.
• Conciliation Period: A 20-calendar-day conciliation period begins immediately upon notice issuance. The caseworker and participant work together to resolve barriers and draft a compliance plan.
• Curing Noncompliance: A participant cures noncompliance by signing a compliance plan and agreeing to complete the assigned activity for up to 30 calendar days.
• Imposition of Financial Sanction: If the individual fails to respond, fails to establish good cause, or refuses to sign a compliance plan, a financial sanction is imposed. The adult's portion of the cash grant is removed, reducing the family's cash aid. The children's benefits continue.
• Curing a Sanction: A sanction can be cured at any time. When the individual agrees to participate and completes a compliance plan, the sanction is removed and the adult's grant is restored on the first of the following month.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Pre-Sanction Outreach: Attempt home visits, phone calls, and outreach to re-engage the customer before issuing a formal sanction.
• Timely Notice of Action: Issue the 10-day Notice of Action prior to reducing the grant amount.
• Restorative Action: Immediately process compliance documents when the participant agrees to cure.

title: H. Employment Services Grievances
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-030: PARTICIPANT RIGHTS
TITLE: H. EMPLOYMENT SERVICES GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participants have the legal right to file a formal grievance regarding any dispute concerning assigned work activities, supportive service payments, assessments, or caseworker actions under CDSS MPP EAS 42-721.5. This section outlines the internal County dispute resolution and independent hearing processes.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & GRIEVANCE RESOLUTION
• Scope of Grievance: A participant may file a grievance regarding:
  (1) Disagreement with the results of a vocational assessment;
  (2) Assignment to an inappropriate or unsafe work activity;
  (3) Refusal or underpayment of child care, transportation, or ancillary supportive services;
  (4) Inappropriate conciliation or noncompliance determinations.
• Informal Conference: Upon receipt of a grievance, a supervisor must schedule an informal conference with the participant within 10 business days to review the dispute and attempt mutual resolution.
• Formal Grievance Hearing: If the dispute is not resolved informally, the participant is entitled to a formal hearing before an independent County Hearing Officer. The hearing officer issues a binding written decision within 30 days.
• State Fair Hearing Right: Participants maintain the right to appeal any County decision directly to the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) for a formal State Fair Hearing, regardless of whether internal grievance procedures were utilized.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Grievance Intake: Accept written or verbal grievances and forward them to the Appeals and Review unit within 24 hours.
• Aid Paid Pending: If the grievance involves a reduction in supportive services or cash aid and was filed prior to the effective date of notice, aid must be maintained at the current level pending the hearing outcome.
• File Maintenance: Preserve all grievance correspondence and written hearing decisions in the official case record.

title: A. Community Service-Work Experience
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-050: COMMUNITY SERVICE
TITLE: A. COMMUNITY SERVICE AND WORK EXPERIENCE

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Community Service provides structured, unpaid work activities in public agencies or private non-profit organizations to enable CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participants who cannot find unsubsidized employment to gain job skills, work history, and professional references while fulfilling their mandatory hourly participation requirements under CDSS MPP EAS 42-716.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & PLACEMENT RULES
• Maximum Hours Determination (FLSA Rule): Community service hours are strictly calculated according to Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) regulations. The maximum allowable monthly hours cannot exceed the household's monthly CalWORKs grant plus CalFresh allotment divided by the applicable California statutory minimum wage.
• Non-Displacement Protections: Community service participants cannot be placed in positions that result in the displacement of regular employees, fill existing vacant positions, or impair existing collective bargaining agreements.
• Core Participation Credit: Community service qualifies as a core WTW activity fulfilling the 20 or 30-hour weekly core participation requirement for single or two-parent assistance units.
• Supportive Services Guarantee: Participants assigned to community service placements must be provided all necessary supportive services, including child care, transportation, and required work equipment, uniforms, or safety gear.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Placement Agreement: Execute the Community Service Agreement with the approved sponsor organization, specifying daily work schedules, learning objectives, and workplace supervision.
• Monthly Attendance Verification: Collect monthly attendance logs verified and signed by the workplace supervisor by the 5th working day following the participation month.
• Skill Development Review: Evaluate participant progress at 6-month intervals to determine readiness for transition to unsubsidized employment or Expanded Subsidized Employment.

title: A. Expanded Subsidized Employment Program
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-150: SUBSIDIZED EMPLOYMENT
TITLE: A. EXPANDED SUBSIDIZED EMPLOYMENT (ESE) PROGRAM

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
The Expanded Subsidized Employment (ESE) program provides wage subsidies to public, non-profit, or private-sector employers to create immediate paid employment opportunities for CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participants, facilitating hands-on work experience, skill acquisition, and permanent job retention under California Welfare and Institutions Code Section 11322.63.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & WAGE SUBSIDIES
• Wage Subsidies: San Diego County HHSA provides subsidies covering a percentage of the participant's gross wages and associated payroll taxes for up to 6 months, with optional extension up to 12 months when retention criteria are demonstrated.
• Real Wages & Benefits: ESE participants are genuine employees of the hiring organization and receive the prevailing wage (at or above statutory minimum wage) along with all workplace protections, workers' compensation, and applicable employment benefits.
• CalWORKs Grant Budgeting: Because ESE wages are earned income, the CalWORKs assistance unit benefits from the statutory $450 earned income disregard plus 50% disregard on remaining wages, allowing families to receive a partial cash grant while working.
• Core Work Participation: All paid hours in ESE count 100% toward federal and state core work participation rate requirements.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Employer Master Agreement: Confirm execution of the County ESE Master Employer Agreement establishing wage reimbursement schedules and employer commitment to retain the employee upon subsidy conclusion.
• Payroll Tracking: Verify monthly earnings through electronic payroll records or paystubs, recalculating the family's cash grant accordingly.
• Transition to Unsubsidized Work: Coordinate job coaching and supportive services during months 4 through 6 to facilitate seamless retention as a permanent, unsubsidized employee.

title: B. Expanded Work Experience Program
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-150: WORK EXPERIENCE
TITLE: B. EXPANDED WORK EXPERIENCE (EWE) PROGRAM

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
The Expanded Work Experience (EWE) program provides structured, goal-oriented workplace training in public, private, or non-profit settings for CalWORKs Welfare-to-Work (WTW) participants who need hands-on occupational experience, updated workplace references, and professional networking under CDSS MPP EAS 42-716.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & WORKPLACE TRAINING
• Educational & Skill Objectives: EWE placements are customized to match the participant's assessment findings and career goals. Placements emphasize real-world skill development in administrative, medical, technical, culinary, or trade occupations.
• Hour Limitations & FLSA Protection: The hours assigned cannot exceed the household's monthly cash and food assistance divided by the state minimum wage.
• Supervision & Mentorship: Sponsoring employers assign a workplace mentor to provide daily training, performance feedback, and monthly skill evaluations.
• Supportive Services: The County provides full supportive service coverage, including child care, transportation passes, professional clothing allowances, and specialized work tools.
• Direct Path to Unsubsidized Work: EWE placements are scheduled for 3 to 6 months with the primary objective of converting the placement into permanent unsubsidized employment with the host employer.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Training Agreement: Execute the tripartite EWE agreement between the client, host employer, and County WTW coordinator.
• Monthly Time Logs: Review monthly timesheets and supervisor evaluations verifying hours and workplace competency progress.
• Employment Transition: Re-evaluate the placement at 90 days to identify opportunities for permanent hire or transition to Expanded Subsidized Employment.

title: A. Wrap Around
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-160: SPECIAL SERVICES
TITLE: A. WRAP AROUND INTENSIVE CASE MANAGEMENT

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Wrap Around is an intensive, family-centered, strengths-based case management model designed to stabilize multi-barrier CalWORKs families facing complex challenges, including imminent homelessness, domestic violence, severe health issues, child welfare involvement, or persistent welfare-to-work non-participation under County HHSA specialized supportive service directives.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & SERVICE TEAMS
• Family Team Conferencing: The Wrap Around process brings together the family, their assigned CalWORKs caseworker, behavioral health clinicians, housing specialists, child welfare social workers, and natural community supports to create a single, unified Family Plan.
• Flexible Funding: Wrap Around provides individualized, flexible supportive service expenditures to remove immediate crises (such as rental arrears, utility shutoffs, vehicle repairs, or specialized equipment) that threaten family stability.
• Clock-Stopping & Good Cause: When participating in intensive Wrap Around family stabilization, participants are granted Good Cause exemptions or WTW barrier removal credit, pausing the 60-month time-on-aid clock where appropriate under EAS 42-713.
• Continuous Coordination: Regular multidisciplinary team meetings are conducted bi-weekly or monthly to review family goals, track progress, and adjust service delivery.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Comprehensive Screening: Refer cases with severe, layered barriers to the specialized Wrap Around coordination unit.
• Individualized Stabilization Plan: Document the multidisciplinary action steps in the CalSAWS case narrative, ensuring all partner agencies share synchronized milestones.
• Re-engagement Transition: As family stability is achieved, systematically transition participants back into standard core Welfare-to-Work education, training, or employment activities.

title: CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR)
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-170: QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
TITLE: CALWORKS OUTCOMES AND ACCOUNTABILITY REVIEW (CAL-OAR)

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
The CalWORKs Outcomes and Accountability Review (Cal-OAR) is California's statewide continuous quality improvement and performance assessment system established under Welfare and Institutions Code Section 11523. Cal-OAR shifts the CalWORKs program evaluation from narrow process compliance to substantive family self-sufficiency, educational attainment, and long-term child and family well-being.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & PERFORMANCE MEASURES
• Core Evaluation Components: Cal-OAR operates on a three-year continuous quality improvement cycle consisting of:
  (1) Performance Measures: Standardized data metrics tracking employment entries, earnings progression, credential attainment, supportive service utilization, and sanction cure rates;
  (2) County Self-Assessment (CSA): A comprehensive multi-year evaluation of local county operational strengths, service gaps, and customer voice;
  (3) System Improvement Plan (SIP): An actionable strategic roadmap setting quantitative targets and procedural enhancements over a three-year period.
• Family-Centered Focus: Cal-OAR metrics evaluate holistic family stability, housing retention, and child care access rather than solely mechanical hourly participation.
• Public Reporting: San Diego County submits all Cal-OAR performance data and SIP updates directly to the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) for statewide publication.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Data Integrity: Caseworkers must accurately log all WTW component activities, supportive services payments, and employment entries in CalSAWS to ensure reliable state data extraction.
• Continuous Engagement: Implement peer review and quality improvement feedback to reduce participant dropouts and enhance employment outcomes.

title: A. Refugee Employment Services
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 10-200: REFUGEE SERVICES
TITLE: A. REFUGEE EMPLOYMENT SERVICES (RES)

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
Refugee Employment Services (RES) provides culturally and linguistically sensitive employment, training, and case management services to refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Amerasians, and certified victims of human trafficking receiving CalWORKs under federal Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) guidelines and CDSS MPP Chapter 69-200.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & SERVICE COMPONENTS
• Target Population: Eligible noncitizens within their first 60 months in the United States who receive CalWORKs or Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA).
• Specialized Components: Services include:
  (1) English as a Second Language (ESL) combined with vocational skills training;
  (2) On-the-job training and subsidized employment;
  (3) Culturally tailored job placement, career counseling, and employer networking;
  (4) Bilingual case management and translation assistance for workplace integration.
• Core Participation Alignment: All hours spent in approved RES language acquisition, skill training, and job search count 100% toward CalWORKs mandatory weekly participation requirements.
• Enhanced Supportive Services: Participants receive transportation assistance, child care reimbursements, and specialized interpretation services for all appointments.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Status Verification: Verify eligible immigration status via Form I-94, permanent resident card (Form I-551), or ORR certification letter.
• Referral to Contracted RES Providers: Route eligible refugee participants to designated County-contracted refugee employment service agencies within 5 working days of granting cash aid.
• Synchronized Case Monitoring: Coordinate monthly participation hours with the RES service provider to ensure timely verification in CalSAWS.

content: 15-00 0 H. CAL-LEARN GOOD CAUSE D Table o f Contents The Cal -Learn Good Cause Determi nation sectio n include s t h e followi ng informatio n: Topi c s Good Cau se Request and Cri t e ria Requ ired Actions Good Ca u se Request and Criteria Teen parents may request a good cause de t e rmination f o r failure to demon st ra t e adeq uate prog ress or for late submittal of report cards or progress reports. Case Manag ers are requ ired t o evalu ate go od cau se util izing the fol lowing criteria: Process Criteria Good Cau se Requ est Requ ests for go od cause Are made by the teen p arent to t he case manager; May be mad e pri or to a repo rt card or du ring the 10-da y reason able effort pe riod under C LPG Section 15-0 00 F. Cal-L earn Case Man agement Services; The case man ager is requ ired to initiate a good cause determin ation when a tee n parent requests such a revi ew. Good Case Evalua t i on Evalua t i on of good cause for failure t o make adeq uate progre ss i s c onsidered w hen: The event was be yond the teen paren t  s con t ro l; The event substantia lly deprived the teen pare nt of the abil ity to make a dequate pro gress in school ; and Home study or othe r speci al arrangemen t s could not be made w ith t he school. Good Cau se Reaso ns Reaso ns f o r g ood cause incl ude, but are not limited to: The tee n parent was/had o Temporari ly ill or incap acitated. o Requ ired to appea r in a court proceedin g or is incarce rated. o Unab le to travel to an activity due to incl ement w eather or other act(s) of nature o Breakdo wn in transportatio n arrang ements wi t h no ready acce ss to al t e rnate transportation. o Refused to accept major medical service s even if the refusal pre cluded pa rt i cipation in the pro gram. o Met any of the exemption or d eferral criteria as specifie d in CLPG Section 15-000 C. Cal-L earn Program Eli gibili t y an d Participation R equiremen t s . o Experie ncing a family crisis or change of individ ual or family circumstance s, such as death or illne ss of a spouse , paren t , or chi ld, w hich requires the t ee ns immedi ate att e ntion. The t e ens schoo l program b reaks for the summer a nd no report card or pro gress report is given f or that peri od. A bre akdown or in t e rruption of child care arr angements occurred , wh ich includ e: o Licen sed o r exe mpt chil d ca re w as no t reason ably avail able d uring the teen pare nts hours of school, inclu ding commutin g t i me; o Reaso nably ava ilable child ca re includ es having at least two choi ces of child care arrange ments, which do not requi re: Addin g more than on e-half hou r t o t h e commuting time each wa y; or The child to transfer to a differen t scho ol. o Chil d care was ne eded for a chil d who did not meet one condi t i on in each of the t w o sections under CLPG Section 1 5-000 E. Cal-L earn Supportive Services and therefore wa s n ot e ligibl e f or C al-Learn pa id child care ; o Suitabl e sp ecial nee ds ch ild care was not reason ably avail able for children wi t h disa bilities, chroni c il lnesses, or other speci al needs. At the discretion of the Cal-L earn Liaison, any su bstantial and compelli ng reaso ns other t h an those specified in this section. Required Actions At the time a teen pare nt requests good cau se determinatio n, t he responsib le staff i s req uired to complete the follow ing actions to approve or den y go od cause for t h e teen s fail ure t o demo nstrate ad equate progress or late submittal of report cards or prog ress reports: Responsible Staff Action Case Manag er 1. Determin e if good cause exists base d on the re asons listed ab ove; 2. Revie w t h e events on which the teen based the goo d cause req uest; o If the teen pa rent had a break in particip ation as describ ed in CLPG Section 15-000 F. Cal-Le arn Case Manag ement Servi ces duri ng the report card perio d, the g ood cause revie w shall incl ude the impact t h e break had o n the tee ns abi lity to make adeq uate progress. 3. Obtain substan t i ating documen t a t i on; 4. Compl ete and submit the CL Co mpliance Tracking T oo l (27-36 0) t o the C al-Learn Li aison; 5. Issue a no t i ce if no good cause is de t e rmined to the teen paren t and the head of the AU no later t ha n 1 5 workin g days after a go od cause de t e rmination w as reque st e d. The C al-Learn Notice of No Good Ca use Determin ation (CL-9) is required to be sent to the t e en paren t and the head of the AU whe n the teen has bee n found to be withou t good cause for faili ng or refusing to comply wi t h prog ram requiremen t s. The CL-9 inclu des an appoin t me nt date for t he teen to discuss the probl em; 6. If go od ca use i s not found for f ai lure or ref u sal t o comply w ith program req uirements on the p art of the teen pa rent, t he case manag er is requi red to inform the teen pare nt and head of the AU o f the co nsequence s of not pa rt i cipating i n the Cal -Learn Prog ram. Should t he teen parent need f urthe r assistan ce, the case man ager is require d to provi de t he teen pa rent w ith the teleph one number and add ress o f the Lega l Ai d Society. Cal-L earn Liai son 1. Review the submitted 27-360 the case manag ers recommen dation, documentation and CalWIN entries to determine i f the teen pa rent has good cause ; 2. Requ est addition al informatio n from the case manager, if neede d; 3. Approve o r d eny t h e good cause req uest; a nd 4. Notify the case ma nager o f the goo d cause determin ation via the 27-3 60.

Example : A teen s CalWORKs case i s discontinu ed on Octobe r 30, 2012 . Treatment of Bonuse s a nd Sanction s In Other Programs The H SS shall not incl ude a Cal-Le arn bon us or san ct i on in t h e calcu lation of an overpaymen t adjustment, a homel ess a ssistance payment, or a reduced inco me suppl ement.

title: B. Customer Request for Information
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 40-100: APPLICATION & INTERVIEW
TITLE: B. CUSTOMER REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND VERIFICATION

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
This section establishes County HHSA procedures for requesting verifications from CalWORKs applicants and recipients. In accordance with CDSS MPP EAS 40-126 and state due process protections, caseworkers must clearly notify customers of required documents, provide adequate response timeframes, and assist families in securing mandatory evidence before taking any adverse eligibility action.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & THE CW 2200 PROCESS
• Mandatory Written Form: All requests for information must be made in writing using the official County Request for Verification form (CW 2200). Verbal requests alone are legally insufficient to support a case denial or discontinuance.
• 10-Day Response Standard: Customers must be given a minimum of 10 calendar days from the mailing date of the CW 2200 to provide requested verifications. If the 10th day falls on a weekend or county holiday, the deadline extends to the next business day.
• Mandatory County Assistance: The caseworker must assist the customer in securing verifications when the customer indicates difficulty, lacks financial resources to pay document fees, or is unable to obtain records from third parties (e.g., employers, banks, landlords).
• Prohibition on Unnecessary Verification: Caseworkers are strictly prohibited from demanding verifications of eligibility factors that are not questionable, already documented in the case record, or available through electronic state data systems (e.g., MEDS, IEVS, EDD).

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Clear Checklist Itemization: On the CW 2200, clearly specify the exact document needed, why it is required, and the due date.
• Extension of Time: Grant extensions of time whenever the customer makes a good-faith effort to obtain the records before the deadline.

sections.heading: B. Customer Request for Information
sections.text:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 40-100: APPLICATION & INTERVIEW
TITLE: B. CUSTOMER REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND VERIFICATION

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
This section establishes County HHSA procedures for requesting verifications from CalWORKs applicants and recipients. In accordance with CDSS MPP EAS 40-126 and state due process protections, caseworkers must clearly notify customers of required documents, provide adequate response timeframes, and assist families in securing mandatory evidence before taking any adverse eligibility action.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & THE CW 2200 PROCESS
• Mandatory Written Form: All requests for information must be made in writing using the official County Request for Verification form (CW 2200). Verbal requests alone are legally insufficient to support a case denial or discontinuance.
• 10-Day Response Standard: Customers must be given a minimum of 10 calendar days from the mailing date of the CW 2200 to provide requested verifications. If the 10th day falls on a weekend or county holiday, the deadline extends to the next business day.
• Mandatory County Assistance: The caseworker must assist the customer in securing verifications when the customer indicates difficulty, lacks financial resources to pay document fees, or is unable to obtain records from third parties (e.g., employers, banks, landlords).
• Prohibition on Unnecessary Verification: Caseworkers are strictly prohibited from demanding verifications of eligibility factors that are not questionable, already documented in the case record, or available through electronic state data systems (e.g., MEDS, IEVS, EDD).

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Clear Checklist Itemization: On the CW 2200, clearly specify the exact document needed, why it is required, and the due date.
• Extension of Time: Grant extensions of time whenever the customer makes a good-faith effort to obtain the records before the deadline.
• Denial or Discontinuance Safeguards: Do not deny an application for failure to provide information until the full 10-day period has elapsed and the case record documents that the County offered and provided all required assistance.

content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page Extended CalWORKs for Non-Min or Dependents 40-18 3.B 1 of 3 Revision Date: Novemb er 29, 2016 Back g r o und: Assembly Bi ll 12 requ ires that child ren who a re under the re sponsibi lity of the Coun t y C hild Welfare Se rvices (CWS) or Prob ation Department at ag e 18 may remain in foster ca re as non-mi nor d epende nts (NMDs) until age 21 u nder the state-funded Extende d F o st e r C are (EF C ) Pro gram. ACL 11-6 1 Poli c y: 40-18 3.B.1 CalWO R Ks Eli gibili ty C riteria CalWORKs NMD s mu st : 1. L ive with an appro ved relative careg iver who is not elig ible for federal o r state foster care payme nts 2. Me et EFC prog ram requireme nts a s d etermined by their CWS Social Worke r. A NMD must: A. Me et a t le ast on e of the fol lowing el igibil ity co nditions: 1. Be e nrolled in , an d working toward s, comp leting high sch ool or an equi valent progra m 2. Be enro lled in a p ost-secondary or vocational school at least half-time, o r be enrol led f o r the next avail able term 3. Be p articipating i n a program o r a ct i vity t h at p romotes employme nt or removes barrie rs t o emplo yment 4. Be e mployed at least 80 hou rs p er mo nth 5. Be incapabl e of participa t i ng in scho ol or empl oyment due to a documented p hysical, mental , o r emotion al conditio n B. Ag ree and adhe re to the Mutual Agreemen t for EFC. If the NMD s volun t a rily exi t and later re-e nter foster care, the NMD must adhe re to a Voluntary Re-Entry Agreeme nt for EFC ra t h er than a Mutual Agreeme nt. ACL 12-1 2 C. T h e CWS Social Worker w ill provide a n ew Si x-Month Ce rt i f i cation of EFC e very six months t o docume nt t h e NMDs contin uing eli gibili t y. This docu mentation must be recei ved in the first month of the new certifica t i on period to preve nt C alWORKs discontinu ance. ACL 11-7 8 Other hou sehold me mbers, such as the relative ca regiver o r t h e NMDs minor chil d(ren), are n ot eligib le to extende d CalWORKs. A NMD may receive C alWORKs while resi ding outside o f Ca lifornia for the follow ing reason s: The N MD is placed wi t h a n a pproved rel at i ve who lives in a nother county or state; or The a pproved rela t i ve with whom the NMD is curre nt l y p laced moves to anothe r co unty or st a t e . ACL 11-7 8 and 12-27 The BDA for N MDs wh o re-enter EFC is the date of pl acement wi t h the approved relative caregive r; provide d the Volun t a ry Re -Entry Agre ement f o r EFC is signe d by the C W S Socia l Worke r a nd all eligi bility criteria are met. ACL 12-2 7 40-18 3.B.5 Payment and Iss u a n c e Metho d The extend ed CalWORKs pa yment amount is e qual to the Ma ximum Aid Paymen t (MAP) for a non-exempt Assistance Unit (AU) of o ne. The payme nt may be issu ed to the N MD via di rect deposit o r Electronic Be nefit Transfer (EBT). ACL 11-7 8 and 12-27 40-18 3.B.6 O v erpayments Coll ection f o r extend ed C alWORKs o verpayment claims may o nly o ccur via gran t reductio n wh ile t h e NMD is actively re ceiving extend ed CalWORKs or if the NMD la t e r re ceives CalWORKs for hi s/ he r own minor child (ren) due to the Hartley v. Lightbo urne settlement. title: D. CalWORKs Reunification Families
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) CalWORKs Program Guide Number Page CalWORKs Family Reunification Program 40-18 3.D 1 of 2 Revision Date: August 1, 2018 Back g r o und: CalWORKs recipi ents, wh ose eligib ility e nds because their childre n w ere re moved from the hom e by Chi ld Welfare Se rvices (CWS), may co ntinue to participate i n Welfare-to-Work (W TW) activi t i es, and re ceive suppo rt i ve services, if the C W S Soci al Worker or Juvenil e C ourt deem services nece ssary t o re unify t h e f a mily. Purpose: The purp ose of this revisi on is to notify staff that Family Re unification (F R ) f a milies may re ceive Temporary Homel ess Assistance (THA) bene f i t s, if otherw ise eligi ble, if the county determin es that T H A is necessary for reuni f i cation to occur. Poli c y: The C W S Social Worke r, or the cou rt , ma y authorize FR services f o r up to 1 80 days from t h e date the childre n are remo ved from t h e assistance un it (AU ). The co urt may also grant the pa rent a good cau se extension to the 180-d ay period. Eligi bility to FR Services To receive FR service s, al l o f the foll owing cond itions must be met: A C W S Social Worker, o r t h e court, have determined t h at t h e provisi on of FR service s is necessa ry f o r family reun ification The ch ild(ren) have b een removed from the hom e a nd placed i n out-of-home care The AU h ad been recei ving CalWORKs when the ch ild(ren) wa s/ w ere removed Note: SSI recipie nts, u ndocumented n oncitizens, or timed -out parents are ine ligibl e t o F R se rvices because they were no t el igible to recei ve CalWORKs benefits When the re are mu ltiple ch ildren i n the AU , but not al l the chi ldren a re removed, a nd the AU becomes inelig ible to CalWORKs due t o i ncome, the paren t (s) may b e eligib le to F R services if there is a cour t -or dered reuni f i cation plan for the chi ld(ren) who we re removed. THA Effective Janua ry 1 , 2 018, FR cases that are experi encing ho melessness may b e eligib le for T H A benefits, if the county determi nes these benefits are nece ssary f o r re unification a nd t h e f a mily is otherwise e ligibl e. title: A. Assistance Unit
content:
COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AGENCY
CALWORKS PROGRAM GUIDE — SECTION 44-200: ASSISTANCE UNIT COMPOSITION
TITLE: A. THE ASSISTANCE UNIT (AU) AND MANDATORY MEMBERS

1. POLICY BACKGROUND & PURPOSE
The Assistance Unit (AU) is the group of persons within a household who are eligible to receive CalWORKs cash assistance together. This section details mandatory AU inclusion rules, optional member choices, excluded individuals, and the relationship between the AU and the Family Budget Unit (FBU) under CDSS MPP EAS 44-205.

2. DETAILED REGULATORY STANDARDS & AU COMPOSITION
• Mandatory Inclusion Rules: The following individuals living in the same home must be included in the AU if eligible:
  (1) The eligible child(ren);
  (2) The natural or adoptive parents of the child(ren);
  (3) All eligible full, half, or adoptive siblings of the child(ren).
• Excluded Persons: Individuals who cannot be included in the AU include:
  (1) Undocumented noncitizens (ineligible immigrants);
  (2) Individuals receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI/SSP);
  (3) Children receiving Kin-GAP, Foster Care, or Adoption Assistance;
  (4) Individuals serving a CalWORKs intentional program violation (IPV) disqualification or felony fleeing felon sanction.
• Caretaker Relative Option: Non-parent caretaker relatives (such as grandparents, aunts, or uncles) with physical custody of an eligible child may choose to be included in the AU with the child or receive aid on behalf of the child only (child-only case).
• Senior Parent / Minor Parent Budgeting: When a minor parent resides with their own parents (senior parents), senior parent income deeming rules apply under EAS 44-133 unless the minor parent is legally emancipated.

3. CASEWORKER OPERATING PROCEDURES & VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
• Family Tree Mapping: Document household relationships, parental lineage, and sibling connections during the intake interview.
• Mandatory Member Screening: Ensure all mandatory siblings and parents residing in the home are added to the application.
• Non-Parent Choice: Formally document the caretaker relative's choice regarding whether they wish to be included in the cash grant or receive child-only assistance.
