title: Section 10 - Pickle Benefits
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Pickle Special Notice Report (503 Lead Fil e R ep ort ) 05.10.01 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/20 19 Back g r o und: The Lynch v. Rank cou rt ord er mandates specific req uirements for both the DHC S an d County of San Dieg o, H ealth and Human Se rvices Agency related to iden t i f i cation, maintenan ce o f li st s, annu al notificatio n and review of ind ividual s p otentially eli gible to Pickle b enefits. In additio n t o the re f o rmatt i ng, t hi s sect i on has been revi sed for clarification . Poli c y: A. Actions Taken SSA Actions Durin g the month of December each year, the Social Secu rity Administratio n (SSA) notifies D HCS of all SSI/SSP reci pients schedule d for discon t i nuance as a re sult of the Cost o f Livin g Ad justment (COLA). These bene f i ciaries must be evaluated for no Share of Cost (SOC) Medi-Ca l, through the Pickle Amen dment. DHC S Action s DHC S wil l i nitiate extended Medi-C al benefits f or all perso ns on the report provid ed b y SSA by placi ng these benefici aries in Crai g v. Bon t a ai d codes; 1E aged, 2E blin d or 6E disable d. Durin g t h e last two w eeks of D ecember, DHCS sends the Pickle Amen dment Notice (Pickle Annu al Stuffer) to Med i-Cal beneficia ries on the SSA di scontinuan ce report. The notice advises i ndividu als that the y may be el igible to Me di-Cal benefits without a share of co st (SOC) un der the Pickle Amendme nt a nd t o contact the ir county social service s of fice t o ap ply. Coun t y Action s By the first or second week of Janu ary, DHC S sends the Pickl e Spe cial N otice (SN ) report of all indi viduals discontin ued f rom SSI/SSP due to the Title II COLA to t he coun t y. T h ese be neficiarie s are also place d on the countys Exception Eligib les rep ort and wil l rema in o n the report until a Pi ckle Amendme nt re view or an ABD Medi -Cal Linka ge determinatio n has been compl eted. Procedures: B. Review Procedures A Pickle Amendment eva luation is mandatory for every indi vidual o n the Pickle SN report. An indi vidual may al so contact t he county t o re quest a Pickle evalu ation. Medi-C al programs un der this Amendmen t are: Pickle Disab led Adult Chi ldren (DAC) Disab led Widow(e r) (D W ) It is important to screen for po t e ntial elig ibility for all t hr ee programs. If the indi vidual i s e ligibl e t o Pickle, DAC or DW at the same time, grant the DAC program first . When the individ ual d oesnt me et the criteria for Pickle , D A C , or D W , review f or othe r Medi-Cal pro gram eligi bility. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Pickle Special Notice Report (503 Lead Fil e R ep ort ) 05.10.01 2 of 2 C. Pickle Amendment Rev i e w A Pickle Amen dment eligi bility review i s re quired: At initial ap plication At redetermina t i on In the month after a Social Secu rity T i t l e I I COLA Upon r equest Follow ing a break in a id The on ly exceptio ns are tho se indivi duals d iscontinue d by SSA du e to dea t h or are incarcerated in a correction al facility. Program Impacts: The report is loa ded into Share Point by Automation for processi ng. Refer ences: ACWDL 02-0 5, 1 0-02 Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be revie wed for continua nce by 12/31/2022 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne , Di rector Eligi bility Operation County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Pickle Amendment Notice (Pickle Annual S t u ffe r) 05.10.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: 12/01/20 19 Back g r o und: In Decembe r o f ea ch year, DHCS mails Pickl e Annual Stuffer notices to active Medi -Cal bene f i ciaries in aid c odes 14, 17, 24, 64, and 67 who : Curren t l y receive Title II Retirement, Survivors an d Disabili t y Insura nce Social Secu rity Benefits Have be en discontin ued from the SSI /SSP prog ram in the last three years Were determin ed ineli gible duri ng the Pickle screen ing process the previ ous year The Pi ckle stuffer no t i ce informs t he se bene f i ciaries t o contact the county if they would like t o apply for zero SOC Medi-Ca l t h rough the Pickle Ame ndment. This section ha s b een reformatted and proce dures moved to Processi ng Guide 29. Poli c y: The be neficiarie s who re ceive the Pickle Ann ual Stuffer are aged, bl ind, and disable d and must be evalu ated f o r Med i-Cal elig ibility through the Pickle amen dment. Whe n d etermined inel igible , eval uate for all other ABD l inked Medi-C al Programs. A. Annual P ick l e A mendment Reviews By terms of the Lynch v. Rank court orde r, the Pickle Amendmen t reviews must be co mpleted d uring the mo nths of Jan uary throug h March of each ye ar. Each potentiall y eligi ble Pi ckle ind ividual must receive a P i ckle Medi-Ca l notice from DHCS for three conse cutive years. O ne y e ar of i neligi bles will be purg ed each year. Persons on the Pickle SN report must have their eligib ility to Pi ckle reevaluated ea ch yea r a t the time of the an nual Title I I C O LA. T h e indivi duals name wil l appea r on the Pickl e SN repo rt when a Pickle determin ation was not completed in the previou s yea r or the indi vidual was not eligi ble for Pi ckle through the Pi ckle Amendmen t for the previo us year. The avenu es in which the staff are notified to proce ss individu als on the Pickle SN rep ort a re: 1) The Pickle SN rep ort is uploade d t o Sh are Point by Automation 2) Individ ual bring s the ir Pickle amend ment notice in to the FRC 3) Individ ual calls Access wi t h q uestions abou t the Pickl e amendmen t notice Procedures: Screen the individ ual f or potentia l Pickl e el igibil ity and determin e if the b eneficiary has an active county Medi -Cal case. Follow the pro cedures outlin ed in Processin g G ui de 29. When t h e Pickle determina t i on is complete. Submi t a HH SA 14-28 MEDS On-Line Reque st , checking the  Remove Pi ckle Indi cator box. T h is remove s the i ndividu als name from the Pickle SN repo rt for the next year. Bonta court o rder mandates indivi duals discon t i nued from SS I/SSP continue to receive full scope, zero SOC Medi-C al u ntil a n el igibil ity determi nation is comp leted. Ba sic Med i-Cal eligi bility requi rements addresse d in this section cover onl y tho se eligibi lity requireme nts tha t are d iff e rent f or Pickle el igible i ndividu als and must be follow ed when eval uating the Pickle p rogram. Include d with the reformatting, this sectio n has been revi sed to provide clarifications to the Pickl e progra m. Poli c y: A. Pickle Elig ibility Criteria An indi vidual must meet all of t h e f o llowin g criteria to be eligi ble to Pickle: Curren t l y receiving Social Security II benefi t s Recei ved Social Secu rity Title II and Supp lemental Secu rity Inco me (SSI ) an d/or St ate Suppl ementary Payment (SSP) benefits simul t a neously in an y month after April 19 77 Discon t i nued from SSI/SSP a f ter Apri l 1977 Recei ved a Social Secu rity Title II Cost-of-Livi ng Adjustment (COLA) since be ing discontin ued from SSI/ SSP and woul d be entitled to recei ve SSI /SSP ben efits i f the COLA was di sregarded B. Pickle Handboo k The DHCS issued Pickle Han dbook sections, referenced in Desk Aid 92, include informatio n a nd instruction s necessary to d etermine Pickl e eligi bility an d comply w ith the Crai g v. Bonta and Lynch v. Rank cou rt ord ers. C. Worksheets and Notice Of Action (NOA) Re min der s A NOA is required w hen appro ving or discontin uing Pickle , DAC , an d DW be nefits If a N O A do es not generate, a manua l NOA m u s t b e used and saved i n t he case file The Pickle Amen dment workshee t s are i n t he E l ectronic Forms Reposi t o ry (EFR) an d on the DHC S forms web site, the N O As are l ocated on the MEDS Homep age EFR/DHCS Website DHC S 70 19 Financi al Eligib ility Worksheet (Pickle Ch ild) DHC S 70 20 Screeni ng Worksheet DHC S 70 21 Financi al Eligib ility Worksheet DHC S 70 29 Pickle D isregard Comp utation DHC S 70 37 Pickle R esources Worksheet DHC S 70 44 Statement of Living Arra ngements DHC S 70 75 Pickle N eeds Test MC 210B Suppl emental to Statement of Fact s (Pi ckle) County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Pickle Program 05.10.03 2 of 3 MEDS Homep age DHC S 70 26 Deni al/Discontin uance (Pickle/DAC ) DHC S 70 27 Pickle/DAC A p proval D. Scree n ing Process The steps belo w are followe d when eval uating for Pickle, DAC, and DW: Step 1 Screen in dividua ls for Age , Bli ndness, or Disab ility Step 2 Identify receip t of Socia l Security Title II in come Step 3 Revie w MEDS Pickle Tickler Field Step 4 Revie w Program Specific C riteria Step 5 Determin e eligib ility Step 6 Notices of Action an d Case Narrative s E. Pickle Amendment Property Rules The Property rule s used for Pickle, DAC, and DW are based o n SSI rul es. The treatmen t of prope rt y is very simil ar to tradi t i onal Medi -Cal with a few differen ces. The di f fere nces includ e: Individ uals cannot spend down excess property to become eli gible wi t h in the month Property Limi t s o Pickle C ouple $3,00 0 o Pickle Indi vidual $2 , 0 00 o Pickle C hild  Allow t he property limit for his/her pare nts of $3,00 0 and then allo w t h e prope rt y li mit for an i ndividu al of $2,000 DHC S 70 37 form may be used to evalua t e the Pi ckle indivi duals prop erty. The table be low shows de f i nitions of certain items of prope rt y. These items are excl uded from the prope rt y rese rve, re gardless of their valu e. Term Definition Examples House hold Goods Items of perso nal property, found in or near the ho me t h at are used on a regu lar basis; a nd items n eeded by the house holder for mainten ance, use and occupa ncy of the p remises as a home. Furniture, app liances, ele ct ro nic equi pment, personal comp uters, televisi on sets, ca rpets, co oking and eating u t e nsils, and dishe s. Persona l Effects Items of pe rsonal property ordi narily worn or carrie d by the indivi dual and art i cles otherwi se having an intimate rel ation to the indi vidual. Clothi ng, personal j ewelry, weddi ng and en gagement ring s, bo oks, mu sical instrumen t s, items of cultural o r relig ious signi f i cance, prosthetic device s, an d wheelcha irs. Items acqui red or h eld be cause of thei r value or as an investment a re not con sidered househol d good s o r p ersonal effects for purposes of this exclu sion. Items of Unusual V a l ue There is no pro perty limit for items of u nusual valu e. Procedures: G. Pickle Program Income The income computatio n for Pickle, DAC, and DW varie s for each program. T he Pickl e D isregard Compu t a t i on determines the dollar amoun t to be disregarde d from the Social Security Title I I benefit amoun t du e to the C O LA. See Processi ng Guide 29 for Pickle pro cedures. content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Adoptio n Assista n c e Payments (AAP), Foster Care , K i nship- Guardian A ssistance Program (KinGAP), and U n a ccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 1 of 4 Revision Date: Septembe r 1 , 20 22 Back g r o und: Chil dren w ho have been adopted f ro m foster care, placed in foster car e supervi sion, or unacco mpanied refuge e mino rs, may be eligibl e for Medi-Ca l. This section provides poli cies to determin e Medi-Cal e ligibi lity f o r the se children. Purpose: This section is up dated t o provid e cla rification regardin g ou t of state non-Title IV-E Foster Care place ments in Californ ia (CA). Poli c y: Basic Cri t er ia: To receive Med i-Cal und er any aid code chi ldren must meet the follow ing basic Medi -Cal criteria: 1. Meet institutio nal status require ments (Article 6 and Med i-Cal Eli gibili t y Proce dures Manua l (MEPM) 6D). Chil dren p laced at Nap a State Hospital (a p ublic mental institution under W e lfare an d Institutions Cod e (WI C ) Se ct i ons 601 and 300) are und er medical ca re, and not custodia l care and may be e ligibl e f or Med i-Cal. Custodi al care mea ns maintena nce provide d by a psychi atric institution to i ndividua ls whose condi t i on does not warran t med ical treatment. Medica l treatment includ es psychotherapy, cou nseling , reh abilitatio n t ra ining, or other forms of medica l t r eatment. 2. Not be under a pe nal hold. Be cause of the complexity of the pena l system and the ma ny types of pena l ho lds ce rt a in cl arifications are addressed bel ow. They are not a ll i nclusive and variation s must be clarifie d on an indi vidual ba sis. Hold Type Clarification Unde r A r rest Chil dren, who have comm itt ed crimes, and who are de t a ined and admitted to hosp itals or held in Juve nile Hal l (detained un der WI C Section 60 2) prior to and/or after a detention o rder being si gned, are unde r a rrest. Med ical treatment involvi ng minor chil dren require s legal consen t of eithe r the p arent/guardia n or some other agen cy or indi vidual wh o has authority to give such con sent. A la w enforcement agen cy ca nnot obtain such au t h ority without one of the followi ng: Placin g t h e child und er arrest The paren t s formal ly surrenderi ng their authority to the law enforceme nt a gency Court action . Hold Pe nding He aring, Arraign ment, Tria l, o r Sentenci ng Chil dren relea sed on bail are not considered h eld unle ss b ail is revoked . County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Adoptio n Assista n c e Payments (AAP), Foster Care , K i nship- Guardian A ssistance Program (KinGAP), and U n a ccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 2 of 4 Serving a Se ntence Chil dren who are p laced on paro le or probatio n pursuant to a dispo sitional ord er under WIC Section 602 are no t con sidered to be unde r a p enal hold and may be elig ible to Medi-Ca l. T he y may be in Juveni le Hall aw aiting place ment in a Foster Care or group ho me or place d in a youth service prog ram (for example, Rite of Passage or Boys Repu blic). Chil dren sentence d t o serve t erm s un der the Californ ia Youth Authority or senten ced to specific time to be spent in Hon or Camps are und er a penal hol d and inel igible to Medi -Cal. Chil dren sentence d t o a term of incarce ration who are temp orarily place d in a Foster Home pend ing availa ble space in the de t e ntion center are i neligib le to Medi-Cal . Placeme nt i n Mental Institution Und er a Pre- Trial or Pre-Sen t e ncing Observation Orde r o r Who Are Sentence d t o Such an Institution Chil dren place d at C amarillo or othe r S tate H ospitals must be evalu ated to determine if they are still un der a penal ho ld (ineli gible) or have be en placed on p robation (poten t i al eligi bility). Chil dren discon t i nued from Medi-Ca l under any pro gram must be evalu ated for eligib ility under other Med i-Cal prog rams. Adoptio n Assistance Payments (AAP): Chil dren may receive a federa lly f u nded adop t i on assistance subsid y un der Title I V-E or a state- funded subsidy per state gu idelin es. Payments to the parents of an eligi ble chi ld with special needs can take the form of either one -t i me (nonrecurri ng) or ongoi ng (recurring) ad option assistan ce. Chil dren receivi ng AAP payments are no t a lways elig ible to recei ve Medi-Cal if residing i n Californi a. AAP children from another state re siding in Californ ia may rece ive Medi-Cal and must be assessed indi viduall y and, if eli gible, gra nted unde r t h e approp riate Interstate Compa ct on Adoptio n and Medica l Assistance (ICAMA) aid code. The depend ent status of t he child is no t a factor i n determin ing Medi-C al eligi bility. Each c h ild i s in his/he r own Medi-Cal Family Budg et Unit (MFBU). The income a nd resource s of the paren t s an d si blings are not considered i n t h e childs Med i-Cal eli gibili t y de t e rmination. AFDC-Foster Care (FC): Chil dren place d in f o st e r care supervisio n may receive a federa lly funded payme nt un der Title IV-E o r a st a t e -f u nded, n on-Title I V-E payment per state guide lines. So me chil dren might no t be eligib le for a paymen t , but migh t still b e eligib le for Medi-Cal. Chil dren placed un der fost e r ca re supervision are n ot al ways eligi ble to receive Medi-C al. Each case must b e asse ssed i ndividu ally and, if eligi ble, gra nted u nder t he app ropriate aid code. T h e dep endent status of t h e child is not a factor in determi ning Medi -Cal elig ibility. Each child i s in his/he r ow n MF BU . The income and reso urces of the pare nts and sib lings are not consid ered in the chil ds Medi-Ca l eligib ility determina t i on. Verify that the sending state is cove ring the child s Medicaid wh ile in CA. Non-foster care childre n from out of state pl aced in a CA medical and mental heal t h facili t y, boardi ng school , educatio nal i nst i t u t i on, or other pa rent or legal guardia ns ho me is considere d a CA reside nt and po t e ntially elig ible to Medi-C al. Kinshi p-Guardian Assi st a nce Program (KinGAP): KinGAP establish es a separa t e payme nt rate for children who are leavi ng t he foster care system an d are pla ced with relative s w ho obtain gua rdianshi p. KinGAP consists of two compon ents  a f e derally-fun ded compone nt a nd a stat e -f u nded compo nent. To quali f y for the KinGAP Progra m, a chi ld must have: Been remo ved from t h e parental home pursuant to a voluntary pla cement agreeme nt o r the re sult of a judi cial determinatio n to t he effect that continua t i on in the home would be contrary to the welfare of the child and be en adjudge d a de pendent child of the juveni le court p ursuant to WIC Section 30 0, or a w ard of t he juvenile co urt p ursuant to WI C Sectio n 601 or 602 Been resid ing for at l east 6 con secutive months in the appro ved home of t h e relative whil e under the juri sdiction of the j uvenile court or under a voluntary pla cement agree ment or of a previo usly appro ved relative gu ardian A w ritt e n bin ding agreemen t entered into by the relative guardi an an d the county w elfare agency, proba t i on departmen t , or Title IV-E tribal agen cy, pri or t o the e st a blishmen t of the guard ianship A ki nship guardia nship establishe d pursu ant to W IC Sections 366.26, 360, or 728(d), and depe ndency dismi ssed pursuan t to WIC Section 366.3, or wardsh ip terminated pursu ant t o WIC Section 73 8(e) concurren t l y or sub sequently to the establ ishment of the kinship gu ardiansh ip. Each Ki nGAP child is in his/her own MFBU, even i f t h ere are other sibl ings or a need y caretaker relative i n t h e home. Unacco mpanied R efugee Minor (U RM): The D epartment of Health C are Service s (DHCS) provides f u ll scop e Medi-C al wi t ho ut a sha re of cost to child ren in the U RM Program, if otherw ise eligi ble. The URM Pro gram provid es culturally and ling uistically a ppropria t e child w elfare, foster care, an d indep endent li ving servi ces to minors w ho do not have parents in the United States (U.S.), or who enter the U.S. unaccomp anied b y a parent, an immedi ate adult relative , or an a dult having do cumentable l egal evide nce of custody of t he minor. These children are pl aced i nt o the U RM Program by the O ffice of Refugee Resettlemen t (ORR). URM child ren do no t e nter the states chil d welfare system b ecause they are not usuall y removed from the home of a pare nt o r l egal gua rdian due to abu se, ne glect, or t h rough a volun t a ry a greement. For Med i-Cal purposes, URM chi ldren are treated like f o st e r care children . Unlike foster care regul ations, O R R re gulation s do not requi re t ha t UR M chil dren be placed in the care and custody of the state. O RR regul ations req uire states t o ensure legal responsi bility, incl uding legal custody and / o r County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Adoptio n Assista n c e Payments (AAP), Foster Care , K i nship- Guardian A ssistance Program (KinGAP), and U n a ccompanied Refugee Minor (URM) 5.11.01 4 of 4 guard ianship , is establish ed for each URM child . Currently the st ate has three U RM Program se rvice provid ers: Cathol ic Charities of Santa Cl ara County (CCSC C) Crittenton Servi ces f o r C hildren an d F a milies (Crittenton ) i n O ra nge County Internation al Christian Ad options (ICA) in Sacramen t o C ounty These service provi ders may place youth who are in the federal URM Program wi t h certified foster paren t s in n eighbor ing counties. Procedure: Follow the rules above to determi ne eligib ility for Medi-Cal f or chi ldren in these pr ograms. content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Program Guide Number Page Presumptive Eligib ility for Pregnant W ome n Program 05.16 1 of 3 Revision Date: 05/08/20 17 Back g r o und: In Novembe r 1 992 the Legi slature passed AB 501 , wh ich required the D epartment of Health Care Se rvices (DHC S) to imp lement the federal op t i on of Presumptive Eligi bility (PE) for pregnan t wo men as described i n section 19 520 of t h e Social Securi t y Act. T h e PE p rogram allo ws qualified Me di-Cal pro viders through out the state to provide thei r l ow-income pre gnant patients immed iate, t e mporary Medi-Ca l coverage for prena t a l care. These patie nts mu st then ap ply formally for Medi-Ca l or CalWORKs within 60 d ays o f thei r PE app lication. On April 01 , 20 17 DHCS imple mented the Cali f o rnia Medicai d Managemen t Informatio n Syst e m (C A-MMI S) Online Po rt a l f o r Qua lified Provide rs (QPs) in the Presu mptive Eligib ility for Pregnant Women Progra m (PE4PW) to assist applica nts a pplying for PE. Purpose: To inform staff o f the Presu mptive Eligib ility for Pregnant Women Progra m (PE4 PW ) and the o nline app lication process. Poli c y: Eligi bility Criteri a: Appli cants must me et the fol lowing el igibil ity cri t e ria t o q ualify for PE: Inco me mu st no t exce ed 213% of the Federal Po verty L evel (FPL) Mu st be a Ca lifornia resi dent Mu st attest to being pre gnant Mu st not be curre ntly enrolle d i n Medi-Cal Mu st not have h ad PE enrollme nt for the curren t pre gnancy Presumptive El igibil ity Ap plication Pro cess: Be neficiaries wi ll apply for bene f i t s in p erson at Qualified Pro viders (QP) o f fice s. The n ew MC 263-P appl ication is a one-p age PE4PW program app lication that wil l allow QPs to collect the appl icants self-attested information . Au t ho rized QP st a f f review the co mpleted one-p age appl ication and in put t h e applican t  s i nformation via the PE4PW Online Portal (C A-MMI S). The MC 2 63-P paper app lication is not to be mail ed or faxed to DHCS for the PE4PW program; rather, the purpo se of thi s p aper appli cation is to assist QPs i n collecting ne cessary information for in put i nto the onli ne portal. PE4 P W Eli gibility determi nation resul t s wi ll be immedia t e ly displayed i n real time. If the appli cant is determined el igible for PE4PW, the benefici ary will be assig ned aid code 7 G and the QP will prin t out the el igibili t y de t e rmination and the Immed iate Need Eli gibility Do cument . PE4 P W ben eficiaries must submi t a compl eted IAP a pplication n o later t h an the last day of t h e month follow ing the month in wh ich PE4PW w as granted. If IAP appl ication is submi t ted d uring the PE4PW perio d, the ir coverage can be exten ded pendi ng the Medi-Ca l determination (a pproval or den ial). NOTE: Ap plicants with a neg ative pregnan cy test resul t or otherw ise found to be not pregn ant by t h e Q P, will not receive a n I mme diate Need Eli gibili t y Do cument . MEDS will place the a pplican t in a id code 7F, and the QP wil l o nly be able to clai m re imbursement for the pregn ancy t e st an d initial visi t . Criteri a for Qual ified Provide rs: In order to become a Qua lified Provide r (QP) for the PE4PW Program, provide rs mu st : Be a Me di-Cal Provi der in good stand ing; AND Pro vide prenatal ca re. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Program Guide Number Page Presumptive Eligib ility for Pregnant W ome n Program 05.16 2 of 3 For Providers wi shing to become a QP, they must request enrol lment by downlo ading the app lication, QP Appli cation and Agree ment f o r Pa rt i cipation in the PE4 P W Progra m a nd follow the di rections for submission . Qualifie d Provider Resp onsibil ity: Qualifie d Providers are respo nsible for the follo wing: Offering the PR4 PW Prog ram t o p regnant patien t s wh o d o not have Medi-Ca l or other adequa t e h ealth coverag e. The MC 2 64-Presumptive El igibil ity Pa t i ent Fact Shee t shou ld be given to the app licant for informatio n. Assi st the app licant with compl etion of t h e MC 263 P appli cation in order to coll ect the a pplicants sel f - attested informatio n. Inform the app licant at the time of t h e PE d etermination that she must file her IAP appl ication within a specifie d t i me (before the end of the month follo wing the of the PE applica t i on) in order for the PE to continu e. Assi st the app licant in compl eting her IAP applicatio n, i f ne eded. N otify the a pplicant in wri t i ng (MC 267- Explan ation of Ineligi bility for Presumptive Elig ibility) if she is determin ed ineli gible for PE and that she may still file a n a pplicatio n f o r Me di-Cal wi t h the C ounty. PE4 P W QPs are requi red t o p rovide ben eficiaries of the PE4PW Program with an Insur ance Affordabil ity Pro gram (IAP) a pplication . Pri nting out the eligi bility determin ation and the Immedia t e N eed Eligib ility Documen t for the bene f i ciary. Ma intain records of PE appl ications and pro vide these records to DHC S u pon request. NOTE: The C ounty is not responsi ble for issuing a rep lacement of the Immediate Nee d Eligibi lity Document. The QP who initia lly determine d e ligibi lity f o r PE is respo nsible for issui ng a replace ment d ocument. Procedure: Medi-C al Applica t i on Process: Women enrolle d in the PE4 P W Program must submit an IAP Ap plication or a Cal-WORKs applica t i on no later than the last day of the month f o llowin g the mon t h in wh ich PE4PW wa s granted. Ap plicants ca n apply online , by phon e, ma il or in person a t any Famil y R esource Cen t e r (FRC ). Retroactive C overage: Some PE Beneficiarie s may have recei ved health care services not covered unde r the PE4PW program or prior t o t h eir appl ication for PE or Medi-Ca l. Eligib ility staff shall a sk if the app licant nee ds retroactive co verage for past medical se rvices. Minor Co nsent Eligib le: If a min or appli es for the PE4 PW Program, she must self-attest to the total family i ncome, to the best of her knowl edge. If a minor a pplicant do es not want her p arents to know tha t sh e is applyi ng for Medi-C al, or is not able to attest to t h e family income, the provide r canno t off e r PE4PW servi ces. The app licant w ill be referred t o appl y for Med i-Cal und er t h e Minor Consen t Prog ram (MPG 04.04 ). MEDS Interface: MEDS will pro vide a response to the PE online portal (C A-MMI S) with an imme diate PE4PW e ligibi lity determin ation in real time . MEDS i s programe d to automatica lly termina t e all PE4 P W benefits for b eneficiarie s who re ach the 6 0-day li mit unle ss MEDS has a record of a pen ding I AP appl ication. If MEDS show s a pendi ng HX-1 8 transactio n (Covere d C alifornia app lication) or AP-18 Transaction (coun t y appl ication) MEDS will not automatical ly terminate the PE4PW ben efits u ntil t h e applica t i on is adjud icated with either HX-2 0 or EW -2 0.

content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Aged and D isabl e d Federa l Pover ty L e vel Prog r ams 05.19.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 12/01/20 20 Back g r o und: Known under the Affordabl e Care Act (ACA) as Non-Mo dified Adju st e d G ro ss I nco me (Non-MAGI) category, the Aged and Disab led Federal Poverty Level (A&D FPL) Program provide s zero Sha re of Cost (SO C ) Medi-C al to eligi ble aged or disa bled individ uals thro ughout t h e State of Cali f o rnia. The A&D FPL Program was estab lished Jan uary 1, 2001. Purpose: This section i dentifies potentiall y elig ible A&D FPL individ uals a nd de scribes i nstructions to determine elig ibility and level of b enefits. This section has been updated to i nclude the new income limit of 138% of the FPL and remo ve the program i ncome disreg ard of $230 for ind ividual s, $3 10 for couples an d is effective December 1, 2020. This section was also up dated with ch anges to how the Medicare Part B deductio n is applie d t o the A&D FPL bud get eff e ct i ve December 1, 2020 . Poli c y: A potentia lly eligi ble A&D FPL indi vidual is ag ed or disab led, but not residi ng in a Lon g-Term Care (LTC) Facility. There is no ag e limit for t h ose in the disabl ed category therefore di sabled chi ldren may be eva luated for this p rogram. Blind individ uals may also be elig ible to the A&D F PL Program if they meet the aged or disa bled criteria. When app licants are blind a nd not in receipt of T i t l e I I disab ility bene f i t s, eval uate for t he F ed eral Poverty Level f or the Bli nd (FPLB) program, refer to MPG 05.19.02. A. Income Eli gibili t y Requi re ments Non-MAGI inco me rules app ly to A&D FPL income eval uations incl uding al locating to othe r public assistance (PA) spouse s (Refer to MPG Articl e 10 for income gu idelin es). Effective 12/1/202 0, the indi vidual s net non-exemp t income must be at o r belo w 13 8% of the FPL for the applica ble f am ily size after deductions. Also effective 1 2/1/2020, do not ap ply t he stand ard d eductions ($230 for an indi vidual and $310 for a coup le) i n A&D FPL Prog ram eva luations. For de f i nitions and examples, see Desk Aid 88 . B. Property Standards Non-MAGI prope rt y rul es apply to the A&D FPL property evalu ation. Refer to MPG Articl e 9. C. Applicatio n Proces s Effective January 1, 201 4, Med i-Cal app licants, are screene d f or el igibil ity t o MAGI Medi-C al as part of the Medi-Ca l hierarchy ap plication p rocess. See Desk Aid 74 for the Medi -Cal hiera rchy when determin ing eligib ility. Whe n no el igibil ity to MAGI Medi-C al exists, Medi -Cal appli cants, not residin g in LTC, w ill be screened for eligib ility t o the A&D F PL Progra m. The order of evaluation whe n determin ing A&D FPL eligi bility is as follow s: 1. Pickle 2. A&D FPL/Aged, Blind , or Di sabled Medi cally Need y (AB D MN) Z er o S OC 3. Federal Po verty Level for the Blind 4. Aged, Blin d and Disabl ed Medical ly Needy (ABD MN) SOC 5. 250% Worki ng Disabl ed County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Aged and D isabl e d Federa l Pover ty L e vel Prog r ams 05.19.01 2 of 3 A&D in dividua ls are poten t i ally eli gible t o t h ree months o f ret r oactive bene f i t s when el igibil ity requi rements are met in the preced ing months. D. Deductions Apply all ap plicabl e non-MAGI in come ded uctions incl uding t h e $20.00 any inco me, health insurance premiu ms, and, where the customer ha s earned income, the $ 65.00 and one-hal f e arned in come dedu ct i ons. Effective Decembe r 1, 202 0, de duct the Med icare Part B Pre mium amount whether it is paid by the customer or t he state. Do no t remove the Medicare Part B premiu m ded uction f ro m the A&D FPL budg et w hen the state begin s pa ying the premiu m. ABD ap plicants i n licen sed board and care (B&C) may be evalu ated for the A&D FPL Progra m and are elig ible to all B&C deductions. They are entitled to receive eithe r the perso nal care service (PCS) dedu ct i on or t h e income dedu ct i on for exce ss B&C (MPG 1 0.06.08). These deduction s will be use d in the A&D FPL income eva luation. E. Case Composition A&D FPL eligib le ind ividual s will be i n their own Med i-Cal F am ily Budg et Unit (MFBU) and el igible coupl es wil l remai n togethe r in one MFBU. A&D FPL el igible indivi duals and cou ples w ill b e ine ligibl e members in the MFBU for othe r family me mbers app lying f or or recei ving Me di-Cal benefits. The income of the A&D FPL indivi dual(s) i s includ ed in t he other famil y members budget a nd the mainten ance need l evel for the family will i nclude the A&D FPL indi vidual(s). If a couple is eligi ble, both spou ses will be on the A&D FPL Prog ram; however, if bo t h spouses canno t qua lify a s a coup le f or the A&D FPL P r ogram, either spouse can appl y sep arately to q ualify. The spo use that cho oses not to be in t he A&D FPL Prog ram may cho ose not to be on Medi-Cal or may quali f y throug h the MN Progra m wi t h a SOC. I t is possibl e for spouse s to be in two different progra ms. A&D FPL individu als may b e d etermined elig ible to t h e Qua lified Medicare Ben eficiary (QMB) progra m o r the S p ecified Low -I n come Medicare Ben eficiary (SLMB) progra m. See Desk Aid 88 f o r examples of different A&D FPL househ olds. F. Level of Benefits A&D FPL eligib le individ uals who are Uni t e d St a t e s (U S) Ci t i zens, US N ationals or immig rants w ith Satisfactory Immigratio n Status (SIS) will receive ful l-scope be nefits. A&D FPL elig ible immi grants withou t SIS will re ceive restricted ben efits. The follo wing aid co des are used for this progra m: 1H Full- S co pe FPL Aged Individu als 6H Full- S co pe FPL Disable d I nd ividual s 1U Restricted F PL Age d I n dividua ls 6U Restricted F PL D isabled Indi viduals Note: A&D FPL eligib le blind i ndividu als are linked as either aged or di sabled. Redeter min a ti ons and Period of Eligi bility Eligi bility for the A&D FPL program must be rede t e rmined ann ually. Regul ar Medi-Cal redetermi nation proced ures are followe d for this prog ram. At redetermi nation, all A&D Medi-C al bene f i ciaries, except for Pickle/Disa bled Adult Child (DAC) benefici aries, w ill be eva luated using Non- MAGI p rogram regul ations. Approval for Release: Rick Wanne , Di rector Eligi bility Operation s County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Federal Poverty Leve l for the Blind 05.19.02 1 of 2 Revision Date: 08/01/20 18 Back g r o und: This program covers b lind individ uals pursuant t o Title X VI who have not yet or cann ot meet t he Title II criteria for d isabili t y based upo n blind ness. This section is being updated t o t h e new forma t , no other chan ges were made . Purpose: This section is to provi de guidel ines for the Federal Pove rt y Le vel Program for the Blind (FPLB). Poli c y: The Fede ral Poverty Level Prog ram for the B l ind (FPLB) mirrors the el igibil ity criteria f or the A&D FPL Program, except the linkage is based on blind ness and t he in come limit ma y be hig her for coupl es. Aid code 2 H is eff e ct i ve July 1, 2009. A. General Rule FPLB is availab le for b lind individu als whe t h er they p reviously applie d for or received SSI /SSP and were de nied or disco ntinued or app lied for Medi-C al-only. FPLB is availa ble for the followi ng blind i ndividua ls who: Have no t met or who cannot meet the Title II criteri a f o r d isabili t y ba sed blindn ess Meet the Title XVI criteria for blind ness Alleg e t h at the y h ave blindn ess and who are w aiting disab ility evalua t i ons Have ha d medical de t e rmination verifie d by a doctor A pe rson is conside red to be bli nd i f there ha s been a me dical determinatio n verified by a doctor that they have ei t h er of the fol lowing con ditions: Central visual acuity if no more than 2 0/200 with correction s Tunnel vi sion, which is a li mited field of 20 deg rees or less Any disabili t y determina t i on ba sed upo n bli ndness would only change retroactively, w hen i t would have a positive effective for all family members livi ng in t he ho me. The effective date of t he po sitive retroactive c hange w ould go back to the o nset date of disa bility for the Medi-Cal recipien t or July 1, 2009 . Persons eligib le und er FLPB must meet the pro perty, citizenshi p, alien status, reside ncy, institutiona l status, and coopera t i on requireme nts spe cified in MPG Articl es 4, 6, 7 and 9. They must also meet the SOC require ment in MPG 1 2.01. B. Case C ompo s i tion FPLB e ligibl e in dividua l(s) wi ll be in their own MFBU an d el igible coupl es wi ll re main t o gether in on e MFBU. content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Safe Arm s Fo r N ew borns 05.20.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 05/01/20 18 Back g r o und: The Safe Arms f o r Newb orns La w wa s enacted to p rovide f o r the health and sa f e t y of un wanted newb orn chi ldren. U nder this law, any chil d less than se venty-two hou rs old, who is volun t a rily surrend ered t o an empl oyee on duty at a public or private hospi t a l eme rgency room, w ill be determin ed eli gible t o Medi-C al. The l aw also requi res that the hospital taking ph ysical cu st o dy provid e a medical scree ning examin ation and any ne cessary medical ca re t o the ch ild. Include d with t h e reformatting, t hi s section is bein g upda t e d to in clude a pplicatio n process clarifica t i ons issued in AC W D L 03-26E. Purpose: This section provides instructions regard ing t he proce ssing of cases unde r the Safe Arms for Newb orns Law. Poli c y: The De partment of Heal t h Care Servi ces (DHCS) has issued instructions for h ospitals an d for county Medi-C al eligi bility staff regarding the Sa f e Arms for New born Law. A. Hospital I nstr u c ti ons DHC S ha s instructed hospital s as foll ows: Upon taki ng physical cu st o dy of surr endered ne wborns, give these chi ldren a medica l screening examin ation and provi de them any necessa ry med ical care. The hospi t a l employee takin g physical custod y of the new born must enter the iden t i f i cation numbe r from the chi lds hospi t a l ankle brace let in the ID number field i n t he t op right corner of the MC 356, SAFE ARMS FO R N EW BORN S Me dical Question naire. The hospi t a l t a king physical cust o dy of the n ewborn must offer the person surre ndering custod y the MC 356. The person su rrenderin g t he child is not requi red to complete or return the MC 356 . The paren t na mes may not be requested . A hospital tha t rece ives a surrende red newborn mu st in itiate a request for Medi-Ca l for t ha t chi ld no later than the fol lowing bu siness day. B. County I nstr u c ti ons DHC S ha s instructed counties as follo ws: Coun t y el igibil ity staff are respo nsible for comple t i ng the appli cation and SOF. When actual n ames and birth dates are u navaila ble, use the health facil ity i dentification informatio n and estimated date of birth, if availa ble, in establi shing the Medi-C al eligi bility record. For the purpose s o f this pro gram, assume that the newbo rn is a United States citizen. A child sup port referral to the Departmen t of Chil d Support Enforcemen t is not requ ired. Upon g ranting, provid e t he health facility with the in f o rmation necessary to obtai n reimbursemen t for care provid ed to t h e newborn as soo n as eligib ility is establish ed. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Safe Arm s Fo r N ew borns 05.20.01 2 of 3 C. Period of Eligibi lity Unde r t h is law, eli gibili t y begins the d ay of surrende r and extends throu gh the last da y of t h e followi ng month. Howeve r, if a chi ld is surr endered on the last d ay of the month, e ligibi lity ma y contin ue through the third mon t h . For exampl e, i f a child i s surr endered to a hospital on the Ma rch 1 5, el igibil ity extends t h rough A p ril 30 . If t h e surrend er date is March 31, elig ibility may be ext e nded t hr ough Ma y 31. In no circumstance will coverag e under this category exten d past t he last day of t he t hi rd month. Newb orns determined elig ible to the Safe Arms f or New borns Program are not el igible to continui ng Medi-C al benefits t h rough the Deemed Eligib ility Program for in f a nts or the Continuo us Eli gibili t y for Chil dren Program. Continu ing eligib ility for the chil d will be establish ed under normal prog ram criteria at the time that the child eithe r enters the fost e r care system or is placed with a responsib le re lative or caretaker. D. Aid Code These chil dren are to be placed in a new ze ro share of cost ai d code 2A. Thi s ai d code will be use d by DHC S to track cases ope ned unde r the Safe Arms for Newb orn Law. E. Surrendered Newborns Not Covered Under the Safe Arm s fo r N ewb orns Program Surrend ered n ewborn babie s, not co vered u nder the Safe Arms for N ewborns Program, are ha ndled on a case-b y-case ba sis usin g formerly establish ed proce dures. Re f e r to De sk Aid 87 for case exampl es. Procedure: F. County Requi r ed Action When proce ssing a request for Medi-Cal for a surrend ered newbo rn less t h an seventy-two hours old and t h e actual name and date of birth of the new born are unava ilable; complete the appli cation an d SOF as an immedi ate need using the hosp ital ide ntification information and estimated date o f birth. For example, if the hosp ital h as assi gned a name for id entification purpo ses, such as Baby Doe BBB or Abandon ed Baby AAA, these are acceptab le and searchab le on MEDS. Names cannot contain n umbers, only letters can be use d. Important Note: Treat these cases as confid ential cases. Do Not use pa rents name, social se curity number, or dates of births, if known. The case numb er assigned i s n ot to be u sed once Safe Arms for Newborn s el igibil ity ends. Do Not ban k the se cases to continuing . Intake is respon sible for holdi ng the case for the period of eli gibili t y. Program Impact/s: Automation : In the "Sele ct e d" group box for all pro grams, click the Emergency checkb ox. The n select the Safe Arms for New Borns Bene f i t s che ckbox. title: Section 21 - In-Home Supportive Services
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page In-Home Supp ortive Ser vices (IHSS) 05.21.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: 06/01/20 21 Back g r o und: In-Home Suppo rt i ve Servi ces (IHSS) provide s homema ker an d perso nal care a ssistance t o low- income customers who need assistan ce in their ho me so they can remain in depende nt. These in- home servi ces are provide d by indepe ndent provide rs/ IHSS provi ders/homemake rs. Customers a pplying for or re ceiving IHSS must have a Medi-Cal e ligibi lity determinatio n completed before in-ho me services are autho rized. IHSS Programs The follow ing progra ms p rovide in-ho me services: IHSS Plus Option (IPO) (Aid Code 2L ) Persona l Care Services Prog ram (PCSP) (Aid Code 2M) IHSS Residu al (Aid Code 2 N) Commun ity Fi rst Cho ice (CFCO) (Aid Code 2K) IHSS aid co des a re rep orted to the Medi-Cal Eligi bility Data S ystem (MEDS) via t he Case Manag ement Information an d Payrolli ng System (CMIPS) and NOT entere d by the Medi-C al Human Services Spe cialist (HSS) into Cal W IN. Purpose: This section is up dated t o add the I H SS-CFCO prog ram an d clar ifications f ro m All Coun t y Welfare Directors Letter (AC W D L) 20-15 regard ing the Beneficia ry Reimb ursement Proce ss (also known as the Conl an process). Poli c y: IHSS Programs: IHSS Plus Option (IPO) (Aid Code 2L ) To qualify for IPO, Medi-Cal eli gibili t y is require d. Custome rs not receivi ng Su pplemen t al Secu rity Income/State Suppleme nt a l Prog ram (SSI/SSP), or anothe r Medi -Cal linked cash-ba sed pr ogram (f o r exampl e: F o st e r Care, CalWORKs, Refug ee Cash Assistan ce [RCA], Adoptions Assi st an ce Program [AAP]) must be determined elig ible for federa lly fun ded f ul l-scope Medi-Ca l an d qua lify for in-home services throu gh a Needs Assessme nt comp leted by an IHSS Social Worke r. Persona l Care Services Prog ram (PCSP) (Aid Code 2M) To quali f y for PCSP, customers not recei ving SSI/SSP, or Medi -Cal linke d to a cash-based pro gram must be determine d eligibl e f or fede rally funded full-sco pe Medi-Cal an d be f o und in need of person al care service s t hro ugh a Need s Asse ssment completed by an IHSS Socia l W o rker. IHSS Residu al (Aid Code 2 N) IHSS Residu al Program services wil l be availab le t o custome rs w ho are eligi ble under curren t IHSS regul ations but are not eli gible for federal ly f u nded full-scop e Medi-Cal . Commun ity Fi rst Cho ice (CFCO) (Aid Code 2K) The CFCO program is an alternative for PCSP and IP O customers. CFCO provides home and communi t y-b ased attenda nt services and su pports for customers who are elig ible for Med i-Cal, meet County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page In-Home Supp ortive Ser vices (IHSS) 05.21.01 2 of 3 specific inco me cri t er ia a nd the Nursi ng F a cility Level of C are (N F L O C ). CFCO customers are e ligibl e to be evalu ated under Medi -Cal Spousa l I mp overishmen t (SI) Provision s, i f app licable . See MPG 05.18.01 for the SI Provisio ns eligib ility and Doctors Veri f i cation process. Case Proce ssing: Appli cation The Sin gle Streaml ined App lication and rela t e d forms are used to comp lete the Me di-Cal determin ation. The Medi-C al appli cation packet must contai n Disabil ity Determination Services Divi sion (DDSD) forms for cases in whi ch the applica nts disabil ity h as not already bee n determined . Rede t e rmination The MC 210R V a nd related forms are used to compl ete t h e annual re determination . Share-o f -C ost (SOC) Customers with a SOC are trea t e d as Medicall y Nee dy customers with a SOC. T he SOC may be met with any medi cal service (inclu ding paymen t s to the IHSS provider) and ou t -o f -p ocket expenses for person al services. IHSS Plus Option Income Payments made under the IHSS Plus Option are exempt as inco me and prope rt y. These e xempt paymen t s in clude: Careg iver wage s t h at are paid to a parent of an I H SS Plus Option min or child reci pient for services pro vided to that child Careg iver wages that a re pa id t o a spouse of an I H SS Plus Option recipi ent for services provid ed to that recipien t Restaura nt me al allow ances from IHSS f or the IHSS Plus Option re cipient The advance payments made t o IHSS Plu s Option recipie nts to pa y their caregive rs dire ct l y for services pro vided und er t he I H S S Plu s O ptio n In-Home C aregiver Wages In-home careg iver wages receive d by a spouse / p arent f o r the care of their spouse or minor child i n receip t of federa l, state, or local governmen t in-home services program are exe mpt as income and prope rt y f or Medi-Cal purposes. This exemption i ncludes p ayments receive d by a pa rent or spouse of an IHSS Resid ual recipi ent. In-Home C are Services Payments Payments made by the D epartment of Hea lth C are S e rvices (DHCS) to an in-h ome care recipient for the purp ose of purchasin g in-home ca re services, inclu ding restaura nt me als, are exempt as in come and pro perty f or Med i-Cal purp oses. Procedure: Appli cation Compl ete a Medi -Cal eli gibili t y determinatio n using Medi-Cal rules, forms, and N otices of Actions (NOAs) for all appl icants or recipie nts of IHSS. The IHSS Needs Assessmen t can b e completed by the IHSS Social Worker at any time du ring this process. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page In-Home Supp ortive Ser vices (IHSS) 05.21.01 3 of 3 Hospi t a l & Community Suppo rt Servi ces HSSs Process IHSS rela t e d Medi-Cal referrals accordi ng to the procedu res outlined in MPG 4. 2 , MPG 4.3, and Med i-Cal Processi ng G u ide 02 CMIPS II Interface Activitie s. Aged & Disa bled Federal P o verty Level (A&D FPL) Program The Medi-Ca l de t e rmination is separate from t he IHSS determina t i on. D et e rmine potential eli gibili t y to the A&D FPL accordin g t o the p olicies ou t l ined in MPG 5.19. Disab ility Determina t i on Services Divi sion (DDSD) For cases that require a disabili t y de t e rmination, follo w t h e DDSD requi rements outlined i n MPG 5.4. CalWORKs Di scontinuance When a C alWORKs recipien t , who is also receivi ng IHSS, is discontinu ed and has n o other MediC al elig ibility, contact the IHSS So cial Worker to request a copy of the D DSD determinatio n. If the DDSD determin ation shows tha t the re cipient is disa bled and t he reexamina t i on date has not pa ssed, use that determina t i on for Medi-Cal e ligibi lity. Rede t e rmination Each Famil y R esource Cen t e r (F R C) is responsi ble for completin g the annua l redetermina t i on of these case s accordin g to the proce dures outli ned in MPG 4 . 1 5 and Med i-Cal Proce ssing Guide 02 CMIPS II Interface Activitie s. Benefici ary Reimburse ment P r ocess (BRP) IHSS benefici aries who are Medi -Cal eligi ble and paid a n out-of-pocket expense for the excess SOC can file a claim to reque st rei mbursement. See MPG 04.02.10J for the BR P (also known as t h e Conl an proce ss). F o r scenario s where S p ousal Impo verishment (SI) pr ovisions a re invol ved, see Processin g G u ide 25. Program Impacts None . title: Section 1 - Institutional Status
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti onal Status 06.01.01 1 of 5 Revision Date: 2/1/2023 Back g r o und: This section provide s staff w ith in st ru ct i ons for the determina t i on o f Medi-C al eligib ility f or peo ple in institution s. Inmates of a pu blic institution who ap ply f o r Med i-Cal must be evaluated . Resid ence in a public institution does not disq ualify a pplican t s from Medi-C al i n and of itself. H owever, i f the in mate meets all other elig ibility standard s, elig ibility must b e gra nted and immediately suspe nded until they are no long er considere d inmates of a public i nst i t u t i on (see MPG 06.02.05 for suspensi on polici es). Inmates who receive inpatien t care of f the gro unds of the f aci lity wh o are otherwi se Medi -Cal eligibl e are eligi ble to the Me di-Cal Inmate El igibil ity Program ((MCIEP), see Article 6, section 2). MC I EP is limi t ed to servi ces inmates receive of f the grou nds of t h e institution. Resid ents of speci f i c inmate faci lities, such as the Mal e Commun ity Reentry Pro gram (MCRP) and Custody to Co mmunity Transi t i onal Reentry Programs (CCTRP), are conside red i nmates of a pu blic institution . This se ct i on wa s upda t e d wi t h the clarification that MCR P and CCTRP residents are n o long er considere d inmates of a public i nst i t u t i on when they rea ch t h e t h ird phase of the progra m. Poli c y: A. Definition o f Pub lic Institutions The follow ing are ide ntified as publi c institutions: State or Federal priso ns Correction al facilities County, city, or t ri bal jail s Detention ce nters Californ ia Youth Authority (CYA) camps Reside ntial facilitie s l ocated on the groun ds of o r a djacent to any large public institutio n Correction al or holdi ng facili t i es for prisoners or ind ividual s bein g held unde r court o rder as witnesse s Detention facilities, camps, trainin g school s, or any other facil ity for chil dren de t e rmined to be deli nquent Education o r vo cational traini ng institutions that provid e an accredited pr ogram for its residents Alternative custody facilitie s where the reside nts are servi ng their sentence i n a commu nity setting (for example , CCTRP, Enhan ced Alternative Custody Progra m (EAC P), Female Offende r Treatmen t and Empl oyment Program (FOTEP), MCR P, and co unty work furlough Prog rams) NOTE: Peopl e w ho reside in publ ic i nstitutions to rece ive education al or vo cational trainin g p rovided by the facil ity (for example, a state sch ool for the bl ind) are n ot considere d inmates of a pu blic institution . . B. Facilities that are not Publ ic Inst i t u t i ons County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti onal Status 06.01.01 2 of 5 The follow ing facilitie s a re not public in st i t u t i ons: A medical i nst i t u t i on An intermedi ate care facility A publicl y o perated resid ence that serves no more than 16 re sidents A child care facil ity tha t acco mmodates no more than 25 children An in st i t u t i on for i nt e llectuall y disabl ed peo ple or persons with rel at e d condi t i ons (chro nic disa bility attributed to cere bral palsy, ep ilepsy, or any othe r co ndition othe r t h an mental il lness closel y related to intell ectual disa bility). Eligi bility and placement are usually thro ugh the San Diego R egional Center A communi t y care facili t y which is maintain ed and operated t o provide 24-hour non-medi cal care f or child ren and/or adults, i ncluding but not limited to, the physi cally handica pped, mentally impair ed, incomp etent persons, and neg lected or abused ch ildren C. Individu als Consid ered Inmates of a Public Institution 1. An inmate i n a prison or a county, city, or t ri bal jail Note: This include s in mates being held p rior to a rraignmen t , convictio n, or senten cing. It doe s no t inclu de indivi duals who are out on bail or their ow n recogniza nce 2. An i ndividu al, who is inca rcerated, but who can leave prison or jai l on work rel ease or work furloug h and must return at specific times (work furlou gh) 3. A minor in a juven ile deten t i on center prio r to his or her disposition (judgmen t ) d ue to a crimina l activity of the minor 4. A minor w ho is pla ced in a d etention or corr ect i onal facil ity aft e r detention, incl uding a youth ranch, forestry camp, or home w hich is part of the criminal j ust i ce system 5. A mi nor pla ced on juven ile i nt e nsive p robation by a juvenil e court with spe cific cond itions o f relea se, i ncludin g residence in a j uvenile de t e ntion center 6. A minor p laced on probation by a juveni le court or on juvenil e intensive p robation to a secure treatment facil ity contracted w ith the juve nile d etention cen t e r if the secu re treatment facil ity is part of the criminal justice system 7. Resid ents of alternative cust o dy facilities w here the in mate serves their se ntence in a co mmunity setting (for examp le, CCTRP, MCRP, or work f u rlough). NOT E: Indivi duals in cou nty facilitie s may be el igible t o MC I EP i f othe rwise Medi-C al eligi ble. CCTRP and MC RP residents who are in phase thre e or f o ur of the p rogram are no lo nger conside red inmates of a publ ic institution D. Individu als Not Consid ered Inmates of a Public Institution 1. An indivi dual who, after arrest b ut be f o re bo oking, is escorted by police to a hospital for medical treatment and hel d under gua rd 2. An in dividua l in priso n or jai l who t ran sf e rs temporaril y (one to two months) to a ha lfway hou se or reside ntial treatment facility prior to a formal pro bation rele ase order 3. An individ ual who is rel eased from priso n or jail , but who is on prob ation, p arole, or rel ease o rder with one o f the foll owing cond itions: Home arr est Work release Commun ity se rvice Outpatient treatment County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti onal Status 06.01.01 3 of 5 Inpatien t treatmen t 4. An ind ividual released f rom prison or j ail unde r a court proba t i on order du e to a medica l emerge ncy 5. A minor hel d in a juveni le detention cen t e r f or car e, pr ot e ct i on, or in the best interest of the child if: It i s prior to dispositio n (judgmen t ), and There is a specific plan for that minor that makes the stay at the detention center temporary (one to two months) This could include those j uveniles aw aiting place ment but st i ll physical ly present in juven ile hall 6. A minor placed on pro bation or juvenil e i ntensive probatio n b y a juve nile court, with home arrest restrictions 7. A mino r placed on proba t i on or juve nile i nt e nsive prob ation to a secure treatment facil ity which contracts w ith the juve nile d etention cen t e r, if the secure treatment facili t y is not pa rt of the crimin al justice system. This i ncludes ju veniles w ho become w ards of the court an d are place d in a 24-hou r non -medical reside ntial f a cility, w hich provides counse ling and other rehabil itative services 8. A minor place d on probation or juve nile intensi ve probation wi t h treatmen t in one of the follow ing as a condi t i on of probation : A psychiatric ho spital A residen t i al treatment center As an outpatie nt 9. Individ uals with tuberculo sis w ho are under an order of detention in one of the f o llowin g faci lities to protect publ ic health: A residen t i al treatment center A skilled n ursing facili t y A county, city or t ri bal jail a waiting pla cement for t re atment 10. Individ uals in a CCTRP or MCR P p rogram who ha ve reached pha se t hre e or four of t he program E. Su spension o f Ben efits When an inmate of a pu blic institution appli es for Medi-C al, they must be evaluated . If the inmate is Medi-C al eligi ble, benefits must be granted a nd immediatel y suspended u ntil release . NOTE: If an app licant repo rt s an addre ss t h at is known to be a C CTRP, EACP, FO TEP, or MC RP, Human Services Spe cialists (HSS) mu st verify the institution al status of the a pplican t . Some of these facilitie s have more than one pro gram and some prog ram residents may be con sidered inma t e s of a publ ic institution, and some may no t . CCTRP and MCRP have four phase s. Once inmates reach the transitio nal phase three, they are no long er consid ered inma t e s of a pu blic i nst i t u t i on and their eli gibili t y must be gr anted or e xisting bene f i t s un suspende d as of t h eir phase 3 start date. The HSS ma y a ccept t h e phase li st e d on appl ication cover l ett e rs f rom C CTRP and MCRP as veri f i cation of the phase . The H SS can also accept t h e custome r attestation of the phase three start date. If the customer is unsu re of t h e pha se three start date, use the report date as the start date. F. Medi-Cal Eli gibili t y for Pena l Codes Rel ated to Competency to Stand Trial County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti onal Status 06.01.01 4 of 5 Penal Code Desc rip tion Elig ibility 1367 Appli es to indivi duals charg ed with a misdeme anor, but who are incomp etent to stand trial. title: Section 3 - Institution for Mental Diseases
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti on for Mental Diseases (IMD) 6.3 1 of 2 Revision Date: April 9, 202 0 Back g r o und: An I MD is de f i ned a s a h ospital, nu rsing faci lity, or o t h er instituti on with more than 16 beds that i s primari ly e ngaged in provid ing diagno sis, treatment, or ca re of peop le w ith me nt a l d iseases. I f a facility functio ns primarily as a f aci lity establish ed and main t a ined for the care a nd treatment of people with mental disease s, then it is an IMD; it does n ot have to be l icensed as su ch. An institution for the devel opmentall y d isabled i s no t an I MD . Purpose: This sectio n has bee n written in the current format; the rules for peo ple age 22 have been corre ct e d to mat ch the State rul es. The prior section stated that peopl e ag e 22 could no long er ge t Medi-C al i n an IMD, which con f l icted with the rest of t h e section. Poli c y: IMD Eligib ility: Peopl e between 21 an d 65 years of age in IMDs can recei ve Medi-Cal if othe rwise elig ible. Note: There is no federa l f i nancial pa rt i cipation for these peo ple. Medi-C al Covered Se rvices in an IMD: Services cove red for people 21 t o 65 years of age in an IMD inclu de the followin g: Facility charg es (t h e daily bed rate) Medi-C al covered ph ysician services Prescriptio n drugs Labo ratory services X-ray services Dental s ervices Vision s ervices Psychiatrist service s Psycholo gist services Note: Service s not related to the I MD (f o r example, hosp ital, emergen cy room, etc. ) would b e covered . Disab ility Determina t i on: Determin e t he Med i-Cal elig ibility of a person admitted to a n I MD or who is a residen t of an IMD a s shown i n t h e t a ble belo w: If di sa b ility Then Has not bee n establi shed, Initiate a referral to Di sability Determi nation Services D ivision (DD SD) f or a disab ility determina t i on. Place the person i n A i d Code 53 un t i l a determinatio n has bee n completed (See MPG 5.4 for instructions on D DSD referrals). Has bee n establi shed, Place the i ndividua l in the approp riate disabil ity aid code. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Instituti on for Mental Diseases (IMD) 6.3 2 of 2 Individ uals 21 and 22 Y e ars of A g e in an IMD: If a Medi -Cal benefici ary i n a n IMD has bee n rece iving psychia t ri c in patient hospital service s pri or to his/her 21 st birthd ay and continues to receive the se services until age 22, he/she remains entitled to receive Medi-Cal be nefits. U se Aid Code 82 (Me dically Indi gent Child). A Medi-Cal Eli gibili t y Data System (MEDS) hold and an ale rt wil l b e g enerated at age 21 indica t i ng that a special Eli gibili t y Status Action Code (ESAC ) i s req uired for this age group and ag e. Sub mit an on-li ne request to the Family Resou rce Center (FRC) MEDS clerk to reactivate the perso n on MEDS using aid code 82 and assign ing a specia l ESAC code of 4 or 9. Set a Case Alert for when the person turn s 2 2 t o e valuate for other Medi-C al programs. At age 22, t h e above person can no l onger receive Med i-Cal in Aid Co de 82, and their Medi-Ca l elig ibility must be reeva luated. If d etermined eli gible, activate them in the ap propriate ai d code. Procedure: See abo ve. Program Impacts : None . Refer ences: MEPM 6E Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be revie wed for continua nce by March 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne , Di rector Eligi bility Operation s

title: Section 4 - Fleeing Felons
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Fleeing Felons 6.4 1 of 1 Revision Date: August 1, 2020 Back g r o und: Fleein g felons are not el igible for CalWORKs, Sup plemental Security Income/State Su pplemen t al Program (SSI/ SSP), CalFresh, or General Relief (GR). However, i f otherwise eligib le, fleein g felons are eli gible to recei ve Medi-Cal b enefits. Purpose: This section has b een written i n the current format; all reference s to drug f e lons, w hich is a separate status than fleeing felo ns, ha ve b een removed beca use the programs listed ab ove no longer den y bene f i t s to drug fel ons. Poli c y: Unde r federal regul ations, a fleeing felon is define d as an in dividua l who is fle eing to avoid prosecu t i on or custody or confinement af ter conviction for a crime which i s a felo ny unde r the laws of the pla ce from whi ch the i ndividua l flees, or (who i s) violatin g a cond ition of p robation or parol e under Federal or S tate l aw. To receive Medi-Cal , f l eeing felo ns are subje ct to a ll the eli gibili t y re quiremen t s of the program. If otherwi se eligib le, f l eeing felon s are eligibl e t o re ceive Medi-C al benefits until they ha ve been booke d, sentence d, or incarcera t e d. W he n any of these o ccur, Medi-Cal eligib ility is suspe nded (see MPG 6.2.5, Suspend ing Benefits for Inmates). Procedure: None . Program Impacts : None . Refer ences: MEPM 6G Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be revie wed for continua nce by July 31, 2023 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne , Di rector Eligi bility Operation s

title: Section 5 - Juveniles in Public Institutions
content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Incarcer ated Juvenil e s 06.05.01 1 of 2 Effective/Re visio n Date : 8/1/2024 Back g r o und: In d etermining the Medi-Cal eli gibili t y of a juven ile (u nder t h e age of 18) in a facility, staff mu st consid er both the dispo sition status of t h e juvenil e a nd the type of f a cility they are in. Customers incarcera t e d in a correction al facil ity who apply for Medi-Ca l must be evalua t e d. Reside nce in a correction al facility does not di squalify appl icants f ro m Me di-Cal, how ever if otherwise el igible thei r e ligibi lity must b e suspe nded until t h ey are no longe r consid ered incarcerated. Incarcerated indivi duals receivin g inpa t i ent or mental health se rvices outside of the correction al facili t y ma y be eli gible to limited scop e coverage that pays only for the inpatie nt or mental health services. This se ct i on was updated to include suspense lang uage. Purpose: This section provides staff with policy guida nce for how to determi ne Me di-Cal elig ibility f o r Juven iles i n correction al facilities. Poli c y: A. D isposition Dispo sition is the deci sion made b y the court f o r t h e juvenil es welfare. A disp osition orde r i s t h e court decisio n that the min or will be placed i n foster care, sentence d, p laced on probation, or re leased e ither temporaril y or perman ently. When t h e juven ile i s determine d a Ward of the Court an d is a waiting f o st e r care p lacement a nd not awaitin g senten cing f o r a crimina l vio lation of la w, the juven ile is el igible for Medi-Cal . (See MPG Article 5, Section 12 for in f orm at i on on Foster Care). B. St a t u s Pri or t o D isposition If a juven ile i s in a deten t i on cen t e r due to crimin al activi t y, t h ey are conside red in carcerated must have their eli gibili t y suspe nded, if currently active. If they are in a deten t i on center for care, protection and/or in the b est i nterest of the ch ild and there is a specific pl an that makes t h e st a y temp orary (1 to 2 months) t h en they are no t co nsidered in carcerated. C. Status Af ter Di sposition Ju veniles on intensive proba t i on w ith a pla n of release , which in cludes residence in a correctiona l facil ity, are consi dered incarce rated and must have Medi -Cal bene f i t s suspe nded until re leased. Ju veniles pl aced or awai t i ng placeme nt, o n intensive pro bation in a re sidential faci lity, are not conside red incarce rated if t h e f a cility is not part of t h e criminal ju st i ce system. D. Facility Publi cly opera t e d community resi dences that se rve no more t h an 16 resi dents are n ot considere d correctiona l facilitie s, an d juvenil es i n t h ese facilities are en t i t l ed to Medi-Cal i f otherw ise eligi ble. These facilities may be psychia t ri c n ursing facili t i es licensed by the De partment of Mental Health or othe r co mmunity care facilities. Example A juve nile is detained f o r criminal activity and i s placed on proba t i on with sp ecific condi t i ons of relea se, inclu ding a stay of 30 days or long er at a co rrectional facili t y. The facili t y is id entified as a juven ile detentio n center, not a treatment ce nter. Upon relea se from this d etention center, they would be placed on probatio n with their pa rent or guard ian. The juven ile is con sidered a n incarcerated individ ual and mu st h ave their ben efits suspen ded until rel ease. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Incarcer ated Juvenil e s 06.05.01 2 of 2 Refer ences: ACWDL 13-1 8, 2 2-27, 24-04 MEM Letter 241 Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be review ed for continuance o n or by 8/31/2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficien cy Services County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Suspension of Benefits for Incarcer ated Juvenil e s 06.05.02 1 of 1 Effective/Re visio n Date : 8/1/2024 Back g r o und: Medi-C al eli gibili t y mu st be suspen ded for in carcerated in dividual in corre ct i onal facil ities unde r t h e age 2 1 who were Medi -Cal elig ible at t h e t i me o f in carceration. This section was upda t e d to incl ude the extension of juven ile suspen sion past one year. Purpose: This section pro vides requi rements f o r su spendin g benefits for incarcerated j uveniles. Poli c y: Juveni les incarcerated in a corre ct i onal facility must have their bene f i t s suspe nded and not discon t i nued until their rele ase. Suspense onl y e nds on the release d ate, de ath, o r i f they are no l onger consid ered juven iles (unde r a ge 21 or age 26 if former foster youth). Annua l and chan ge in circu mst a nces redetermi nations are n ot required f o r t h e juveni le while incarcerated , b ut the worker shall update to the approp riate a id cod e if notified of a change such as a ging out of a sp ecific ai d type. An ex parte redetermi nation is only req uired at release i f on e hasnt been comp leted in the past year. Incarcerated juven iles are conside red tempora rily ab sent from the home a nd still part of t h e tax ho usehold unle ss the re is evidence to the contrary. Procedure: Refer to Processin g G u ide 13  Incarcerated C ustomers f o r su spension p rocedures. Refer ences: ACWDLs 10-0 6, 1 4-26, 21-22, and 24 -04 Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be review ed for continuance o n or by 8/31/2027 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficien cy Services County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Incarcer ated Juvenil e Pre -Release Application Pr o c ess 06.05.03 1 of 1 Effective/Re visio n Date : 8/1/2024 Back g r o und: Juveni les i ncarcerated in county correctional facili t i es (Juve nile Hall, a ca mp or ranch) for more tha n 30 days may beg in the Medi -Cal app lication p rocess whil e incarcera t e d so that they may have Medi-Cal eligib ility immedi ately upo n relea se, if possib le. This se ct i on was revised to include direction t o grant an d immedi ately suspen d eligib ility when there is no rel ease date on the referral form. Purpose: To provide staff with pol icy guidance for the ju venile pre- release app lication pro cess. Poli c y: A. Notification The Coun t y of San Diego D epartment of Pro bation will no t i f y the inca rcerated indivi duals pare nts du ring intake that they intend to obtain Medi -Cal for t h e i ncarcerated ind ividual . If the p arent requests an appli cation or t h ere is no re sponse within 30 d ays, the Department will send referral f o rm 14-8 8 to HHSA to Self-Sufficien cy services to eval uate at the time o f in t a ke. B. Evaluation If there is a n active case, su spense proce dures app ly. If the re is no a ct i ve case, it shou ld be trea t e d as a ma il- in appl ication reque st with the referral date serving as the date of ap plication and the rele ase date a s the begi nning date of aid. Juvenil es with no release date on the referral shall be evalua t ed and if e ligibl e, granted and imme diately suspe nded until a rel ease date is communi cated by the Departmen t of Probatio n. C. Communi cation with Dep artment of Pro bation Use form 14 -88 H HSA to communicate to the San Diego Coun t y Probatio n Dep artment the outcome of the elig ibility de t e rmination o r if t h e determina t i on cannot be completed pri or to the relea se date, at least ten da ys prior to the sched uled relea se via secure emai l t o the p robation contact on the form. D. Relea se Date Change s When a rele ase date change s, the Prob ation Departmen t wi ll send a modifie d referral form with the new date. Chan ge the begin ning date of aid to the new rel ease date. NOTE: So me i ndividua ls may h ave shorter incarceratio ns a nd t h e referral form w ill reach the HSS very close to the relea se date. T h e HSS must ma ke e very eff o rt to grant the case pri or to rel ease. E. Notice of Action When notifyin g the incarcera t e d juvenil es family of grantin g or suspense o f be nefits, se nd a copy of all n ot i ces to t h e you t h in the county correctional facility as well if the add ress is known . Send notices for incarcerated juven iles in cases by t h emselves o r adults i ncarcerated in a j uvenile facility to the correctiona l facility i f known, if not then use the last known a ddress. Procedure: Suspen sion proced ures are in the Incarcerated C ustomers Processing Guid e section 9. Refer ences: ACWDL 07-3 4 and 24-04 Sunset Date: This poli cy w ill be review ed for continuance o n or by 8/31/2027 County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Incarcer ated Juvenil e Pre -Release Application Pr o c ess 06.05.03 1 of 1 Approval for Release: Rick Wanne, Director Self-Sufficien cy Services

content: County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Non-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 1 of 3 Revision Date: Decemb er 1, 2025 Back g r o und: Non-ci t i zens fall under multiple categories that impact Medi-Cal eligi bility an d the l evel of benefits they are entitle d t o . Purpose: This se ct i on descri bes the non-citizen categories and pr ovides gu idance on de t e rmining residency f o r those who p ossess a Border Crossin g Card or non-i mmigrant visa. Poli c y: A. Q u alified No n-Citizens (QNC) QNC in the follo wing catego ries are eligi ble for full scope Medi -Cal coverag e. Lega l Permanent Resid ents (LPR) LPR who were admitted into t h e Un ited States (U.S.) on a permane nt basis or for an inde f i nite p eriod are entitled t o full scope Med i-Cal if otherwi se eli gible. Refer to Medi-Cal Desk A i d 78 for U.S. Citizen ship and Immigratio n Services (USCIS) docume ntation types. Battered Non -citizens Non-ci t i zens who were b att e red or sub jected to e xt re me cruelty a re consid ered QNC and eli gible t o full scope Med i-Cal ben efits un der federal law if they mee t ea ch of the fou r re quiremen t s bel ow. 1. The customer has be en approve d or has a petition pen ding unde r o ne of t he I mmi gration and Nation ality Act p rovisions. Note: Pendi ng adjud ication for one of the provisi ons may be verified w ith a Notice of Prima Facie Case i s val id until USCIS has mad e a determinatio n. 2. The customer, their chil d, and/or the parent of a non-citize n child app licant were battered o r subje ct e d t o e xt re me cruelty. 3. The battered no n-citizen has provi ded verificatio n t ha t there is a substantial conn ection between the battery and the ne ed for benefits. Acceptable veri f i cat i on includ es a sworn statement from t h e customer that describ es any one of the followi ng circumstances: The non-ci t i zen or their child i s re ceiving cash assi st a nce based on ba t tery or extreme cruelty Loss of financi al support resultin g f ro m the n on-citizen and / o r the ir childs sep aration from the abuse r The non-ci t i zen or their child re quires medi cal attention, mental hea lth counseli ng, or has become d isabled be cause of the battery/cruelty Unwa nted pregna ncy or children resu lting from the abusers sexu al assault or abusi ve relatio nship with the no n-citizen or their chil d Need s to rep lace coverag e t he cust o mer/child had w hile livi ng with the abuser If t he c u st o mer presents different facts than those above an d claims a connectio n between the battery and the ne ed for benefits, an elevatio n must be submitted to t h e Medi-Cal Pro gram team using the p roper chann els. County of San Diego, Health and H u m an Ser vices Agency (HHSA ) Medi-Cal Program Guid e Number Page Non-Citizen Categories 07.02.01 2 of 3 4. The customer must no long er live in the same ho usehold as the ab user. Permane ntly Residin g Under Colo r of La w (PRUCOL) Non-ci t i zens in the PRUCOL categ ory are entitle d to full scop e Medi-Ca l bene f i t s i f ot h erwise el igible . Non-ci t i zen Me di-Cal appl icants may claim any one of the PRUCOL categori es li st e d on the Stat e ment of Citizenshi p, Ali enage and Immigratio n Status (MC 13). Refer to Me di-Cal Desk Aid 78 for PRUCOL categori es and documen t a t i on require d. B. Non-Citize ns with Unsatisfactory Immigration S tatus (U I S) Non-C itizens with U I S will recei ve full or restricted benefits based on w hich of the followi ng categ ories they fall und er: Non-ci t i zens with UIS who apply for Medi-C al on or aft e r Ja nuary 1, 2 026 will rece ive restricted scope Med i-Cal if otherwi se eligibl e. Non-ci t i zens with U I S who were active prio r to January 1 , 2026 wi ll continu e to receive f u ll scope Medi-C al as long as they do not experience a b reak in aid. C. Reside ncy f o r Bo rder Crossing C ard (BCC) or Non-Immig rant Visa Holde rs USCIS issues BCC and non-immi grant visas to non-citizen s w ho reside in a nother country and provid e documen t a t i on that t he y intend to enter the United States for onl y a temp orary period . Border C rossing Card Due t h e require ments for receip t of a BCC, posse ssion of a va lid and current card is compell ing evide nce that the holde r is no t a resid ent of the st a t e of Cal ifornia. A non-citizen with a BCC may establi sh resid ency by presenting persua sive evid ence tha t they ha ve taken st e ps consi st e nt with the ir stated intent to l ive in C alifornia permanen t l y, o r indefini t e ly, or have e ntered the state for emplo yment reasons. The cl aim of Californ ia reside ncy must be evalu ated using all avai lable informatio n with the r esults clearl y detailed in a j ournal en t ry. If una ble to de t e rmine Cal ifornia reside ncy, st aff must initia t e a fraud referral as i ndicated in Medi-Cal Pro cessing Guide 1 9 Fraud Preventio n. Non-Immig rant Visa A val id and current n on-immigra nt visa, incl uding but not limited to B-1 and B-2 visas, which allows entry for a pe riod of less tha n one year co nstitutes strong evide nce that the bea rer is not a resi dent of Cali f o rnia an d is not eligibl e for any Medi-Cal benefits, unl ess they pre sent persua sive evide nce to the contrary. People with non-i mmigrant visas are permitted entry in t o the United States for pe rsonal or busin ess purposes. At t h e port o f entry, USCIS frequently stamps the I-94 with permi ssion for t h e person to stay for a perio d of six months or less. If after consideri ng al l avai lable information , the H SS is un able to de t e rmine the cu st o mers claim of Californ ia reside nce, then ini t i ate a fraud referral due to incon sistent or que st i onable information, that cannot be re solved. Cle arly narrate all facts in ca se comments if it is determine d t h at the cu st o mer is not a resident of the state. Purpose: To provide guid elines for t he pro cessing Medi-Ca l case s wh en one or more family membe rs are in LTC, B&C, or enrolle d in PACE. Poli c y: Appli cants/beneficia ries who are Me di-Cal eligib le und er Modifie d Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI ) continu e to recei ve LTC/B&C servi ces unde r their MAGI full-scop e aid code. If ineli gible t o MAGI , process the case using pre-ACA rule s.
